packages.changelog:
**This release contains no game assets. Requires a USA disc image (GAFE01, ISO/GCM/CISO). Always keep a backup of your save files.**

A bug-fix update to v1.0.0-beta. To update, replace `AnimalCrossing-gcNX.nro` in your gcNX folder; your saves and settings are kept.

### Fixes
- **A/B and X/Y were swapped** ([#2](https://github.com/digdat0/ACGC-Switch-Port/issues/2)). The buttons now match their Switch labels everywhere: in the game and in the − menu. If you swapped buttons in `keybindings.ini` to work around this, put them back (or delete `keybindings.ini` to restore the defaults).
- **Town tune changed after a reboot** ([#3](https://github.com/digdat0/ACGC-Switch-Port/issues/3)). Pressing OK while your tune was still playing could save a changed first note, so the tune didn't match after restarting. Tunes now save exactly as you made them. A tune that was already affected needs to be fixed once in the editor.

### Install
1. Make a folder under `switch/` on your SD card (any name) and put `AnimalCrossing-gcNX.nro` in it.
2. Put your own **Animal Crossing (USA, GAFE01)** disc image (`.iso`, `.gcm` or `.ciso`) in the same folder.
3. Hold **R** while starting any game, open the Homebrew Menu and start **Animal Crossing gcNX**.

Full instructions, controls and settings are in the README.

### Reporting problems
Press **−**, open the **Gameplay** tab, set **Enable logging** to **On** and apply, reproduce the problem, then attach `stdout.log` and `stderr.log` from the gcNX folder to an issue.

Unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo.

packages.changelog:
> [!CAUTION]
> **This app writes directly to your Animal Crossing: New Horizons save, and a corrupted island may be impossible to recover.**
> Back up your save with [JKSV](https://github.com/J-D-K/JKSV) or [Checkpoint](https://github.com/BernardoGiordano/Checkpoint) before every editing session, and copy that backup to a computer.
> Tested on **one console and one save only** (game 3.0.3). Use it offline. No warranty of any kind.

**New: 30 and 40 pocket slots.** If you bought the pocket upgrades at Nook's Cranny, the app now shows and edits all of your slots, not just the first 20.

![Pockets with 40 slots](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chatelp/ACNH-Power-Pockets/v1.2.0/docs/screenshots/pockets-40.png)

## What's new

- **All your pocket slots.** The game keeps slots 21 to 40 in a second block of the save, with a counter of how many are unlocked (0, 10 or 20). The app reads that counter, never changes it, and shows your 20, 30 or 40 slots in 2, 3 or 4 columns. Every pocket action works on all of them: **Y** to the next empty slot, *Fill empty slots*, *Quantity…*, *Clear slot*, *Revert*, the Review screen. Locked slots are never touched.
- **Loadouts follow.** A loadout of 30 or 40 slots is saved in a 320-byte file; 20-slot loadouts keep the old 160-byte format. A loadout that uses slots you don't have is refused instead of being loaded halfway.
- **69 built-in favorites.** Useful items and tools (fish bait, medicine, ladder, fossil…), seasonal materials (pine cone, maple leaf, snowflakes…) and a few rare finds (golden toilet, robot hero, coelacanth, golden stag…) join the fruits, vegetables and materials of 1.1.1. Favorites can hold 100 items.
- System › Info shows how many pocket slots the save has.

## Checked in the game (ACNH 3.0.3)

On a 40-slot save, items placed in slots 21 to 40 landed exactly where they should (slot 21 = first of the third row, slot 40 = last of the fourth), with the right quantities. Stack quantities were already confirmed in 1.1.x. The Turnips panel still hasn't been compared with Nook's Cranny.

The save engine is unchanged; a script checks it on every build. The only new place the app writes to is the bag block of the pockets, exactly like the first 20 slots.

## Install or update

1. Extract `ACNH-Power-Pockets-v1.2.0.zip` to the root of your SD card and overwrite the old files. Your favorites, loadouts and backups stay.
2. Fully close Animal Crossing (HOME › X › Close).
3. Hold **R** while starting Animal Crossing to open the Homebrew Menu, then launch **ACNH Power Pockets**.

Questions and feedback: [GBAtemp thread](https://gbatemp.net/threads/release-acnh-power-pockets-pocket-bells-editor-for-acnh-on-the-console-fork-of-acnh-save-editor-pre-release.686451/) · Bugs and test results: [GitHub issues](https://github.com/chatelp/ACNH-Power-Pockets/issues/new/choose)

packages.changelog:
**Lost Odyssey Recomp for Switch – v1.2.0**

**Fixed**
The game could close itself ("The software was closed because an error occurred") when you pressed Start on the title screen, on some discs and with some languages. Since v1.1.0, the optimised build mishandled errors the game normally recovers from, and one of them crashed it. The build is fixed, and every release is now checked for it (#35).
Memory use no longer creeps up during long battles. The occlusion system kept a few MB of buffers it never gave back, more the longer you played (#41).
A memory leak in the graphics library is fixed. deko3d is now built from source, with the fix (#3).
env.txt now applies to every setting, including the ones read at start-up, such as LO_VERBOSE and LO_GPU_STATS (#38). The LO_DEKO3D_<NAME> lines work again (#34).

**Changed**
The console can sleep again. Auto-sleep and the HOME menu work as in other games: the screen stays on only during loads, the preparation screen and cutscenes. LO_SWITCH_AUTO_SLEEP=0 and LO_SWITCH_HOME_SUSPEND=0 bring back the old behaviour (#7).
Merged with upstream v1.1.0: Switch button icons on Auto, the settings menu in Spanish, French, German and Italian, Scene fades, the XMA audio fix and more (#9).
Settings: Frame rate is hidden and stays at 30, because the screen runs at 60 Hz and the game can't hold 60. Shader preparation is hidden too (#12).
The version in the Homebrew Menu and in the logs is now the Switch release's own number (1.2.0). It used to show 1.1.0.

**Performance**
Unchanged from v1.1.0A: 28.4 FPS in the first battle, handheld, stock clocks, 540 rows. Zcull was measured at about 2% less GPU time in battle; it was already on (#26).

**Upgrading**
Replace LostOdysseyRecomp.nro in sdmc:/switch/LostOdysseyRecomp/. env.txt and the shader packs are the same as v1.1.0A. Your saves and settings are kept.

packages.changelog:
---
Changes to Amiigo:
---
Features

- Amiibo image saving toggle — Option added to control whether downloaded amiibo images are saved to disk.
- Amiibo image previews — When selecting an Amiibo in the My Amiibo list an image preview is shown if an image is available.
- Generate all amiibos at once — New buttons in both the Settings UI and the Amiigo Store context menu to generate every amiibo in bulk.
- Full settings UI overhaul — Settings reorganised into submenus with a dedicated theming menu, a reinstall Emuiibo button, a dropdown for category options, and a checkbox for the random UUID setting.
- Multi-language support — UI text is now fully localised; English (en-GB), Spanish (es), Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans/zh-CN), and Traditional Chinese (zh-Hant/zh-TW) are included.
- Automatic image resizing — Downloaded images are resized for compatibility with Tesla / Ultrahand.
- Amiibo name from JSON — Amiibo display names are now read directly from the amiibo JSON data.
- Re-introduced the ability to update the local amiibo API cachie from the internet.
- O(1) series data extraction — Amiibo series lookup replaced with a constant-time function.
---
Bug Fixes

- Emuiibo install now reboots the console — After installing, the app prompts to reboot so the sysmodule loads correctly.
- Emuiibo path buffer size — Passed the correct buffer size to SetActiveVirtualAmiibo.
- Misc networking and utility fixes — Corrected edge cases in download logic and amiibo path handling.
---
Changes to Arriba:
---
Features

- Wrapped text element — New WrapText element that automatically breaks text onto multiple lines when it exceeds a configurable pixel width.
- Improved Chinese font support — Extended the font rasteriser to better handle CJK glyphs, with fallback glyph resolution for characters not covered by the primary face.
- O(1) tag lookups — findObjectsByTag is now backed by a hash structure.
- Shader uniform location cache — Uniform locations looked up once and cached per shader.
- Faster mat4 multiplication — Matrix multiply logic reverted to old version, ~11% faster at -O0.
- Steam Deck / SteamOS support (Not used for Amiigo) — Added an SDL-based input backend so Arriba can run on Linux.

---
Bug Fixes

- UI object lifecycle — UIObject construction/destruction made fully explicit.
- InertialList stability — Suppressed a lag spike during list load, and corrected several edge-case scrolling behaviours.
- Vsync frame cap — Vsync enabled on the swap buffer call.
---

packages.changelog:
**1.12.2** is Atmosphère's ninety-fifth official release.

**Please be sure to update fusee when upgrading to 1.12.2**. fusee-primary no longer exists, and will not work any more.

With thanks to the @switchbrew team, Atmosphère 1.12.2 is bundled with [hbl](https://github.com/switchbrew/nx-hbloader) 2.4.5, and [hbmenu](https://github.com/switchbrew/nx-hbmenu) 3.6.1.

The following was changed since the last release:
* Basic support was added for 23.5.0.
* General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience.

And the following was changed in 1.12.0:
* Support was added for 23.0.0.
* Special thanks to @alula for handling the implementation of several kernel changes.
    * The console should boot and atmosphère should be fully functional.
    * **Please note**: As a result of changes made to nintendo's software in 23.0.0, there is even less memory available for custom system modules.
        * The amount of memory we can steal from the applet pool has been reduced beyond 7MB and we can no longer launch browser applets (e.g.: eshop) without crashing.
        * To compensate for this, a set of patches for the browser applets has been introduced.
            * Thanks to the redesign of the browser applets in 22.0.0 there are only 3 applets we need to worry about: systemWeb, openWeb and LibAppletOff.
            * With the added burden of maintaining patches for these applets, we can reclaim around 9MB of reserved memory by patching out their allocations.
            * This memory is provably unused and stealing it should not affect the browser applets in any way as the applets themselves tag it as reserved and never access it.
            * As a result, the memory available for custom system modules has been experimentally increased to 16MB.
            * Preliminary testing has seemingly shown no downsides to the overall functioning of the OS and the browser applets in particular.
            * Nonetheless, please report any issues you may face to ensure no edge cases have been missed and to determine if the memory amount needs to be adjusted. 
            * These patches may be deprecated at any point in the future if a better solution is devised.     
    * `exosphère` was updated to reflect the latest official secure monitor behavior.
        * A new ConfigItem was added to the secure monitor for the first time since firmware 5.0.0.
    * `mesosphère` was updated to reflect the latest official kernel behavior.
        * The kernel now supports a 42bit wide address space.
        * A new memory region dubbed ShadowStack has been introduced.
        * Kernel RNG was changed to CTR-DRBG.
    * `boot` was updated to reflect the latest official behavior and to implement a previously missing change.
        * The way battery i2c shutdown was being enabled changed in firmware 18.0.0 and we missed it.
        * It is possible this might have been related to a known battery draining issue reported to have started around firmware 18.0.0. Further testing will be needed to confirm.
    * `loader` was updated to reflect the latest official behavior.
    * `erpt` was updated to reflect the latest official behavior.
    * `pgl` was updated to reflect the latest official behavior.
    * `ro` was updated to reflect the latest official behavior.
        * NROs can now be lz4 frame compressed.
* ZBIC compresison/decompression has been properly implemented. Applications using it should now launch and work properly.
* A dockerfile has been added to atmosphère (thanks @alula).
* R_DISCARD macro has been adopted across the entire codebase where applicable. This finishes the work started in version 1.10.0 and eliminates the nodiscard warnings during compilation.
* General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience.

For information on the featureset supported by 1.12, please see [the official release notes](https://github.com/Atmosphere-NX/Atmosphere/releases/tag/1.12.0).

packages.changelog:
This is an UNOFFICIAL, UNSUPPORT Atmosphere fork. Do not report any issues with this to Atmosphere maintainers

- Support for booting from eMMC
  - Fusee will check for a FAT32 filesystem on eMMC BOOT1 (at 1MB offset), eMMC BOOT1 (at 0MB offset), and eMMC GPP partition, any SD card partition. It will pick the first one it finds that does not have a .no_boot_storage file in the root directory
- Support for emuSD
  - Allows redirecting all SD accesses in HOS to a separate file or partition on the SD card or eMMC. Note: HOS will crash, if no physical SD card is inserted
  - emuSD configuration is read from /emusd/emusd.ini with the following format:
```
[emusd]
enabled=[1 for SD card | 4 for eMMC]
sector=[start sector of emuSD partition]
path=[path to emusd file]
```
- For eMMC file based emuSD, the file is read from the first available FAT32 partition on eMMC
- Support for emuMMC on eMMC
  - Allows creating file or partition based emuMMC on the eMMC
  - emuMMC configuration is read from /emummc/emummc.ini with the following format:
```
[emummc]
enabled=[1 for SD card | 4 for eMMC]
sector=[start sector of emuMMC partition]
path=[path to emuMMC file]
nintendo_path=[path to Nintendo folder]
id=[emuMMC id]
```
- For eMMC file based emuMMC, the file is read from the first available FAT32 partition on eMMC

Some of the DLLs in this package are heavily patched Wine builds, modified so Wine can run on the Switch's OS at all. This can trip antivirus and scanner heuristics. That's a false positive caused by the patching, not malicious code — the source is in this repository if you want to check it or build it yourself.

packages.changelog:
Blur (Bizarre Creations, 2010) on the Nintendo Switch (homebrew). You need your own copy of the Xbox 360 disc and its title update 2.
Thanks to masterspike52's reNut, whose renderer this port draws with, and to every port renut_nx_ultimate_base gathers.

## Install

Use the **[web installer](https://chanseyisthebest.github.io/blur-nx-installer/)**. It makes the whole package from your own disc and title update 2 (the Xbox 360 package or an extracted folder), in your browser, and nothing is uploaded. It gives you this NRO too, with the game's shaders translated and compiled for the Switch from your files.

Extract `blur-nx.zip` to the root of the SD card, then in **Sphaira** find Blur, press **X**, choose **Install Forwarder**, set **Address Space** to **39-bit**, choose **Create Forwarder**, and start the game from the Home Screen (the forwarder gives it four CPU cores).

## What's in 1.0.0

- The whole game's code statically recompiled (ReXGlue), with title update 2, drawn by reNut's Direct3D-level renderer on deko3d.
- Races at 30 fps most of the time at stock clocks (handheld, four cores: 29.3 fps on average with the cap at 30).
- Built with link-time optimisation and a profile (PGO) from a race on the console; the hottest game functions as checked machine copies and hand-written natives.
- A game menu (hold A+B+X+Y+L+R): the settings, the game's achievements, each player's controls.
- No logging in normal play; a crash writes `switch/blur-nx/logs/rex/rex_crash.log`.

Not tested yet: split-screen multiplayer. Online play needs Xbox LIVE and is not supported.

Bug reports: add `log_level = "info"` at the top of `switch/blur-nx/blur.toml`, play until the problem happens, and include the `switch/blur-nx/logs/` folder.

## 🎮 bo2-360-nx Release 1.1.0

**Call of Duty: Black Ops II** for the **Nintendo Switch** and **Windows**, recompiled from the Xbox 360: **Zombies, Multiplayer and Campaign**, running as native code. This release fixes online play with friends on the same network, split screen online, the music and the first load of a map, and lets the extractor and the build kit handle every mode with all the DLC.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included, and none ever will be.** You need your own Xbox 360 copy of Black Ops II and its **Title Update 18**. Everything is built on your PC from your own files.

---

## 🛠️ Fixed in 1.1.0

- **Music:** menu and in-game music play again (the game was told a custom soundtrack was playing, so it muted its own).
- **First load of a map:** no more black screen for a minute on a fresh install. The picture and HUD come up within seconds and the world fills in while the map's graphics are prepared, with **FIRST VISIT - PREPARING GRAPHICS** at the top.
- **Online with friends on the same network or phone hotspot:** two consoles behind one internet connection can now join the same game; both show in the lobby and stay in it.
- **Split screen in System Link and online lobbies:** another controller can join on the host and on a console that joined, with the same controller screen as Local, up to 4 players per console.
- **Mod menus in split screen online:** menus fit each player's screen on the host and on consoles that joined.
- **All the DLC at once:** the extractor and the build kit can now make the shader library for Zombies and Multiplayer with every DLC pack (it stopped at 32,768 shaders before), and unpack the game's zones several at a time, which makes that step much faster.
- **Updating the tools:** a new extractor or kit run in an older one's work folder now uses its own scripts instead of the old ones.

---

## 📦 Assets

| File | What it is |
|------|------------|
| `bo2-360-nx-switch-PGO-NRO.zip` | The ready-made Switch programs (`bo2zm.nro` for Zombies and Multiplayer, `bo2cp.nro` for Campaign), optimized with link-time and profile-guided optimization, plus their settings |
| `bo2-360-nx-gamefiles-shader-extractor.zip` | Prepares your game files and the shader libraries from your own copy, for the prebuilt programs |
| `bo2-360-nx-release-1.1.0-switch+windows-build-kit.zip` | Builds everything from scratch on your PC: the Switch programs, the Windows version, the game files and the shaders |

---

## 🚀 Getting started

**You need:** your Xbox 360 copy of Black Ops II (ISO or extracted), **Title Update 18 (required)**, your DLC packs if you have them (optional), a Windows PC with **Python**, and for the Switch a console that runs homebrew.

1. Download `bo2-360-nx-switch-PGO-NRO.zip` and `bo2-360-nx-gamefiles-shader-extractor.zip`.

The shaders take a while on a fast PC: about 10 minutes for Zombies and Multiplayer, about 20 with all their DLC, and about 20 for Campaign.

# CDDA for Switch v0.1.1

## English

Save reliability patch for the native Nintendo Switch port, based on
Cataclysm: DDA 0.I (Ito).

Fixes:

- Safely replaces existing save files on Horizon, where rename cannot
  overwrite a destination directly.
- Explicitly commits completed save operations to the SD-card filesystem.
- Stores UTF-8 world names in reversible ASCII-safe directories while keeping
  the original name in the game interface.
- Stores achievement files for UTF-8 character names under ASCII-safe names;
  the original character name remains inside the JSON data.
- Preserves and continues loading existing legacy world directories.
- Adds detailed Switch save-stage diagnostics to `user/config/debug.log`.

Install by extracting `CDDAforSwitch` to `sdmc:/switch/` and launch it from a
full-memory Homebrew Menu session. Sound is not enabled in this release.

## 简体中文

这是基于 Cataclysm: DDA 0.I（Ito）的 Nintendo Switch 原生移植版存档可靠性
补丁版本。

修复内容：

- 修复 Horizon 文件重命名无法直接覆盖旧存档的问题，安全替换正式存档。
- 保存完成后显式提交 SD 卡文件系统，防止重启后存档丢失。
- 中文等 UTF-8 世界名使用可逆的 ASCII 安全目录，游戏界面仍显示原名称。
- 中文等 UTF-8 角色名的成就文件使用 ASCII 安全名称，JSON 中仍保留原名称。
- 保留并继续读取旧版世界目录，不自动删除或迁移用户存档。
- 在 `user/config/debug.log` 中增加 Switch 保存阶段诊断信息。

packages.changelog:
# 安装说明 — cod6-nx v325

**本包不包含游戏数据。** 你需要自备正版《使命召唤：现代战争2》的游戏文件。

---

## 一、包里有什么

```
switch\cod6-nx\
├── cod6.nro        主程序（41.6 MB）
├── cod6.toml       配置（已预设 very_low 画质）
├── README.md       项目说明
├── update\         标题更新设备（空，必须保留）
├── user\           存档与设置（空，会自动写入）
├── cache\          着色器缓存（空，第二趟起会变快）
└── cap\            诊断导出（空，平时不用）
```

---

## 二、放到卡上

把整个 `switch` 文件夹复制到 SD 卡根目录，得到：

```
SD:\switch\cod6-nx\cod6.nro
SD:\switch\cod6-nx\cod6.toml
SD:\switch\cod6-nx\game_root\   ← 这一步要你自己放
```

`game_root` 里应该是**从你自备的游戏本体提取的文件**，包含：

```
game_root\
├── default.xex
├── default.ff
├── common.ff
├── ...（各种 .ff 文件）
└── ...（其他资源）
```

> **`game_root` 不在本包内**，也不接受索取。请用你自己的正版游戏。

---

## 三、启动

1. Switch 上打开 hbmenu（相册或按住 R 点游戏图标）
2. 运行 `cod6-nx` → `cod6.nro`
3. 首次启动较慢（要翻译并编译着色器），**第二次起会快很多**

---

## 四、默认配置

`cod6.toml` 里已经设好 `very_low` 画质预设（关闭阴影、降低特效与模型细节），
实测比默认画质明显更流畅（22~32 → 35~60 fps）。

### 想画质好一点

编辑 `cod6.toml`，把 `cod6_dvar_set` 那一行里的这些去掉或调小：

| 想恢复 | 改成 |
|---|---|
| 纹理清晰度 | `r_picmip 2` → `r_picmip 0` |
| 模型细节 | `r_lodScaleRigid 6` → `r_lodScaleRigid 1` |
| 阴影 | `sm_enable 0` → `sm_enable 1` |
| 屏幕特效 | `r_glow 0` → `r_glow 1`、`r_bloom 0` → `r_bloom 1` |

> 动态阴影目前与阴影贴图互相影响，建议保持关闭。

### 长时间游玩后画面变差

显存只增不减，玩久了新贴图会分不到空间。把这一行改成 600 可以让它自动回收：

```toml
cod6_native_texture_evict_frames = 600
```

---

## 五、已知问题（不是你的操作问题）

| 现象 | 状态 |
|---|---|
| 部分平表面（选枪台、集装箱）呈蓝紫彩色噪点 | 未解决 |
| 枪焰、尘土显示为巨型方块 | 未解决 |
| 只有角色附近被照亮，远处偏暗 | 未解决（光照体积未移植） |
| 玩久了新出现的贴图会失真 | 未解决（可临时用上面的淘汰设置缓解） |
| 动态阴影 | 已默认关闭 |

详见 `README.md` 的「已知问题」。

---

## 六、遇到问题怎么报

附上这四样：

1. `SD:\switch\cod6-nx\logs\rex\rex_stderr.log`
2. `SD:\switch\cod6-nx\logs\rex\rex_perfil.log`
3. 你的 `cod6.toml`
4. 出问题位置的截图（**带 HUD 更好**）

日志里的版本行也请一并附上：`[cod6] VERSION 2026-11-03-325`

---

## 七、授权与声明

- 本项目以 **GPL-3.0** 分发，源码见仓库
- 基于 ReXGlue / Xenia（BSD-3-Clause），声明见 `sdk/LICENSE`
- **不含任何游戏数据**；游戏本体版权属于 Activision Publishing, Inc.
- 仅供学习与技术研究

## Cold Fear NX 0.1.37

Port refeito sobre o XboxSwitchPortKit: o Direct3D 8 e o DirectSound do Xbox reescritos em Vulkan (NVK) e no áudio do Switch, sem emular a NV2A.

### Novidades
- **Giroscópio na mira:** segure **ZL** e mova o console. Sensibilidade, velocidade vertical, eixo, estabilidade, correção de drift e inverter X/Y.
- **Sombras das lâmpadas** corrigidas.
- **OLED SCREEN BOOST** (AUTO / OFF / ON): clareia os tons escuros na tela OLED.
- Menu do port: **L3 + R3**.
- Menus sem faixas pretas; as faixas ficam só no gameplay.
- Capa do jogo no menu do Switch.
- 30 FPS na maior parte do jogo, sem overclock.

### Como instalar
1. Copie `coldfear.nro` para `sdmc:/switch/coldfear/`.
2. Copie os arquivos do seu disco de Cold Fear (Xbox, NTSC-U) para `sdmc:/switch/coldfear/game/` (ou um `.iso`).
3. Abra pelo hbmenu **segurando R ao abrir um jogo instalado** (modo título).

O jogo não está incluído: você precisa da sua própria cópia.

### Problemas conhecidos
- Quedas para 23–26 FPS nas áreas mais pesadas e em carregamentos.

---

## English

The port rebuilt on the XboxSwitchPortKit: the Xbox's Direct3D 8 and DirectSound rewritten over Vulkan (NVK) and the Switch's audio, with no NV2A emulation.

### What's new
- **Gyro aiming:** hold **ZL** and move the console. Sensitivity, vertical speed, axis, steadiness, drift correction and invert X/Y.
- **Lamp shadows** fixed.
- **OLED SCREEN BOOST** (AUTO / OFF / ON): lifts the dark tones on the OLED screen.
- Port menu: **L3 + R3**.
- Menus without black bars; the bars stay in gameplay only.
- Cover art in the Switch menu.
- 30 FPS for most of the game, with no overclock.

### How to install
1. Copy `coldfear.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/coldfear/`.
2. Copy the files of your own Cold Fear disc (Xbox, NTSC-U) to `sdmc:/switch/coldfear/game/` (or an `.iso`).
3. Open it from hbmenu **while holding R on an installed game** (title mode).

The game is not included: you need your own copy.

### Known issues
- Drops to 23–26 FPS in the heaviest areas and during loads.

---

## Español

El port rehecho sobre el XboxSwitchPortKit: el Direct3D 8 y el DirectSound de la Xbox reescritos sobre Vulkan (NVK) y el audio de la Switch, sin emular la NV2A.

### Novedades
- **Giroscopio al apuntar:** mantén **ZL** y mueve la consola. Sensibilidad, velocidad vertical, eje, estabilidad, corrección de deriva e invertir X/Y.
- **Sombras de las lámparas** corregidas.
- **OLED SCREEN BOOST** (AUTO / OFF / ON): aclara los tonos oscuros en la pantalla OLED.
- Menú del port: **L3 + R3**.
- Menús sin franjas negras; las franjas quedan solo en el gameplay.
- Carátula del juego en el menú de la Switch.
- 30 FPS en la mayor parte del juego, sin overclock.

### Cómo instalar
1. Copia `coldfear.nro` a `sdmc:/switch/coldfear/`.
2. Copia los archivos de tu propio disco de Cold Fear (Xbox, NTSC-U) a `sdmc:/switch/coldfear/game/` (o un `.iso`).
3. Ábrelo desde hbmenu **manteniendo R al abrir un juego instalado** (modo título).

El juego no está incluido: necesitas tu propia copia.

### Problemas conocidos
- Caídas a 23–26 FPS en las zonas más pesadas y durante las cargas.

---

packages.changelog:
Test build **0.57** of Conker: Live & Reloaded for the **Nintendo Switch, Windows, Linux and Android**. It is an unofficial fan port. The original Xbox game is recompiled ahead of time to native code, and its GPU commands are translated to Vulkan (Mesa NVK, on the Switch) or OpenGL.

This is a **pre-release for testing**. The single-player game is playable. Please report what you find (see "Report a bug").

## What is new since 0.56

- **Slingshot fix on all four platforms: download this build even if you do not need anything else.** In every published build up to 0.56 the slingshot pellets could ignore the aim and fly past the target (one x87 compare in the shot's direction code was translated wrong). The source of 0.56 already had the fix, but the game code inside the four published programs was generated before it. 0.57 is the first release whose generated code has it. Checked on a Switch console in a test build: the pellet flies to the reticle. Issue #18 (Android, pellets pass the dung beetles) is probably the same bug; not confirmed on Android.
- **Gyro aim on the Switch** (motion aim, issue #17 item 2): turn the console or the Pro Controller to move the slingshot, bat and frying-pan aim; the right stick still works on top. Off by default: settings menu (**−**) → **GYRO AIM**, **GYRO SENSITIVITY** (50-300 %, 100 = the view turns as far as the pad). Up/down follows the vertical aim inversion (the game's own Invert Aim in the pause Options, and `camera_invert_y`), so the gyro and the stick always agree. **GYRO FLIP LEFT/RIGHT** and **GYRO FLIP UP/DOWN** reverse a direction on top of that. Handheld, Pro Controller, or the right Joy-Con of a pair. Checked on a console (handheld). The "player space" mapping follows the idea of Steam Input and JoyShockMapper; the code is ours.
- **Aim speed** option (issue #17 item 2): **AIM SPEED** 50-300 % in the menu (`aim_speed=` in `clx_options.txt`, 25-400) scales the stick's aim camera for the slingshot, bat and pan.
- **`camera_invert_y` now also flips the aim camera** (slingshot, bat, pan), as the player camera. The game's own Invert Aim (pause → Options; it is **on** by default in the game) stacks with it. Checked on a console.
- **Switch button prompts show the right letter** (issue #17 item 8): the pause board said "(B) Resume" for the button that is A. The Switch glyphs now keep the Xbox letter, because the Switch buttons act by name (A is A). `RECOMP_PAD_LAYOUT=position` keeps the old mapping.
- **Fewer stalls on the Switch** (issue #17 items 4 and 5): the Vulkan pipeline cache (2-5 MB) was written from the rendering thread every 20 s (0.5 s freezes); it is now written on its own thread. The `[hitch]` log line now itemises pipeline compiles.

## Not verified in this build

- **Switch:** `clx-vulkan.nro` is the same code as the test build 0.56.6-g17 that ran on a console on 2026-11-06 and 2026-11-07 (slingshot, aim inversion, gyro, 30 fps); only the version text differs. This exact file has not been run.
- **Linux:** one headless boot with software OpenGL reached the title screen and rendered frames (90 s, no failed calls); not played.
- **Windows, Android:** built, **not run**. The changes against 0.56 are in the game layer shared with the Switch (aim, options, menu) plus the generated-code fix above. Android is signed with the same test key as 0.56 (`adb install -r` updates in place).

## Read this first

- The download contains **no game data**: no disc files, no textures, no sound. It does contain **code made from the game**.
- You need your **own unpacked copy** of Conker: Live & Reloaded for the original Xbox. Only the **retail NTSC (North America)** version works. SHA-1 of its `default.xbe`: `2232a1b3874d67b4bb4cf53a940420d2dab59535`.
- Switch: a console with **Atmosphère** and hbmenu, and about **6 GB free** on the microSD card. This release has the **Vulkan** program only.
- Windows 10/11 x64 or Linux x86-64, with a GPU that has OpenGL 3.3. Linux needs SDL2, OpenSSL and li

This release provides translations for **DBI version 921**.

> [!IMPORTANT]

### 🆕 What changed in DBI 921 (compared with 920)
- **FTP:** a serious bug in the FTP server is fixed (from the DBI author). No other user-visible changes were found in the 921 binary.
- **Translations:** the patch now supports DBI 921; the red `[ERROR]` status (e.g. after "Waiting for interface to come up:" in MTP) is translated; the USB "connect your console to the PC" prompt fits on one line in Ukrainian, Belarusian, German, French, Lithuanian and Turkish; Ukrainian "Запустити HTTP сервер..." matches the FTP item.

DBI does not publish a changelog. This list comes from the strings and settings of the 920 binary.
- **Forwarder settings** (new `[Forwarder]` section in `dbi.config`): address space (`32 Bit`, `32 Bit No alias`, `36 Bit`, `39 Bit`, `42 Bit`), four CPU cores, video capture and screenshots. DBI now reads and checks the forwarder's `main.npdm` (`META`, `ACI0`, `ACID`).
- **`PatchDistributionBit`** install option ("Patch XCI originated nca"): NCAs taken from a game card image can be patched.
- **Saves:** new "Increase size (in MB)" action; new "Save data information" and "Ticket information" views.
- **NACP viewer:** new fields `Accessible program index flags` and `Album file export`. **NSO viewer:** module name (`.module_name`) and the `.embedded` part of `.rodata`.
- **On-screen keyboard:** `L+⬅` / `L+➡` jump to the start / end of the line.
- **FTP server** replies were reworked; the old confirmation prompt for deleting lost content is gone.

### 🩹 Translation changes in the 920 release (since v0.0.108)
- **DBI 920 support.** The patch and all 24 translation tables work with DBI 920.
- **Game info panel:** "Total play time", "Game start" and "Game end" are translated also for titles without play data, including lines such as `Total play time : - (2)` (the number is put into the translation).
- **New strings translated:** the forwarder "Address space" setting; "Searching for old placeholders on SD / in NAND" in the cleanup log; the red "Title not installed" message.

### ✨ Earlier in the 912 line (still included)
- Translation engine in this repository (`vendor/dbi_translate`, originally [0xroast/dbi-translate](https://github.com/0xroast/dbi-translate)); hash-index lookups, no menu lag ([#28](https://github.com/rashevskyv/DBIPatcher/issues/28)); translated game info panel ([#25](https://github.com/rashevskyv/DBIPatcher/issues/25)); no "Invalid UTF-8" in the `(+)` menu ([#29](https://github.com/rashevskyv/DBIPatcher/issues/29)); whole `(+)` menu items; aligned game info panel; version line shows the language, e.g. `921-ua`.

### ✨ Cyrillic glyph repair
The bundled `DBI.nro` repairs the embedded glyphs `Є/є`, `І/і`, and `Ї/ї` used by Ukrainian, Belarusian, and Kazakh translations.

packages.changelog:
## Deadpool — Nintendo Switch Port (`deadpool-nx`) v1.0.0

Initial public release of **Deadpool** (2013, Xbox 360) statically recompiled for the Nintendo Switch using **ReXGlue** and **Renut's native deko3d renderer**.

### Highlights
- **Native AArch64 Execution & deko3d Renderer:** Direct3D 9 / Xbox 360 command streams rendered natively on the Switch's Maxwell GPU via deko3d (`1280x720` handheld / `1920x1080` docked, targeting `30 FPS` at stock clocks).
- **Complete Precompiled Shader Cache:** Ships with all **13,307** translated UE3 Xenos shaders (`deko3d_glsl.bin`) and **26,394** precompiled Maxwell GPU shader variants (`deko3d_shaders.bin`) for zero first-run compilation freezes.
- **Unreal Engine 3 Xenos EDRAM & FP10 HDR Fixes:** Accurate `7e3` (`D3DFMT_A2B10G10R10F_EDRAM`) exponent bias (`2^3`) across scene color, bloom/exposure gather, radial blur, and Near-Death vignette post-processing.
- **Nintendo Switch Controls & Momentum HUD Patches:** Physical Switch face-button mapping with in-memory HUD icon patches for all 4 Momentum combo prompts (`LB + B`, `LB + Y`, `LB + X`, `LB + A`).
- **ARM64 NEON XMA Audio & Codegen Fixes:** Vectorized XMA audio packet decode/resampling and verified stack-slot vector forwarding for UE3 Matinee `InterpActor` transforms.

### Installation
1. Download **`deadpool-nx-v1.0.0.zip`** below and extract it to the root of your Switch SD card (`sdmc:/`), creating `sdmc:/switch/deadpool-nx/`.
2. Copy your extracted Xbox 360 game files (`default.xex` and `TransGame/`) into `sdmc:/switch/deadpool-nx/game/` (both `game/` and `game_root/` are supported).
3. Launch via **Title Override** (hold **R** while starting any installed Switch title) or a **39-bit address space** NSP forwarder.

packages.changelog:
# dishonored-nx v0.50

## Installing / updating
**You need the EU version of the game**
1. **Delete your old `dishonored.toml`** in `sdmc:/switch/dishonored-nx/`. The `.nro` does not replace it, and the old
   one holds outdated settings. A fresh one is written at the next start.
2. Replace `dishonored.nro` in `sdmc:/switch/dishonored-nx/`.
3. Keep `pipeline_list.bin` and the shader cache next to it. Some shaders changed, so the first start can spend a
   little longer compiling them in the menus.
4. Use the 4-Core forwarder.

## What's new
- **Higher picture quality.** 480p by default, upscaled to the screen with sharpening (FSR-style). 540p is optional.
- **Better performance.** Less CPU work per frame and a steadier frame rate.
  Tested with an overclock (sys-clk): CPU 1428 MHz, RAM 1600 MHz, handheld: mostly 30 fps. Performance work is ongoing.
- **Clean sound.** No more choppy audio during fights and teleports.
- **Texture fixes.** No more purple/black textures or garbled text after loading a save.
- **Stability.** Fixed freezes and Atmosphère panics.
- **Fewer black objects.**
- **Gyro aiming.** While playing, press `L` + `R` + right stick click to turn it on or off. (you can tweak it how you want in dishonored.toml)

## Settings
`dishonored.toml` now explains every option and shows its default.
- `dishonored_render_height_handheld` / `dishonored_render_height_docked` (default `480`). `540` = sharper, a little
  more GPU time.
- `dishonored_fsr` (default `true`). `false` = plain bilinear upscale (softer picture).
- `dishonored_fsr_sharpness` (default `0.3`), from `0.0` to `2.0`.
- `input_gyro` (default `false`). `true` = gyro on from the start.

## Known issues
Stock clocks: frame drops in busy fights and teleports (CPU-bound). Overclocking fixes most of it. Performance work is ongoing.
An object can sometimes turn dark from far away and look normal up close.
Rare GPU crash (error `2359-0001`). If you happen to experience it be sure to send me a log, because I haven't been able to replicate it for now.
Blood stains fade quickly.
Album (applet) mode is not supported: too little memory.

## Found a bug or a crash?
Create an Issue and send me the newest `logs/dishonored_XXX.log` (next to `dishonored.nro`). After a crash, also send the file with the
same time from `/atmosphere/crash_reports/` (or `/atmosphere/fatal_reports/`). Add a short note on what you were
doing when it happened.

Support my ports: [buymeacoffee.com/czn999](https://buymeacoffee.com/czn999)

Fixes the textures that went black after a long session, and makes 60 fps Interpolated smoother while running.

### What's new since v1.1.1

- **Textures no longer go black or noisy after playing a while.** The Switch's GPU service (nvdrv) keeps one record per texture in a memory area that libnx sizes at 8 MiB. GLideN64 keeps up to 8,000 textures, and past about 5,000 every new texture failed to load (GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY), which showed as black or noisy surfaces until the game was restarted. The area is now 32 MiB. On the console, a tour of seven levels with the texture cache full (8,000 textures, more than 10,000 created) gave no error, where the old build failed from 5,200 textures.

- **Resolution 4x (1080p, experimental):** 1280x960 drawn into a 1920x1080 picture, 16:9 kept, for a docked console. It costs more GPU time and was measured at 1428 MHz only. Settings > Display > Resolution, then Restart Game.

- **Dev Tools > Warp** now waits for a loaded file: a warp from the intro left the main menu without input.

## DARK SOULS II: Scholar of the First Sin — Switch, build v121

Static recompilation of the Xbox 360 release (Title ID `465307E4`) with a native Vulkan renderer.
You need your **own Xbox 360 game files** and Compatibility Pack 4 — none are included.

### What's new since v104
- **Start screen** (Dark Souls style): choose **720p** (native, default) or **540p** (higher FPS where the GPU is the limit,
  optional **sharpening**), **Frame Rate Lock 30/60**, and the **interface language** (Russian / English / the one set
  in `ds2.toml`). Buttons or touch. The choice is remembered and starts automatically after 20 s; press any button
  or touch the screen to stay.
- **No more stutter on autosave:** saving no longer freezes the game for ~0.1 s every 30–60 s.
- **Faster game code:** profile-guided optimisation of the recompiled code and tuned critical-section spinning.
- **Bottom-of-screen blur strip fixed** (depth of field read stale rows).
- Resolves that did not change are skipped (less GPU work in some scenes).
- Crash fixes around the achievement notification and recoverable game faults.

### Installation
Copy to `sdmc:/switch/ds2/`:
```text
ds2.nro
ds2.toml
ds2_shaders.spvlib
ds2_shaders.spvlib.idx
game_root/   (your Xbox 360 game files, original structure)
dlc/         (your Compatibility Pack 4 STFS file)
```
Install `DARK SOULS II Scholar of the First Sin (port) [0100D52000560000][v0].nsp` with DBI, as usual (same as v104).

**Updating from v104 or earlier:**
1. Delete from `sdmc:/switch/ds2/`: `ds2_shaders_v103.spvlib`, `ds2_shaders_v103.spvlib.idx`, `ds2_shaders_v104.spvlib`,
   `ds2_shaders_v104.spvlib.idx` and `ds2_shader_cache.spvlib` (recreated automatically).
2. Copy `ds2.nro`, `ds2.toml`, `ds2_shaders.spvlib` and `ds2_shaders.spvlib.idx`, replacing existing files.
3. Keep `user/` (your saves).

From v121 on the shader pack has a fixed name: future updates only replace `ds2.nro` and `ds2.toml`.

> [!WARNING]
> `ds2.toml` requests non-stock clocks (CPU 1963 / GPU 1267 / RAM 2500 MHz). They only apply with a suitable
> clock sysmodule and hardware. Set `ds2_switch_cpu_mhz`, `ds2_switch_gpu_mhz`, `ds2_switch_mem_mhz` to 0 to keep stock clocks.

❤️ **Enjoying the port?**
If this project helped you out, consider [buying me a coffee on Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/thorhax) or supporting on [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/c/Thorhax) to support future updates!
------

### Runtime update
Ducktales-NX now builds on [Thorhax/android32](https://github.com/Thorhax/android32), a fork of aks796's [android32](https://github.com/aks796/android32) runtime. The fork is based on aks796's current runtime, and the three fixes this port needed for FMOD's sound now live in the runtime itself instead of in workarounds:
- **Thread stacks from 8 KB, as Android allows,** so FMOD can create the threads that stream the music and voices.
- **OpenSL ES found through `dlsym`,** with the audio configuration interface FMOD requires.
- **A load-order-aware import generator,** so functions that only a later library provides are no longer left silently unbound.

What this means for you:
- **The same features as 1.2.0:** music, voices, cheats and quick save/load.
- **Slightly lower CPU use,** because the port no longer needs its own extra wrapper layer.
- **Hardware-tested:** 60 fps, music, voices and effects, cheats and quick save.

### Updating
Copy the new `ducktales_nx.nro` over the old one in `sd:/switch/ducktales_nx/`, then launch your icon. The launcher installs the new version itself.

As always, no game files are included: you need your own APK and OBB (see the [README](https://github.com/Thorhax/Ducktales-NX#install)).

packages.changelog:
# Emulanders 1.0.1

Maintenance release. No change to the sysmodule's behaviour; the main changes are in Emulanders Portal and the overlay translations.

## Changes

### Emulanders Portal
- Language support expanded from 2 to 10: English, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Russian, Korean, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese. The selection is stored in `sdmc:/emulanders/config.json` and shared with the overlay.
- Buttons now size themselves to their label, and the language and theme lists wrap onto a new row, so longer translations no longer overflow.
- Cyrillic and CJK text is rendered with the console's shared system fonts.
- Figure Image Editor: the `Figures / Scans / Favorites` and `Menu / Back` buttons are on a single row, and the step header is one line instead of three. This gives the figure and photo lists roughly 95 px of extra height (about seven visible rows instead of four).
- Figure Image Editor (Step 3 Crop Tool): tuned live preview sizing and button heights so `(B) Back to Photos` has generous vertical clearance and is never clipped by the bottom status bar in 720p handheld mode.
- Download failures (no network, bad URL) are reported instead of silently extracting an empty archive.
- Fixed controller hot-plugging when docking and undocking, and resizing between 720p and 1080p.

### Tesla overlay
- All 10 languages are fully translated (previously only English and Portuguese were).
- Reads the language chosen in the Portal; falls back to the system language otherwise.
- Fixed the version-mismatch warning, which was being overwritten and never shown.

### Sysmodule
- Fixed a possible panic when the debug log was trimmed in the middle of a multi-byte character (for example accented figure names).

## Packages

| File | Contents |
|:--|:--|
| `Emulanders-Bundle-1.0.1.zip` | Everything: sysmodule, overlay, Portal and language files. Extract to the SD card root. |
| `Emulanders-Portal-1.0.1.zip` | Portal only (`switch/EmulandersPortal/`). |
| `Emulanders-Core-1.0.1.zip` | Sysmodule and overlay only. |
| `emulanders_assets_pack.zip` | Portrait pack (unchanged, from 1.0.0). |

## Upgrading from 1.0.0
Extract the bundle over the existing install and restart the console. Figures, assets and settings are kept. The sysmodule and overlay must be updated together; the overlay warns if their versions differ.

## Compatibility
Fully verified and tested on **Firmware 23.0.1 with Atmosphère 1.12.1** (CNX 23.0.1-1) and Firmware 22.1 with Atmosphère 1.11.1. Full hardware validation confirmed for `nfc:mf:u` protocol emulation, physical Joy-Con Mifare tag dumping, Tesla Overlay hot-swapping, and in-game figure write-back. Compatible with all firmwares 4.0.0+.

## Credits
- XorTroll and Emuiibo contributors (Subv, ogniK, averne, spx01, SciresM): original sysmodule architecture and `nfp-mitm` research.
- libtesla developers (AD2076, AmonRaNet): overlay framework.
- Switchbrew and the aarch64-switch-rs team: libnx and the Rust bindings.
- Skylanders community: research on the figure format.

Art assets are pre-cached at startup, so maps, saves and area transitions load quicker. Note that initial load will be a bit longer. I would expect less stutter if any also. - Runtime diagnostics overlay. Press L+R+Right Stick Click for live FPS, frame time, memory usage and startup load timing. More a curio than useful to average person using this, but at least you can tell me if there's bad framerate somewhere! ### Controls - **L shoulder button now toggles active item, to stop using the cursor to do it. Should make switching items much, much smoother.** - Pressing the left stick now opens the native keyboard when a text input field is present. Otherwise, it's stealth mode. - No more accidental double-triggers on menus, inventory, the Skilldex and quick save/load. ### Native keyboard - Character names, save names and search dialogs all use the Switch software keyboard, sorry about this not being included on initial release. - Item quantity dialogs use a dedicated numeric keypad instead of increment and decrement buttons. - The "Ask About" dialog for dialogue with NPCs opens the keyboard automatically. ### Save compatibility - Save files from the PC version of Fallout 1 CE generally work on Switch now, and Switch saves work back on PC. Some heavily modded or unusual saves may still fail to load. **This is experimental.** - Make backups before moving saves between platforms. ### Setup and configuration - `fallout1_nx.ini` is created automatically on first launch with sensible defaults. - Introduced `fallout1` fallback folder on root of SD card, like the Fallout 2 port. [Fallout 2 port that I've also worked on. (similar QOL updates soon!)](https://github.com/ryandeering/fallout2-ce-switch/releases/latest) Thank you for your patience and enjoy. ## Vulkan rendering

- Stencil shadows take fewer GPU instructions to read vertices when their streams use the same byte order. This applies to the shadow volumes that F.E.A.R. draws for dynamic lights.
- Vulkan reuses the full 1280×720 depth texture when only stencil has changed since the previous conversion. A depth write or clear forces a fresh conversion. Effects that read stencil still receive its current value.

The existing Switch FPS measurements are for v0.2.0. [Performance by clock setting](https://github.com/infriker/fear-nx/blob/v0.2.1/docs/performance.md#switch-performance-in-v020)

## Updating

To update an existing installation and keep your settings, replace `sdmc:/switch/fear-nx/fear_nx.nro`. For a fresh installation with your own Xbox 360 game files, use the [browser installer](https://infriker.github.io/fear-nx/).

# Friday Night Funkin' V-Slice 0.8.7 for Nintendo Switch (unofficial) — release 1

An unofficial homebrew port of the official V-Slice engine by The Funkin' Crew, version 0.8.7, aiming to play exactly like the PC game.

## Install

1. Copy `Funkin.nro` to `/switch/Friday-Night-Funkin/Funkin.nro` on the SD card (or install it from the Homebrew App Store).
2. Open the homebrew menu **from a game** (hold R while launching any title) and start it.
3. On first launch it downloads the official game files (about 734 MB) from The Funkin' Crew's repository, [FunkinCrew/funkin.assets](https://github.com/FunkinCrew/funkin.assets), at the commit of version 0.8.7, checks each file against its SHA-256 and restarts into the game. Without internet on the console, the screen explains how to copy the files from a computer.

About 1.1 GB free on the SD card is needed. Saves and mods live in `/switch/Friday-Night-Funkin/`.

## What's in it

- V-Slice 0.8.7: every week, Weekend 1, Erect and Pico mixes, Freeplay, Story Mode, Character Select and Polymod mods.
- Asset installer with resume after a lost connection or a closed game.
- Cutscenes played from the official video files (minimal LGPL FFmpeg on a free CPU core).
- A Switch audio driver that recovers after HOME, sleep and long sessions; memory management for the console's heap; GPU at 460.8 MHz handheld and 768 MHz docked.
- Nintendo button layout and names, HD Rumble, Switch settings page.

## The .nro contains no game assets

It contains the game's code (Apache-2.0), the port's code and libraries, and a list of the official files with their sizes and hashes. No art, music, sounds, videos, charts or scripts from Friday Night Funkin' are distributed here; they come from The Funkin' Crew's own repository, under its licence, for your own use. Please don't share them.

## Licences

- Game and port code: Apache License 2.0.
- FFmpeg (LGPL 2.1+), built with `tools/nx-tools/build_ffmpeg_nx.sh` from the FFmpeg 7.1 release; OpenAL Soft (LGPL 2.0+) from devkitPro's `switch-openal-soft`; SDL2 (zlib); curl (curl licence); Mesa, FreeType, HarfBuzz and the other devkitPro portlibs under their licences. The full source to rebuild and relink this `.nro` is in this repository at this tag, with every library pinned in `hmm.json`.

## Credits

- The Funkin' Crew: Friday Night Funkin'. Please support the official game.
- FunkinNXTeam (ヴェン, Andres_Github and the team): the first V-Slice 0.8.1 Switch port this one started from.
- Slushi: lime-nx and hx_libnx.

# Golden Balloon NX v1.2.1-nx1

This update focuses on **save support, stability, and Nintendo Switch performance**.

## Highlights

### 💾 Save & configuration fixes

* Fixed save data handling on Nintendo Switch.
* Adventure progress can now be stored correctly on the SD card.
* Configuration/settings persistence has also been improved.
* Save data and configuration are stored under:
  `sdmc:/switch/goldenballoon/`

If you are upgrading from the previous release, you can keep your existing `save/` folder and `mdkr64.ini` and simply replace `goldenballoon.nro`.

### ⚡ Major Switch performance improvements

* Removed a redundant offscreen framebuffer path from normal Switch gameplay.
* Removed an unnecessary full-screen framebuffer blit that was still being performed even when the game was already rendering at native Switch resolution.
* Switch now reports the actual effective 1x render scale to the OpenGL backend instead of retaining Golden Balloon's desktop-oriented 2x supersampling setting.
* Disabled an unused framebuffer-memory compatibility path by default on Switch.
* Added GCC Link-Time Optimization (LTO) for the Switch build.
* Improved performance and frame consistency, especially in heavier areas such as the Adventure Mode hub worlds.
* These optimizations do **not** reduce the normal 1280×720 output resolution.

### 🔊 Audio

* Includes the Switch-specific audio buffering improvements designed to reduce underruns and crackling.
* The game's original audio synthesis rate, music timing, and pitch remain unchanged.

## Installation

Copy:

`goldenballoon.nro`

to:

`sdmc:/switch/goldenballoon/`

A legally dumped **Diddy Kong Racing US 1.1** ROM is required:

`baserom.us.v80.z64`

Place it in the same Golden Balloon folder.

> **No ROM, copyrighted game assets, or Nintendo/Rare game data are included with this release.**

## Notes

Golden Balloon NX is still under active development. Further Switch-specific CPU/GPU optimizations and presentation improvements are being investigated.

Thanks to everyone testing the port and reporting issues! ❤️

## Performance Edition — stable test build

> **This is not the final GTA4NX version.** Development continues toward a port that is truly
> worthy of Nintendo Switch. v35 is the established performance-focused option while that work
> continues.

### Who should use this build?

Choose v35 if you want the more conservative, established option. It uses a longer 150 m horizon
and more traffic/pedestrians than v50 RC1, with a lower nearby detail scale of 0.45.

### Observed performance

These are approximate results from real Nintendo Switch testing, not fixed guarantees. Performance
can vary with the area, time of day, on-screen effects, shader cache and console mode.

- General gameplay: **25–30 FPS**.
- Some interiors: up to **30 FPS**.
- Driving through the city: **22–28 FPS**, depending on the in-game time of day.

### Improvements in v35

- The small sun-shadow-caster filter now works during normal gameplay, instead of depending on the
  profiler's pass tag.
- Three diagnostic fixed-state hashes per draw are disabled on Switch.
- A diagnostic setting is read once per frame instead of copied for every renderer command.
- Repeated `required-binding-failed` messages are rate-limited, preventing tens of thousands of
  synchronous SD-card log writes during a session.
- Retains the established PGO build, native audio DSP, texture cache without age-based eviction and
  reserved texture memory arena.

### Profile

| Setting | v35 Performance |
|---|---:|
| Nearby detail scale | 0.45 |
| Far clip | 150 m |
| Traffic / parked cars | 0.38 / 0.35 |
| Pedestrians / scenario pedestrians | 0.45 / 0.45 |
| Sun-shadow distance scale | 0.65 |

### Installation

Players only need **`GTA4NX-v35-performance.zip`**. Extract it to the root of the SD card and keep
the included NRO and profile together:

```text
sdmc:/switch/gta4nx/gta4nx.nro
sdmc:/switch/gta4nx/LibertyRecomp/native.toml
```

You still need your own GTA IV Xbox 360 USA disc files and Title Update 8. See the
[Spanish installation guide](https://github.com/kabba536/Grand-Theft-Auto-IV-Native-Port-Nintendo-Switch/blob/main/INSTALL_ES.md)
for the full procedure. Developers can download the separately named source-code ZIP.

# Guardian Heroes (XBLA, 2011) static recompilation, build 0.79.0c97cca

An unofficial port of **Guardian Heroes** (Xbox Live Arcade, Treasure/Sega, 2011, title ID `58410B2B`) to **Nintendo Switch** and **PC (Linux, Windows)**.
The Xbox 360 program is recompiled to native code with the [ReXGlue SDK](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) v0.10.0.
Switch: deko3d renderer, libnx audio, 60 fps. PC: Vulkan.

**No game data is included.** You need your own copy of the game (the XBLA package, title ID `58410B2B`; the recompiled code matches the retail `default.xex` of 2011, 3,178,496 bytes). See the README for how to extract it.

## Files
| File | Platform |
| --- | --- |
| `gh-0.79.0c97cca-switch.zip` | Switch (unzip to the SD card root) |
| `gh-0.79.0c97cca-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64, needs a Vulkan driver |
| `gh-0.79.0c97cca-windows-x86_64.zip` | Windows x86-64, needs a Vulkan driver (MSVC runtime DLLs are included) |
| `SHA256SUMS`, `SHA1SUMS` | checksums |

## New in 0.79
- Switch menu (**+** and **-** together): a new item **overlay** turns the version + fps strip on or off.
- The three menu settings (fps counter, sound, overlay) are saved in `sdmc:/switch/gh/settings.txt` and restored at the next start.
- A step-by-step guide for sprite replacement: `docs/SPRITE-REPLACEMENT.md` (files, formats, tools, the mod folder, how to test, pitfalls).

## Switch: install and run
1. Unzip the Switch zip to the root of the SD card. It creates `sdmc:/switch/gh/`.
2. Copy your extracted `game/` folder (it holds `default.xex` and `media/`) to `sdmc:/switch/gh/game/`.
3. Start **Guardian Heroes** from the homebrew menu in **title takeover**: hold **R** while you start any game. Applet mode is not tested.
4. Buttons follow the Xbox layout by position (Switch B = Xbox A). **+** and **-** together open a small menu (resume, fps counter, sound, overlay). **-** is Back (skips cut scenes).
The version shows at the bottom-left of the screen. Logs: `sdmc:/switch/gh/gh_log.txt`.

## What works
- Switch: Story mode at 60 fps, both graphics modes (Remix and Original), sound, Nintendo-style button icons, a sprite replacement hook (`sdmc:/switch/gh/mods/sprites/`, see `docs/SPRITE-REPLACEMENT.md`).
- Linux and Windows: plays, keyboard and gamepad, in-game settings window (F1 or Start+Back).

## Known issues
- Xbox Live, avatar items and the camera are not supported.
- Switch: only title takeover is tested. Not every mode and stage was played through.
- Linux: sound not checked by ear. Windows: gamepad not checked.
- Sprite replacement works on Switch only.

## Licence and legal
- The source code is BSD 3-clause, with parts of the ReXGlue SDK (BSD 3-clause, (c) Tom Clay) and the Xenia project (BSD 3-clause, (c) Ben Vanik and contributors). See `LICENSE`.
- **The binaries contain the recompiled game program** (the Xbox 360 code translated to native code). That is a derived work of the original game code and is not covered by the BSD licence. They contain no graphics, sound or music of the game. Use them only with a copy of the game that you own, and at your own risk. The authors are not linked to Sega, Treasure or Microsoft.
- Do not ask for game files.

- **Massive Performance Boost:** Significantly smoother framerates and drastically reduced frame-time latency compared to OpenGL, especially when running intensive gameplay mods like *Brutal Doom*.
- **Dynamic Light Optimization:** Completely eliminated GPU hangs and stalls when loading dynamic light buffers.
- **Credit:** Immense credit and special thanks to **[NaGa](https://github.com/NaGaa95)** for developing the Vulkan driver for Nintendo Switch!

## 🎼 Soundfont Support (.sf2) & Setup
- **Direct Soundfont Selector:** You can now choose your active soundfont directly inside the game! Go to `Options -> Sound Options -> Soundfont`.
- **Auto-Detection:** GZDoom automatically scans `sdmc:/switch/gzdoom/soundfonts/` and loads external soundfonts seamlessly.
- **Supported Synthesizers:** Upgraded **FluidSynth** and **Timidity++** engines.

### How to Use Soundfonts:
1. Place your `.sf2` files into `sdmc:/switch/gzdoom/soundfonts/` (e.g., `AweROMGM.sf2`, `SC-55.sf2`, `FluidR3_GM.sf2`, `gzdoom.sf2`).
2. In-game, open **Options** -> **Sound Options**.
3. Set **MIDI Device** to **FluidSynth** (or **Timidity++**).
4. Select your preferred soundfont from the **Soundfont** option list.

## 📦 Package Contents
- `gzdoom.nro` (Vulkan-enabled GZDoom 4.14.2 binary)
- `gzdoom.pk3`, `brightmaps.pk3`, `game_widescreen_gfx.pk3`, `game_support.pk3`, `lights.pk3`
- `gzdoom_launcher.nro` (Mod / IWAD selector)
- Default soundfonts & FM sound banks

## Installation
Extract `gzdoom_2026_switch_release.zip` to the root of your SD card (`sdmc:/switch/gzdoom/`). Place IWADs in `iwads/` and mods in `pwads/`.
Extraxt the `extract.this.too.zip` to the root of your SD card for OTHER necessary files.

I've included my recommended `gzdoom.ini` file which enabled autorun and turns off vertical look with the right analog stick.

Additionally I have include an edited Brutal Doom v21(The most recent full release), which allows vertical auto aim, so you don't need to use mouse look to shoot up and down. As well as removing recoil from weapons so you'll never have to adjust the camera.
Just the way Carmack Intended!

packages.changelog:
Build 143: Faster map sharing, custom Xbox maps and moving game files!

### Map sharing

- New: between two SlipstreamCE machines, maps go over a fast encrypted connection of their own instead of the game's tunnel, for both MCC packages and Custom Edition maps. A joiner opens up to 16 connections to the host (4 on the Switch), all through one port, which the host forwards with UPnP; a host serves 32 in all. Over the internet a joiner connects straight to the host's address when it can. A Custom Edition map still comes from the other players too, with the host as one more source. OpenCE hosts and joiners work as before. (thelinkin3000)
- Uploads use the whole line outside a game. During a game they leave room for the game's own traffic and slow down only when the players' pings show the line filling up. (thelinkin3000)
- The upload limits in Network Setup and Server Setup go up to 250 MB/s. (thelinkin3000)
- A download's speed is shown correctly past 2 MB/s. (thelinkin3000)
- Fixed: a download stuck at 0 KB/s when the host offered the map as the player joined. (thelinkin3000)
- Fixed: the Switch froze for 20 to 30 seconds while downloading a map and was dropped from the game. Downloaded pieces are now written to the SD card on a thread of their own. (thelinkin3000)

### Custom Xbox multiplayer maps

- New: Xbox multiplayer maps (from mods such as Halo CE+ X) can go in custom_maps. They're listed, described as "Custom Xbox multiplayer map", shared, and played like the game's own maps, even when they have the same names as the stock ones. (thelinkin3000)
- A dedicated server's rotation takes them. An Xbox campaign map is still refused, with a message saying why. (thelinkin3000)
- A game on one of these maps needs a client that supports them. A player whose client doesn't is told "You need a client with support for custom OG Xbox multiplayer maps." and removed. (thelinkin3000)

### Game files (Android)

- New: Settings > Gameplay > GAME FILES moves your maps, custom maps, mods and MCC maps to another place: APP DATA (the app's storage) or OTHER FOLDER (any folder you choose, such as one on a memory card). The game restarts to move them and shows its progress, then says where they are. A move that stops loses nothing: try again, or move them back. (thelinkin3000)

### Hosted servers

- Watching a player through their eyes from the host's screen now turns smoothly, as a replay does, instead of jumping each time their input arrives. (thelinkin3000)

### Custom campaigns (experimental)

- New: play an Xbox or Custom Edition campaign from its own folder in custom_campaigns, alone or in split screen. Its maps are found by the names inside them, so nothing needs renaming, and a campaign never mixes with the stock maps or with another campaign. A campaign with its own ui.map uses it as the main menu, with a BACK TO HALO button added. Each campaign has its own saved game. For now a campaign is chosen in config.toml (`[debug] custom_campaign = "<folder>"`); a menu for it comes later. (thelinkin3000)
- The unpacked map cache is now kept in memory on Android and the PS5, as it already was on the Switch, and it's emptied whenever the maps change under the same names. The old cache files on disk (about 730 MB) are deleted once. (thelinkin3000)

### Steam Workshop and MCC

- A joiner's Workshop download shows its progress and speed, says it's from the Workshop, and moves to another content server sooner when one refuses. (thelinkin3000)
- Fixed: a joiner was asked to download from the host a package Steam had already installed. (thelinkin3000)
- The Workshop screen's NEXT and PREVIOUS PAGE select the new page's first item, an installed item asks DOWNLOAD AGAIN? before downloading it again, and the rows' names are wider with shorter messages. (thelinkin3000)
- A hosted server identifies an MCC package's Workshop item from its ModInfo.json when it has no download record. (thelinkin3000)
- Security fixes from a review of the Steam client: a malform

Hard Corps: Uprising (Xbox 360 XBLA, 2011) on Nintendo Switch, by static recompilation with the ReXGlue SDK. Built from commit `c728c58`. This release has the Switch build only: the PC code did not change since 0.303 (see "Windows and Linux" below).

## New since 0.303

- **Boss and enemy graphics**: 12 shaders that were missing on the console are now translated (34 files in `shaders/`). Without them some objects were not drawn, for example the cart enemy and parts of a boss cannon on stage 1.
- **Switch button icons** in the game's prompts: our own drawings of the Switch buttons (A, B, X, Y, L, R, ZL, ZR, +, -, the d-pad, the sticks, HOME) replace the Xbox icons. No Nintendo files are used.
- New port menu item **BUTTON ICONS**: SWITCH (default) or XBOX (the game's Xbox icons with the A/B and X/Y pictures swapped, as in 0.303). It applies at the next start. In `settings.txt`: `button_glyphs=switch` or `button_glyphs=xbox`.
- The log `hcu_log.txt` names each shader pair that has no translated shader (one line per pair), so a missing object can be reported with its shader numbers.

## Known gaps

- The boss and cart fix is checked on stage 1 only.
- Not replaced yet: the controller picture on the How to play screen, the Guide button ring, and the texts "Press START" and "Xbox 360 controller" that are part of the game's images.

## Read this first: experimental

- **Very little testing.** A few hours of single player on one console, and a short check of local 2-player and the DLC characters. Many stages and menus are not checked. Graphical glitches, crashes and freezes are possible, and save data may be lost.
- **Local 2-player needs two full controllers**: a Pro Controller, a Joy-Con pair, or the console in handheld mode. A single Joy-Con (one half) is not supported. The Xbox LIVE features are not available.
- **30 fps by default.** The game runs at full speed and every second frame is drawn. The 60 fps modes (FRAME RATE in the port menu) can slow the game down in busy scenes.
- Enemy cries may sound too loud.
- Quit with the game's own menu, not by resetting the console.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `hcu-0.310.c728c58-switch.zip` | Switch (Atmosphère + hbmenu). Unzip to the SD root. To update 0.303, unzip over it: your `settings.txt`, game files and saves stay |

- Docked, or with the Joy-Cons detached, wireless controller 1 is player 1 and wireless controller 2 is player 2.

PCSX2 on Nintendo Switch — **Vulkan/NVK** branch (separate lineage from the deko3d `master`).

### Highlights
- **Vulkan GS renderer (`GSDeviceVK`)** running on the switch-nvk (NVK/Mesa) driver, replacing the hand-written deko3d path. Loaderless ICD bootstrap, zero-copy `VK_NN_vi_surface` WSI, runtime TFX shader compile.
- **FastmemLite identity-map fix** — keeps the EE fast path enabled across identity TLB maps of the low 32MB instead of disabling on any TLB write (big EE perf win for games that identity-map, e.g. to set a cache mode).
- Reverted the AArch64 vector-register-file expansion (it regressed FPS via the MTVU sync stub on this hardware).
- Docker build + nxlink deploy tooling.

### Install (clean Switch)
1. Copy `armsx2nx.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/`.
2. Put your **PS2 BIOS** dump in `sdmc:/switch/armsx2/bios/` (required, not bundled).
3. Put game ISOs in `sdmc:/switch/armsx2/games/`.
Resources/shaders/driver are bundled in the NRO and self-extract on first boot.

> WARNING - untested-on-hardware: the FastmemLite identity-map change is correct by construction but still needs on-device validation per game.

Built from branch vulkan-nvk @ 45d51127.

## How Many Dudes? NX v1.0.0

The first public release of the unofficial **How Many Dudes? Android wrapper for Nintendo Switch**.

This port runs the original Android ARM64 GameMaker runner natively through a lightweight Android/JNI compatibility layer.

### Features

- Fully playable gameplay
- Touch-screen controls
- ASTC texture rendering
- Native audio playback
- In-game cutscene support
- Local saves and preferences
- Suspend and resume support
- Optimized performance during high-unit-count battles
- Automatic handheld and docked resolutions
- Built-in crash and performance logging

### Controls

This game is designed around tapping, dragging, and direct unit placement. Therefore, this port intentionally uses the Nintendo Switch touch screen.

**Handheld mode is required for practical gameplay.** Joy-Con and Pro Controller controls are not currently supported.

### Installation

This release does not include any copyrighted game files.

You need a legally obtained Android ARM64 APK of **How Many Dudes?**, specifically build `100.0.890` (`com.bscotch.hmd`).

From the APK, extract:

- `lib/arm64-v8a/libyoyo.so`
- The complete `assets/` folder
- The APK itself, renamed to `game.apk`

Place everything on your SD card as follows:

```text
sdmc:/switch/hmd_nx/
├── hmd_nx.nro
├── libyoyo.so
├── game.apk
└── assets/
    ├── game.droid
    └── ...
```

Launch the Homebrew Menu using a full title override by holding **R** while opening an installed game. Applet/Album mode is not supported.

See the repository README for automatic Windows setup and complete instructions.

### Limitations

- Google Play Games, cloud saves, achievements, billing, ads, and Android in-app updates are unavailable.
- Other APK versions may use a different GameMaker runner and are not guaranteed to work.
- Controller input is not implemented.

### NRO Checksum

SHA-256:

```text
8CA8DFF643C3AC9DFA97C9710887459E23ED035E6C016F71A1FC9F3C14E45EA0
```

### Legal

This is an unofficial compatibility wrapper. No APK, game code, `libyoyo.so`, `game.droid`, or other original asset is included.

**How Many Dudes?** and its assets belong to Butterscotch Shenanigans and their respective rightsholders. Users must obtain the original game legally.

- **Saving to all three slots works**: the game no longer says there are not enough free blocks
- **Pressing B on the save slot screen no longer closes the game**: it asked for the Xbox Dashboard; the game now restarts instead

> **How to save:** the game does not save on its own. Open the menu and choose **Save** to write your progress.

Earlier in 0.3.x:
- **Docking now switches the resolution live** (0.3.0 kept the one it started with)
- **Steadier 30 fps** in busy scenes: the recompiled game code is 20-35% shorter in its hottest functions (stack accesses skip a needless address check, the memory base is loaded once per function), and the renderer does less work per draw
- **No more shader stutter** after the first run: the shader cache was being written to another port's folder and never loaded; it now lives in `/switch/iceage2/`
- **Sharper when docked**: renders at 1440×1080 docked and 640×480 handheld, switching live when you dock

Resolution can be changed in `/switch/iceage2/iceage2_env.txt` (`RECOMP_DOCK_SCALE`, `RECOMP_HANDHELD_SCALE`). Above the defaults, overclock the console (sys-clk) or busy scenes drop below 30 fps.

The NSP forwarder is unchanged: if you installed it before, just replace `iceage2.nro`.

Installation:
1. Extract the archive to the root of your SD card: you get `/switch/iceage2/`.

packages.changelog:
**Jak II and Jak 3 on the native deko3d renderer: big bug-fix + performance update.** This is still a **Beta**.

## Jak 3 — What's New
- **60 FPS in Haven City**: Jak 3 now holds 60 FPS even in busy fights (tested with ~28 flying enemies on screen). It used to run at about 50 FPS with constant stutter.
- **Stutter fixed**: The game no longer checks the save card every frame (it waited ~11 ms per frame for streaming reads).
- **Black screen after death fixed**: The screen now comes back after you lose a life.
- **World drawn at the correct height**: World geometry is no longer stretched.
- **Missing textures fixed**: The minimap, eyes and animated textures draw correctly again.
- **Menu background fixed**: No more plain yellow background in the pause menu.
- **Faster sky**: The sky is drawn at half resolution, with no visible loss.
- **Weather cheats**: Good/Bad weather now work properly and can't both be on at once.

## Jak II — What's New
- **Much better performance**: Removed a debug log that was writing ~11,000 lines per second to the SD card.
- **Mission black screen fixed**: Some missions no longer go to a black screen.
- **Audio sync fixed**: Voices and cutscenes stay in sync.
- **Screen effects restored**: Zoom blur, colour filter, slow-motion and fades now draw correctly (the fade is no longer drawn twice).
- **Faster sky**: Half-resolution sky, with no visible loss.
- **Weather cheats**: Bad Weather turns off instantly, and the cheats are remembered between boots.
- **Less stutter**: Same save-card fix as Jak 3.

No overclock is needed, and game resolution is unchanged.

## Known Issues
- Loading a new area can still pause for a moment.
- Please report any save/load problems: save-card handling changed in this build.
- Black walls

## Install
1. Download the latest source (`main`) and **re-run the extractor for Jak II and Jak 3** (see the README) to update your `data/` folders.
2. Copy `jak2.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/jak2/jak2.nro` and `jak3.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/jak3/jak3.nro`, replacing the old files. To roll back, restore your previous NROs.

Jak 1 is unchanged; keep using `v1.0-jak1`.

Native ARM64 static recompilation of Lost Odyssey (Xbox 360) for the Nintendo Switch 2, running under [kaiHEN](https://github.com/ouncebrew/kaihen) with Vulkan graphics through [OunceVK](https://github.com/ouncebrew/ouncevk).

**No disc files are included.** You need your own Lost Odyssey discs.

### What's in this version
- Targets 60 FPS: dynamic resolution (576–1080p handheld, 720–1440p docked) with FSR 1.
- Handheld: 60 FPS in fields at up to 1920×1080; 52–59 FPS in Uhra's Main Street.
- Settings changes (resolution, FSR, effects, overlay) apply while playing.
- Fixed: GPU stops after closing menus or changing graphics settings (NVK command overrun from large clears).
- HOME → X closes the game cleanly; kaiHEN's R hook keeps working.

### Install
1. Extract your discs with the [PC version](https://github.com/freefrank/LostOdysseyRecomp/releases/latest)'s importer ([how](https://github.com/Jorsall1/LostOdysseyRecomp/blob/switch2-ouncevk/docs/INSTALL-SWITCH.md#step-1-extract-your-discs-on-a-pc)). 2. Extract this ZIP to the **root** of the SD card. It creates `switch/LostOdysseyRecomp/` with the game, `env.txt` and the shaders.
3. Copy `disc1`–`disc4` into `sdmc:/switch/LostOdysseyRecomp/game/`.
4. Hold **R** while starting any installed game to open the Homebrew Menu, then choose **Lost Odyssey Recomp**.

The full SD card layout is in the [README](https://github.com/Jorsall1/LostOdysseyRecomp#sd-card-layout).

### Credits
Switch 2 port by [Jorsall1](https://github.com/Jorsall1) and Claude ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com)). ## kickNX v0.5.2

### Added
- **Daily Reward bar**: while you watch a live stream signed in, a bar above chat shows your progress toward Kick's daily watch reward, counting up smoothly. When it is full, press the right stick to claim it and see the collectible you got.
- **Gift button on Home**: a small window with your daily reward progress, a Claim button when it is ready, or the time until it resets.
- **Emote tabs**: Recent, Channel, Global and Collectibles, in landscape and portrait. Animated collectible emotes now animate in chat.
- **Subscriber emotes** in the Channel tab when Kick confirms you are subscribed.
- **Stream thumbnails for followed channels**: live followed cards show the stream's thumbnail instead of the streamer's profile picture.
- **Count watch time for rewards**: a Player Settings switch to turn watch time reporting off.

### Changed
- **Watch time check-ins**: kickNX reports watch time in a brief check-in every 2 minutes instead of holding a connection open for the whole stream.
- **Fewer connections for chat**, and emote lists are kept for ten minutes per channel.

### Fixed
- **Wi-Fi drops**: chat reconnect loops, buffering and "Couldn't resolve host" errors that often needed Airplane mode to clear. kickNX now asks the Switch to keep its internet connection, as games do, and waits out brief drops instead of failing.
- **Channel emotes missing** after the Switch sat idle or after switching channels.
- **Emote pictures turning into text** after watching several channels.
- **SSL errors and buffering when sending** chat messages.
- **Stretched thumbnails** on stream and clip cards, **blurry live event cards**, and **cropped offline profile pictures**.

> [!TIP]
> **Full RAM Mode Recommended:** For the best performance and 60 FPS playback stability, launch the Homebrew Menu by holding the **`R`** button while launching any installed game (title override), rather than launching through the Album. Will not run in applet mode.

### Install

packages.changelog:
**Kirikiroid2-NX v1.0.1** — compatibility fixes.

### What's new
- **windowEx plugin** added (the Android APK has it built in). Games that call `Window.registerExEvent()` and other windowEx methods no longer stop with *Member "registerExEvent" does not exist* — e.g. **Ninki Seiyuu: How to Make a Pop Voice Actress** (#1).
- **Modal dialogs close properly.** A dialog opened with `showModal()` is now hidden when it closes. Before, a game's own dialog (e.g. Ninki Seiyuu's language selection) stayed on screen, or left the game on a black screen.
- **No more black bars on 16:9 games.** The screen was set up as 960×640 internally, so 16:9 games (most of them) got thin black bars at the top and bottom and the UI was slightly squashed. It now uses the real 1280×720.
- The log file is saved to the SD card once a second, so it is kept even when you close the app with HOME.

### Install / update
1. Download `Kirikiroid2-NX.nro` below and copy it to `sdmc:/switch/` (replace the old one).
2. Open the Homebrew Menu in **title-takeover mode** (hold **R** while launching a game) and start Kirikiroid2-NX. Applet mode (from the Album) does not have enough memory for most games.
3. Copy your game folder to the SD card as you would for Kirikiroid2 on Android and open `data.xp3` from the file selector.

### Known issues
- Yes/No system message boxes always pick the first button.
- Plugins not ported yet: KAGParserEx, E-mote/motion player, scriptsEx, layerExRaster, layerExMosaic, shrinkCopy and others.
- Exiting a game may show "The software was closed because an error occurred".
- Software renderer only.

Logs for bug reports are written to `sdmc:/switch/kirikiroid2/` (`k2s_boot.txt`, `k2s_log.txt`, `k2s_log.prev.txt`, `k2s_crash.txt`) — please attach them to issues.

No game data is included. Use only games you legally own. `LICENSE` and `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md` apply to the binary.
