### About this preview

First public preview. Plays the Philips CD-i game Laser Lords (1992) natively on macOS,
Windows, Linux / Steam Deck and Nintendo Switch (homebrew), with your own disc image and
without a CD-i emulator or BIOS.

**Works and checked against the real CD-i** (MAME running the original ROM):
- Intro and title: same images, fades and timing; skippable with any button.
- Planet gameplay (Luxor): walking pace, smooth scrolling, screen placement.
- Action menu and conversations (text and voices), sound effects and music.
- Saving and loading through the game's own Computer screens.

**Platforms:** universal macOS app (Intel + Apple Silicon, macOS 11+), Windows x64, Linux
x86_64 (also Steam Deck), Nintendo Switch homebrew (.nro). Tested on macOS and a Switch; the
Windows and Linux builds pass the tests but haven't been run on real machines yet.

**Known limitations**
- All planets have been visited, but the game hasn't been tested extensively yet.
- The macOS app isn't notarised and the Windows exe isn't signed: see READ ME FIRST for how
  to open them.
- No graphics cursor on screen, as on the original (menus use a blinking highlight).


**Downloads**
| System | File |
|---|---|
| macOS 11+ (Intel and Apple Silicon) | `LaserLords-0.8.1-macOS.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11 x64 | `LaserLords-0.8.1-windows-x64.zip` |
| Linux x86_64 / Steam Deck | `LaserLords-0.8.1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |
| Nintendo Switch (homebrew) | `LaserLords-0.8.1-switch.zip` |

You need your own Laser Lords disc image (.chd, or .cue + .bin). No game data, game code or BIOS is included. Unofficial fan project, not affiliated with the game's rights holders; see the README disclaimer. Each download includes READ ME FIRST, the MIT licence and the third-party notices; SHA256SUMS.txt has checksums.

packages.changelog:
**Experimental.** Static recompilation of the Xbox 360 game for Nintendo Switch. **No game data is included:** you need your own copy of the disc. Read the [README](https://github.com/surblazer/legobatman-recomp#readme) first.

## What is new since 0.1.1

- **Fixed:** studs dropped by broken objects were invisible (they were collected, but not drawn). Vertex shaders with a fetch that writes only constants, which Direct3D adds for a vertex element the mesh lacks, read their inputs one slot off. Other models drawn with such shaders are fixed too.
- To update from 0.1.1 or 0.1.0, unzip over it: your saves are kept. The zip's `legobatman.toml` replaces yours, so set your settings again if you changed any.

## Install

1. Unzip `legobatman-0.1.2-switch.zip` to the root of the SD card. It contains `sdmc:/switch/legobatman/legobatman.nro` and `legobatman.toml` (the settings, explained inside).
2. Extract your disc into `sdmc:/switch/legobatman/game_root/`: `default.xex`, `GAME.DAT`, `GAME1.DAT`, `Audio/`, `Movies/`.
3. Start it from hbmenu with title takeover (hold R while starting a game), for the full memory.

Supported disc: *LEGO Batman - The Videogame (USA, Europe) (En,Fr,De,Es,It,Da)*, title ID 575207D7, media ID 191B0669 (`default.xex` SHA-1 `3902914a108c968c4dfcd4991b756a7ff7ec36da`). Other releases and title updates do not work.

## What to expect

- About 30 fps in typical gameplay on a stock Switch Lite; the busiest views drop to 16-20 fps. The 3D image is drawn at 1280x720 and lowered automatically, down to 853x480, when the GPU falls behind. sys-clk (GPU 768 MHz, RAM 1600 MHz) helps the most.
- Every shader on the disc is translated ahead of time and packed into the NRO.
- Status Monitor Overlay shows FPS and the current resolution (SaltyNX 0.7.0 or later).
- The face buttons go by letter (Switch A is Xbox A). `input_xbox_layout = true` in `legobatman.toml` switches to the Xbox positions.

# LM-NX v1.0.1

An update to **LM-NX**, the native Nintendo Switch port of the GameCube version of **Luigi's Mansion**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This release doesn't include the game. You need your own copy of Luigi's Mansion, dumped from your own disc: the USA disc (`GLME01`), the PAL disc (`GLMP01`, Rev 0) or both.

## What's new

### Installer page

- **The PAL disc works on it's own.** The USA disc is no longer required: choose only your PAL disc and the package starts the PAL version.
- **Much smaller packages.** The page keeps only the game's files and leaves out the filler data of the disc: about **190 MB** for the USA disc and **275 MB** for the PAL disc, instead of 1.36 GB each. The game files are unchanged.

  You can turn this off with the **Make the discs smaller** box.

- **Choose the game's language** (English, Spanish, German, French or Italian) before making the package. Spanish, German, French and Italian use the PAL disc.
- **New guide:** *How to use the installer*, opened from the menu or the new **Help** button.

### Game

- **Fixed:** light colours for Luigi's clothes, such as Wario's yellow, turned almost white. They now keep their colour and their shading.
- **Fixed:** with the Fire Luigi preset, the L on the cap was hard to see. The cap is now white with it's white badge and the green L.

## How to change Luigi's colours

1. While playing, press **both sticks at once (L3 + R3)** to open the settings menu.
2. Go to **Enhancements → Silly**, section **Luigi's clothes**.
3. Press one of the **Outfit** buttons to dress Luigi in one go: **Classic** (Luigi's own colours), **Mario**, **Wario**, **Waluigi** or **Fire Luigi**.
4. Or set each piece yourself: tick **Cap**, **Shirt**, **Overalls** or **Shoes** and pick it¡s colour. The **Poltergust 3000** section changes the colour of the vacuum's tank.

The colours change and are saved at once. To go back to normal, press **Classic** and untick **Poltergust**.

## How to update

1. Open the installer page: **https://stevensnd.github.io/lm-nx/**
2. Press **Create lm-nx-update.zip** and copy `LM-NX` folder over the one on your SD card. Your discs, saves and settings stay as they are.

To make your discs smaller or install with only the PAL disc, make a new **lm-nx.zip** instead (your saves are in `guardados/`: keep a copy).

You don't need to download `LM-NX.nro` from this page: the installer page takes it from this release for you.

## Help

- Questions and common problems: the **FAQ** and **Troubleshooting** sections of the [installer page](https://stevensnd.github.io/lm-nx/).
- Found a bug? Open an [issue](https://github.com/StevensND/lm-nx/issues) and attach the files from `sdmc:/switch/LM-NX/logs/`

This is an unofficial, fan-made port with no affiliation with Nintendo. **It's free: if you paid for it, you were scammed.**

Primeira versão pública. Port por recompilação estática feito com o XboxSwitchPortKit: o Direct3D 8 e o DirectSound do Xbox reescritos em Vulkan (NVK) e no áudio do Switch, sem emular a NV2A.

packages.changelog:
Native Nintendo Switch port of Mass Effect (Xbox 360), work in progress.

### What's Changed in v0.2.1

**Please rebuild your shader package.** Packages made with the browser installer before this release missed shaders:
the values in the settings menu and the bar under its title did not draw, and two other game shaders were missing.

- **Installer:** builds every shader of your discs (31,128 of 31,128 on the Russian release with both DLC). It no longer
  skips shaders it cannot make: it retries once and otherwise stops with an error instead of writing an incomplete
  package. Fixed the browser shader translator crashing after many shaders on computers with few CPU cores.
- **Installer:** can install the full NSP straight to the console over USB from Chrome or Edge (Sphaira, Install ->
  USB); nothing is saved on the computer.
- **New companion app for macOS:** [Switch USB Installer](https://github.com/nebadasSwifty/switch-usb-installer) - drag
  an NSP onto it to install it over USB with Sphaira.
- The game itself is the same as v0.2.0.

**How to update:** open [the installer](https://nebadasSwifty.github.io/masseffect-nx/) again and build the package from
your discs, then replace the files on the SD card (at least `masseffect_shaders.mesp` and `masseffect_shaders.mesp.idx`),
or install the new full NSP.

### What's Changed in v0.2.0

**Performance**
- The scene renders at 960x544 and is upscaled to 720p with AMD FSR 1 (sharper than plain scaling at the same cost).
  Most locations now hold 30 fps; the heaviest scenes (Eden Prime after the opening cutscene, large fights) run at 20-26 fps.
- Large CPU and GPU savings in the renderer and the game code: native audio mixing and resampling (NEON), shader constants
  updated per changed vector, vertex data reused across frames, texture sign handling folded into shaders, much cheaper
  EDRAM emulation, fewer per-draw allocations, lighter kernel waits.
- Per-edition shader prewarm list: the game's pipelines are compiled in the background (from 25 s after launch), so the
  0.5-1 s stalls on the first visit of a place are gone.

**Stability**
- Fixed hangs and crashes at start: "Disc Read Error", a frozen intro / BioWare logo, a black screen. Cause: the first
  launch (no shader cache yet) compiled thousands of shaders while the game was loading, and the console ran out of
  system resources. The game now also leaves 64 MB more memory to the system.
- The screen no longer freezes on the intro when the console briefly refuses a frame.
- Long sessions no longer crash on memory fragmentation (shader cache saving, texture uploads); the shader memory use
  is about 200 MB lower.

**Image**
- Fixed missing letters in terminals, dialogues and the autosave label; characters "vanishing" on fast camera turns;
  the black start screen; Shepard rendered black.

**Controls and audio**
- Nintendo Switch button names in the game texts and the Switch layout in the decryption mini-game.
- Rumble on both Joy-Cons, scaled to the game's motor speeds.
- Experimental touch screen (handheld): drag to turn the camera, tap a dialogue option to pick it.
- Fixed a constant buzz that could replace music (XMA loops).

**Installation**
- Installable full NSP per edition (Russian and English install side by side, separate saves): the browser installer
  can build it from your own discs.
- Russian two-disc merge verified on real discs. The unused, broken `GlobalTlk_ES.xxx` of the Russian discs is now a
  short note instead of a "re-dump your discs" warning.

**Known issues**
- Pressing HOME during the first ~30 seconds after launch, while the game is loading, can freeze the console. Wait until
  the main menu.
- Rarely (about 1 launch in 10) the game can stop at the intro. Close it and start it again.
- Sysmodules and overlays use the same system memory the game's display and file access need; with many of them
  installed, the risk of the issues above grows.

### What's Changed in v0.1.3
- **Russian Edition Support*

packages.changelog:
**Headlight beams in both games, and the first Android beta.** At night your car finally lights up the road ahead and we're releasing the Android version for further testing.

## Features

- **Headlight beams.** Turning your lights on at night now throws a beam of light onto the road ahead, as on the original Xbox: it brightens the street, cars and walls it reaches and stops where it meets them ([#10](https://github.com/laureladastra/mcdub3-nx/issues/10), thanks for the report). Before, the lights worked in the game but no beam was drawn. Other emulators (i.e. xemu → https://github.com/xemu-project/xemu/issues/996) show a solid white shape instead. The game builds the beam in a small hidden picture using two tricks of the Xbox's graphics chip that the port did not reproduce yet: it reuses a picture as a depth map, and it counts the beam's layers with a special blending mode that works with negative numbers. Both are emulated now. Tested in the DUB Edition and the Remix. The WHITE button flashes your high beams while you hold it. The main headlights are on by themselves at night.
- **Android beta (app version 0.1.0).** Both games can be installed as an Android app: `mcdub3-0.1.0.apk` (DUB Edition) and `mcdub3remix-0.1.0.apk` (Remix). Like on the Switch you bring your own copy of the game.

## Android Installation Instructions

1. Download the APK for your game from the [release page](https://github.com/laureladastra/mcdub3-nx/releases/tag/v1.1.0): `mcdub3-<version>.apk` for DUB Edition, `mcdub3remix-<version>.apk` for Remix. Both can be installed side by side.
2. Open the APK on your phone to install it. Android asks you to allow installing apps from your browser or file manager; allow it. If Google Play Protect warns about an unknown app, choose **More details › Install without scanning**. The app is not on the Play Store, so Play Protect does not know it.
3. Start the app once before the next step. The `Android/data/…/files/` folder will be created only after starting the application for the first tinme.
4. Copy your extracted disc (the folder with `default.xbe` in it) to the app's own folder:
   - DUB Edition: `Android/data/io.github.laureladastra.mcdub3/files/game/`
   - Remix: `Android/data/io.github.laureladastra.mcdub3remix/files/game/`

   The app finds it there by itself and needs no extra permission. On Android 11 and newer most file managers cannot open `Android/data`, so copy it from a computer over USB. Note that Android deletes this folder, saves included, when you uninstall the app.

   **Or keep the game elsewhere:** put it at the top of your internal storage or SD card (`/sdcard/mcdub3-nx/`)
    `sdcard/mcdub3-nx/` (Remix: `sdcard/mcdub3remix-nx/`)where it is found by itself. Alternatively you can pick any folder with **Add folder** on the start screen. Both need **All files access**, which the app asks for.
5. Optionally choose how the on-screen gamepad behaves: **Automatic** (hidden while a controller is connected), **Always**, or **Never**. Controllers (Bluetooth pads, Joy-Cons) and keyboards work without setup.
6. Press **Play** to start the game.

If the game doesn't start, the log is `mcdub3_log.txt` (Remix: `mcdub3remix_log.txt`) in the same app folder as in step 3, one level up from `game/`. Please attach it to a bug report.

> [!WARNING]
> **The most common mistakes are: copying the disc image (`.iso`) instead of its extracted files, or the wrong game's disc (the DUB Edition application with the Remix disc, or the other way round).** The app needs the folder of extracted files, with `default.xbe` in it. To unpack an `.iso`, use [xdvdfs](https://github.com/antangelo/xdvdfs): `xdvdfs unpack <your disc>.iso <folder>`. The wrong game's disc is refused with a message when you press **Play**.
>

## Medabots NX v0.2.0 - Dual Edition (Rokusho & Metabee)

This major release integrates full dual-version support into a single Nintendo Switch NRO binary, statically recompiled using [GBARecomp](https://github.com/Mr-Wiseguy/gbarecomp) and matching source decompilations ([medabots-rokusho](https://github.com/medabots-re/medabots) & [medabot-decomp](https://github.com/lucasderksen/medabot-decomp)).

### What's New:
* **Dual-Version Support**: Play either **Medabots: Rokusho Version** or **Medabots: Metabee Version** with automatic detection at boot.
* **Non-Colliding Dispatch Architecture**: Over 82,000 statically recompiled functions across both games co-exist seamlessly in one Switch NRO.
* **Independent Save Management**:
  * Rokusho saves to `sdmc:/switch/medabots_nx/save/rokusho.sav`
  * Metabee saves to `sdmc:/switch/medabots_nx/save/metabee.sav`
  * Existing `save/rom.sav` from v0.1.0 is automatically migrated to `save/rokusho.sav` on first launch with zero data loss.
* **Interactive Error Screen**: Clear guidance displaying supported SHA-1 hashes and ROM filenames if an incorrect file is provided.
* **Controls & Display**: Authentic integer-scaled 4:3 presentation, top-right live FPS pill counter (click R3 to toggle on/off), and simultaneous (+ and -) exit to hbmenu.

### Installation & SD Card Layout:
1. Extract `medabots-nx-v0.2.0.zip` into `/switch/` on your microSD card:
   ```
   /switch/medabots_nx/
    ├── medabots_nx.nro
    ├── config.txt
    ├── gba_bios.bin (your legally dumped GBA BIOS)
    ├── rokusho.gba  (optional: Medabots: Rokusho ROM)
    └── metabee.gba  (optional: Medabots: Metabee ROM)
   ```
2. Launch via Title Override (hold `R` while starting an installed game) for full RAM access.

*Legal Disclaimer: No copyrighted game ROMs or BIOS binaries are included.*

## Mercenaries 2: World in Flames — 0.2.0

### Русский

- Оптимизированы два CPU-помощника с проверкой эквивалентности при запуске и исходным fallback. В изолированном CPU-замере время снизилось на 20,7% и 28,6%; это не процент прироста FPS всей игры.
- Объединены улучшения загрузки данных рендера, ZCULL, ограниченные кеши изображений/материалов и повторное использование staging-памяти. Сборка PGO USE.
- Исправлено замедление камеры, движения и анимаций в проверенном помещении.
- Добавлены ожидание востребованных текстур и прогрев накопленных shader/pipeline-вариантов перед началом игры. Неизвестные варианты могут компилироваться при первом появлении; публичный архив не содержит игровой кеш.
- Обновлены четырёхъядерный форвардер и инструкции установки, обновления и сборки на русском и английском.

**Установка:** распакуйте ZIP в корень SD, добавьте данные собственной Xbox 360 копии в `SD:/switch/Mercenaries2/game_root/`, установите NSP через DBI и запускайте с HOME. Подробности и контрольная сумма исходного XEX — в README.

**Обновление:** закройте игру, сохраните копию `SD:/switch/Mercenaries2/mercenaries2/` и TOML, обновите NRO/конфиг/VERSION и форвардер. Сохранения и `game_root` не удаляйте.

**Известные ограничения:** при въезде в новые локации остаются возможны краткое мерцание зданий и просадки. Финальная проверка именно релизного NRO и нового форвардера на консоли ещё ожидается; сборка, целостность пакета и обратное чтение файлов с консоли проверены. Сравнение старого/нового релиза по ABBA не выполнено; гарантированный прирост FPS не заявляется.

Игровые данные, ключи, сохранения, кеши и сырые PGO-профили не распространяются.

### English

- Two native CPU helpers with startup equivalence checks and original fallback. Isolated CPU-workload time decreased by 20.7% and 28.6%; these are not whole-game FPS gains.
- Combined renderer upload/ZCULL improvements, bounded image/material caches, staging-memory reuse and PGO USE.
- Fixed slow camera, movement and animation in the tested interior.
- Referenced textures complete before drawing; recorded shader/pipeline variants warm up before gameplay. Unknown variants may still compile on first use. No game cache is included in the public ZIP.
- Updated four-core forwarder and Russian/English installation, update and build instructions.

**Install:** extract the ZIP to the SD root, supply your own Xbox 360 game data in `SD:/switch/Mercenaries2/game_root/`, install the NSP through DBI and launch from HOME. See README for details and the supported XEX checksum.

**Update:** close the game; back up `SD:/switch/Mercenaries2/mercenaries2/` and the TOML, then replace NRO/config/VERSION and update the forwarder. Preserve saves and `game_root`.

**Known limitations:** brief building flicker and frame drops may persist at new-area transitions. The final console smoke test of this exact release NRO/new forwarder is pending; build, package integrity and console readback checks passed. No old/new release ABBA comparison was completed, and no guaranteed whole-game FPS improvement is claimed.

No game data, keys, saves, caches or raw PGO profiles are distributed.

packages.changelog:
Reduces GPU work in MSAA passes, depth resolves and close-up grass while retaining 1280×720 and 4× MSAA. The final 1.0.8-rc.3 candidate was tested on Nintendo Switch; the stable NRO has identical executable code and changes only the displayed version. Gameplay profiling is disabled.

## GPU improvements

- Hardware 4× MSAA now covers smaller compatible passes: the minimum sample-space pitch drops from 640 to 160.
- Compatible depth resolves read the native MSAA image directly, avoiding an intermediate unpack.
- Render targets allocate the required rows and grow while preserving colour, depth and stencil, reducing oversized allocations and clear work.
- The grass shader removes redundant alpha-comparison branches and discards transparent pixels before colour/fog calculations. Grass density, alpha thresholds, fade, blending and depth/stencil behaviour are preserved.
- Retains the previous deferred/useful-area clears, compatible resolve/copy elimination, guarded early depth tests, unnecessary fragment-shader removal, and CPU PGO/LTO optimizations.

## Performance

| Gameplay on Nintendo Switch | CPU | GPU | `minininjas_fps_limit` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nearly stable 30 FPS | 1020 MHz | 307 MHz | `30` (default) |
| Stable 30 FPS | 1020 MHz | 460 MHz | `30` |
| 60 FPS target | 1785 MHz | 614 MHz | `0` (uncapped) |

The 30 FPS results were reported during testing of this release. The 60 FPS clock settings are unchanged. Set the clocks on the console; edit `minininjas.toml` beside the NRO and restart to change the frame limit.

## Updating

For an existing v1.0.3–v1.0.7 or v1.0.8 release-candidate installation, replace only `sdmc:/switch/mini-ninjas/mini-ninjas.nro`. Keep your game files, saves, configuration and shader cache. The runtime archive is unchanged from v1.0.7; the new grass shader creates its own cache entry when first used.

For a fresh installation, use the [browser installer](https://infriker.github.io/mini-ninjas-nx/) or follow the [manual setup](https://github.com/infriker/mini-ninjas-nx/blob/v1.0.8/docs/installing.md). Launch in title takeover mode, not Album/applet mode.

The grass optimization is enabled by default. For comparison, set `minininjas_foliage_fast_alpha = false` in `minininjas.toml` and restart; this leaves MSAA enabled.

Shader validation covered 54,848 discard/colour cases and all alpha-comparison variants. A saved grass-frame replay retained byte-identical colour and depth. See the updated [performance notes](https://github.com/infriker/mini-ninjas-nx/blob/v1.0.8/docs/performance.md) for conditions and validation.

Assets: `mini-ninjas.nro`, the matching `mini-ninjas-runtime.zip`, and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Original game assets are not included.

# v1.01.0 — for Mega Man X Regenesis 1.01.0

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This build only works with game version 1.01.0.** 1.01.0 ships a rebuilt engine binary, so older port releases will not start on it, and this one will not run correctly on an older game version. Use the `assets/` folder and the two `.so` files from the **1.01.0** APK.

## Updating from an earlier release

Unlike previous game updates, this time you have to replace **everything**:

| Replace | From |
| --- | --- |
| `mmxregenesis_nx.nro` | this release |
| `libgodot_android.so` | the 1.01.0 APK, `lib/arm64-v8a/` |
| `libc++_shared.so` | the 1.01.0 APK, `lib/arm64-v8a/` |
| `assets/` | the 1.01.0 APK |

**Keep your `save/` folder** — saves, touch settings and language carry over. Everything else regenerates by itself.

The first launch rebuilds the asset pack and takes about a minute longer than usual. That is normal and happens only once.

## The renderer changed: Vulkan → OpenGL ES 3

The 1.01.0 Android build ships a Godot engine compiled **without the Vulkan backend** — it is a GL Compatibility-only build, which is also why the engine binary is roughly half the size it used to be. That is how the game was built; it is not a choice this port made.

The wrapper detects this at boot and renders with GLES3 instead. There is nothing for you to configure, and `enable_vulkan` in `config.txt` has no effect on this game version.

**Performance may differ from the 1.00.92 release, in either direction.** This is a 2D game and GL Compatibility is the renderer Godot recommends for exactly that, but it is new ground for this port. If something runs noticeably worse than it used to, please say which level, and whether you were in handheld or docked. If you would rather stay on the Vulkan path for now, the previous release with game 1.00.92 still works.

## Port changes in this release

- Both engine patches re-derived for the new binary. They verify the instructions they expect before touching anything, so a mismatched game version skips them instead of corrupting the engine.
- Removed the save-file patch for touch transparency: 1.01.0 supports 0% by itself.
- Touch controls still start **off**, at 0% transparency, with the "TC" button hidden. Turn them on in Options → Controls → Touch Controls. Settings you already saved are kept.

## What to expect on Switch

- **Text looks flat**, without the beveled style of the PC/Android version. The game's text shader loops 16 times per glyph across 4 samplers, which this hardware does not handle well, so the port substitutes a simpler one.
- **Level ambient lighting is off.** The game's full-screen 2D light locks up the GPU on this console, so the wrapper disables it; levels look unlit compared to PC. Menu lights are unaffected.
- The **touchscreen** works as a single touch. The gyro is not used.
- In-game Video options: Renderer is hidden, V-Sync has no effect (FIFO only), Max FPS and the 4:3 toggle work, Fullscreen has no effect, and every screen filter costs GPU time — 1.01.0 adds four more, so leave it on None for the best framerate.
- Bugs that also happen on PC/Android cannot be fixed here; the game is closed-source.

## Requirements

Atmosphère, launched through a **forwarder** or a **title takeover** (hold **R** while starting an installed game). Album applet mode does not provide enough memory or the code-memory permissions. See the README for the full install layout and the recommended Sphaira forwarder settings.

## If it crashes

Send the newest file from `/atmosphere/crash_reports/` on your SD card, along with what you were doing and which game version you have.

---

Mega Man X Regenesis is a **free** fan game — get it from the developers' [itch.io page](https://mmxregenesis.itch.io/mega-man-x-regenesis). The game's own 1.01.0 changelog (Zero as a playable character, the PSX-style soundtracks, Arabic support and the rest) is theirs, not this port's.

# mp2-nx 0.5.0

A native Nintendo Switch port of **Metroid Prime 2: Echoes** (GameCube, USA). The game code comes from
[Echoes Unbound](https://github.com/Odrannnn/MetroidPrime2Port), built on the Echoes decompilation; mp2-nx adds
the Switch layer. Unofficial and fan-made. **No game files are included**; you need your own USA GameCube disc
(G2ME01).

## What's new since 0.1.0

- **A new renderer, deko3d**, which draws through the Switch's own graphics API, is now the default and the one
  this release was tested on. 0.1.0's Vulkan renderer stays available in System > Renderer (applies on the next
  start). If deko3d ever fails to show a picture on two starts in a row, the game switches itself to Vulkan and
  says so.
- **The map runs at 60 fps** (tested on deko3d). The map is now drawn on the GPU in one batch, instead of
  thousands of small draws.
- **Beam selection with twin stick aiming:** hold L and press the D-pad (up Power, right Dark, left Light, down
  Annihilator). The right stick only aims, so a hard turn no longer swaps beams. In morph ball, L also springs
  the ball when Spring Ball is on.
- **Faster start-up**, with a loading screen instead of a black screen.
- **New option:** Video > Map performance shows frame timings while the map is open (off by default).
- Precompiled shaders for deko3d are built into the NRO (no game assets), so areas draw smoothly the first time.

## Install

1. Extract `mp2-nx-v0.5.0-switch.zip` to the root of your SD card. It makes `switch/mp2-nx/`.
2. Copy your disc image (.iso, .gcm, .rvz, .wia, .gcz or .ciso) into `switch/mp2-nx/`.
3. Hold **R** while opening any game to get the homebrew menu with full memory, then start **mp2-nx**.

**Updating from 0.1.0:** replace `mp2-nx.nro`. Your saves and settings in `switch/mp2-nx/user/` are kept.

## Known issues

- Played from the start through Agon Wastes (up to the Dark Beam) so far.

## Reporting problems

Send `mp2-nx.err.log` and `mp2-nx.log` from `switch/mp2-nx/logs/` (and `crash.txt` if there is one).

## Source and licenses

Source: this repository. mp2-nx is MIT; the files from other projects keep their own licenses (MIT, MPL-2.0,
zlib, CC0), listed in the README.

# naruto-nx 0.1.5 (playable test build)

Nintendo Switch homebrew port of *Naruto: Rise of a Ninja* (Ubisoft Montreal, 2007, Xbox 360). Fan project, not affiliated with Ubisoft, Bandai Namco, Microsoft or Nintendo. The game's files are not included: you need your own copy of the game.

**Status: playable test build.** Measured on a Nintendo Switch in handheld mode on stock clocks (CPU 1020 MHz, GPU 460 MHz, RAM 1600 MHz) at native 720p.

## Performance Status

- **Open-world Konoha (Leaf Village, Story mode): 30 FPS reached in stationary vista on stock clocks (1020/460 MHz)** at native 720p (up from 25–28 FPS in 0.1.4 and ~20 FPS in 0.1.1/0.1.3). Measured median frame interval in pilot spot p50 = **33.39 ms** (target 33.33 ms). Dynamic movement routes across the full village remain under test.
- **CPU Allocator Bottleneck Eliminated:** Memory allocation overhead in `sub_82180568` (`MmAllocatePhysicalMemoryEx` / `AllocRange`) collapsed from **31.5% down to 1.6% of running samples** (a 95% reduction in allocator CPU time). `BaseHeap::AllocRange` completely vanished from the top-30 CPU profile.
- **Draw Calls & GPU Margin:** Modular static world culling distance tuned to 135m (`naruto_max_view_distance`), reducing draw calls from ~1,955 to ~1,518 (-437 draws/frame, -22%). Freed ~5.0 ms of CPU render thread time and ~4.1 ms of GPU time, eliminating GPU fillrate saturation.

## What is new in 0.1.5

- **64-bit Free-Page Bitmap (`heap_free_bitmap`):** Replaced the 131,072-entry linear page table scan in `BaseHeap::AllocRange` with an L1-resident 16 KB 64-bit bitmap (`free_bits_`). Page range search now scans 64 physical pages per clock cycle using hardware `__builtin_ctzll`.
- **Kernel Physical Memory Pool (`kernel_physical_pool`):** Implemented an in-memory pool (up to 16 MB) for unconstrained physical allocations. Frame-cyclic physical allocations are reused instantly without acquiring heap locks, scanning page tables, or issuing Horizon OS memory mapping syscalls.
- **Modular World Culling Tuning (`sub_820FD5F8`):** Fine-tuned static geometry culling threshold to 135.0m via `naruto_max_view_distance`, cutting off distant unseen meshes while maintaining full scene aesthetics and skydome integrity.
- **In-Game Diagnostic Overlay & Measurement Hotkey:** Added instant profiling trigger via gamepad shortcut **`L + R + Minus`** (or F8 / `M` on keyboard). Added a lightweight HUD indicator (`[● REC]`) during active measurement windows.
- **Automated Console Diagnostic Pipeline:** Added `tools/switch/ftp_run_summary.py` for automated compact Markdown report generation directly from console FTP sessions without keeping full logs in repository context.

## Installation

1. Open the web installer: **https://malinkin-s.github.io/naruto-nx-installer/**
2. Select `default.xex` and `xeshader.sdb` from your extracted game disc, and extract the resulting zip to the root of your SD card.
3. Copy your game files to `switch/naruto-nx/game/` (so that `switch/naruto-nx/game/default.xex` exists).
4. **Recommended: Make a HOME Menu forwarder via Sphaira** (CPU cores = 4, address space = 39-bit) for best audio stability and performance.
   *Or start the Homebrew Menu by holding **R** while starting any game (title override: full memory, three cores).*

---

packages.changelog:
Nexus Atmosphere 1.12.2 N4R2 includes Nexus Manager 0.2.24. Both packs keep the standard Hekate appearance and original Atmosphere splash, with Nexus USB support and the Nexus build version.

## Changes and fixes

- **Fixed the Silksong launch problem.** A game-data reading fault was corrected in the shared reader, so the fix also applies to other games using the same path. Silksong with its update now reaches gameplay in the reported test.
- **Safer USB installs.** Fixed a shutdown problem that could crash the system during an install from USB to USB.
- **More room for USB libraries.** The mapping limit is now 4,096 title records and 262,144 content-file entries, with lower memory use for large lists. This is a larger limit, not unlimited storage.
- **A recovery copy of your USB links.** Valid existing links are saved automatically inside the current console system, and later changes refresh that copy. Manager can preview restoring missing links if the SD-side mapping files are lost. This stores links only, not games, tickets or saved progress; each emuMMC/sysMMC has its own copy.
- **Clearer Manager repair.** Removed the repeated startup and Installed games warnings. Run USB library repair when you need it. Empty drives, old updates and missing ticket-backup files should no longer be mistaken for broken installed games.
- **Safer Cleanup.** Installed games are protected from cleanup based only on a ticket warning, and selections are checked again before removal. Manual game deletion remains available and keeps saved progress.
- **Simpler progress screens.** One overall bar, transfer speed, a larger game cover and bold title make installs, copies and moves easier to follow.
- **Better local XCI support.** Improved handling of trimmed files and split XCI sets. Keep all parts together on SD/USB and select the first part. This does not add cartridge mounting.
- Earlier USB sleep/wake recovery, SD/internal-storage destination fixes, cheat-service protections, port management and network/PC transfer features remain included.

## Which download do I need?

| Download | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Nexus-1.12.2-N4R2-Standard-No-HOC.zip** | Standard-looking Nexus USB pack without HOC clock controls. |
| **Nexus-1.12.2-N4R2-Standard-HOC.zip** | The same Nexus fixes with Nexus-compatible HOC 2.6.0 and its overlay. The existing pack profile is retained. |
| **Nexus-Manager-0.2.24-R1.zip** | Manager NSP and NRO for updating the app separately. |
| **Nexus-HATS-Installer-1.0.1.nsp / .zip** | Switch installer: NSP for HOME, ZIP for the homebrew menu. |
| **Nexus-HATS-Desktop.x64.exe** | Windows installer for downloading and applying a pack to your SD card. |
| **Nexus-HATS-Desktop-Universal.dmg** | Mac installer for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs on macOS 14 or later. |

Both firmware packs include Manager 0.2.24 NSP/NRO, the USB Content overlay with coloured notifications, sys-patch, Nintendo DNS rules and Hekate Launch entries. They use Atmosphere 1.12.2 for Switch firmware 23.5.0, official Hekate 6.5.5 and Nyx 1.9.5. The HATS installers remain version 1.0.1 and retain their USB-library protection rules.

## Updating

Choose one firmware pack. Fully shut down the Switch, extract it to the microSD root and replace matching pack files. Keep your Nintendo/emuMMC folders, games, saves, mods and USB mappings. Boot through **Hekate > Launch** using the included payload.

To update Manager on HOME, install **install/Nexus-Manager-0.2.24.nsp**. Copying the pack updates its NRO but does not install the NSP. Existing Manager users can also use the in-app update prompt.

Switching from HOC to No-HOC requires disabling the old HOC module's `atmosphere/contents/00FF0000636C6BFF/flags/boot2.flag`. An extracted ZIP cannot remove old modules or custom background files.

**Testing:** the no-HOC N4R2 firmware was tested with Silksong reaching gameplay, and Manager 0.2.24 was reported working. No new crash reports were found in that test. Both packs pass

packages.changelog:
**Vibration, all 11 languages readable, your game's icon on the Homebrew Menu and forwarders, and a fix for the docked map that stopped loading after a few events.**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own copy of *Need for Speed Most Wanted* for Android, version **1.3.128**: the APK and the OBB (or one `.xapk` file with both).
> Only the **Android** version works: not the PC, PS3, Xbox 360, PS Vita or Wii U versions.

## Which file do I download?

| File | For whom |
|---|---|
| ✅ **`NFSMostWanted2012-0.3.2.zip`** | **Everyone who wants to play.** The port, the player's guide and the optional PC script. It's the only file you need. |
| `NFSMostWanted2012-0.3.2-symbols.elf` | Developers only: it helps read crash reports. Not needed to play. |
| Source code (zip / tar.gz) | Added by GitHub to every release: the port's code, for developers. It has nothing to play with. |

## What's new in 0.3.2

- **Vibration** (on by default). Every crash gives a thump: light, medium or hard, matched against the game's own three crash levels, so a scrape is a tap and a head-on hit is a jolt. Nitro gives a steady buzz while the gauge goes down. Debug menu → CONTROLS & SOUND → *Vibration*: off, low, normal or strong. It stops in the HOME menu and while the debug menu is open.
- **All 11 languages are readable** ([#2](../../issues/2)). Russian, Japanese, Korean and Chinese text was blank: the game's font only has Latin letters, and on a phone Android fills in the rest. The port now takes the missing letters from the Switch's own system fonts.
- **Your game's icon and title** ([#3](../../issues/3)). At the first start, the port takes the icon out of your APK and puts it, with the title "NFS Most Wanted 2012", on the `.nro`. The Homebrew Menu shows it from then on, and so does a **forwarder made after that first start**. The released `.nro` still has the port's own icon: no EA artwork is shipped.
- **Docked map fix** ([#1](../../issues/1)). Docked, the map could stop loading after a few events, and entering an event then crashed. Docked, the game loads its menu and map texture packs at their biggest size, 58 to 67 MB each, two or three at a time, and frees them a moment later; they broke up the game's memory a little more on every visit to the map. Big blocks now get their own area of memory, as Android does it. Found on the PC test build at docked resolution, **not yet confirmed on a console**: if it still happens, please send `log.txt`, which now shows the game's memory every 10 seconds.
- **Texture filtering is now called Anisotropic filtering**, its usual name. Same options, same default (4x); your setting is kept.
- The port now frees the Java objects the game no longer uses (until now, none was ever freed).

## How to install

1. Download **`NFSMostWanted2012-0.3.2.zip`** below, under **Assets** (not "Source code"), and copy its `switch` folder to the root of your SD card.
2. Copy your APK and your OBB into `switch/NFSMostWanted2012/game/`, without unzipping or renaming them. A single `.xapk` file works too.
3. Hold **R** while launching any game, open **NFS Most Wanted 2012 Loader**, wait for the setup screen and press **A**.

## Updating from 0.3.1

Copy the new `switch` folder over the old one. Your game files, saves and settings are kept, and the old `.nro` is removed automatically the first time you start the new one. **If you use a forwarder, make it again after that first start:** the new `.nro` has a new name, and the game's icon and title go into it then.

## Known issues

- **Experimental:** back up your SD card and use emuMMC.
- **Tested on a Switch Lite:** the new languages and the game's icon and title work. **Vibration and the docked map fix are not yet tested on a console:** reports with `log.txt` are very welcome, also to say how the vibration feels on your controller.
- **Nitro vibration** could not be tried on the PC test build (the tutorial there blocks nitro);

# NFSMW-NX v1.0.0

First public release of NFSMW-NX: the native Nintendo Switch port of **Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005)** (Xbox 360).

## Update (September 29, 2026)

The NROs of this release were replaced with a new build. It's still version 1.0.0.

- **Dubbed videos:** videos re-encoded by fan translations such as the Brazilian Portuguese one no longer come out
  green or with glitches. They use B-frames and the in-loop deblocking filter which the game's own videos don't.
- **Color filter:** a new setting, `nfsmw_tratamiento_visual`, makes the game's yellow tint (its "visual treatment",
  which players call the "piss filter") softer (`suave`) or turns it off (`apagado`). The default, `original`, looks
  as on the Xbox 360. It can be changed while playing from the Debug Menu (L + R + D-Pad Right), category `Graficos`.
- **Installer page:** it recognizes the Brazilian Portuguese translation which uses the Spanish PAL executable. For an
  edition it doesn't support yet, it can create `nfsmw-nx-report.txt` to send us, even from `default.xex` alone.

To update, open the installer page again, choose your game and use **Create nfsmw-nx-update.zip**. It contains only
the NRO, `nfsmw.toml` and the shader library. Copy it over your folder on the SD card: your saves are kept and the
new `nfsmw.toml` replaces yours (if you had changed a setting in it, change it again).

## How to install

Use the installer page: **https://stevensnd.github.io/nfsmw-nx-installer/**

It reads your own copy of the game in the browser and builds a package ready to copy to the SD card. The NROs
attached to this release are what the page uses: on their own they do not run, because they need the game files and
the shader library that the page builds from your disc.

## Supported editions

One NRO per edition of the game (the installer picks the right one automatically):

| File | Edition |
|---|---|
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-es.nro` | PAL - Spanish & Brazilian Portuguese (Fan Version) |
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-en.nro` | PAL - English & Russian (Fan Version) |
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-fr.nro` | PAL - French |
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-de.nro` | PAL - German |
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-it.nro` | PAL - Italian |
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-pl.nro` | PAL - Polish (Fan Version) |
| `nfsmw-nx-usa.nro` | NTSC-U |
| `nfsmw-nx-jpn.nro` | NTSC-J |
| `nfsmw-nx-kor.nro` | NTSC-K - Korean |
| `nfsmw-nx-cht.nro` | NTSC - Asia, Traditional Chinese |

## Requirements

- A Nintendo Switch that can run homebrew.
- Start `nfsmw-nx.nro` from the Homebrew Menu in title takeover mode (launch a game while holding R), or through a
  39-bit forwarder made with [Sphaira](https://github.com/NaGaa95/sphaira)

## Controls

Each Switch button acts as the Xbox 360 button with the same letter: **A** accepts and **B** goes back, as in other
Switch games, also in the Debug Menu. To use the face buttons by position instead, as on an Xbox pad (B acts as A,
A as B, Y as X and X as Y), set `input_xbox_layout = true` in `nfsmw.toml`.

## Resolution

Automatic by default: **1280x720** in handheld mode and **1920x1080** docked, chosen when the game starts (after
docking or undocking, restart the game to switch). To use one resolution in both modes, set
`nfsmw_resolucion_interna` to `1280x720` or `1920x1080` in `nfsmw.toml`. If the frame rate is too low docked, use
`1280x720`.

## Notes

- The Debug Menu (L + R + Right) and the log files are in Spanish in this version.
- The first race after installing or updating compiles the graphics pipelines it has not seen yet, so it can stutter
  for a few seconds. They are saved on the SD card and later sessions start smoothly.
- Performance, overclocking and all the settings are explained in the README.
- Source code and documentation: this repository. The code of these NROs is the `main` branch as of September 29,
  2026. The licenses of the NRO and its libraries are in `LICENSE` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

Configure the Nintendo Switch daily play-time limit and manage parental controls offline — no phone app, no account, no internet (CFW required)

packages.changelog:
**v3.1.0 — play-timer fixes, bedtime alarm, launch PIN check.**

Fixes for every open issue, a bedtime alarm, and a PlayTimerSettings layout confirmed by reversing the fw 22.5.0 `pctl` sysmodule (see [`docs/pctl-reverse-engineering.md`](https://github.com/tailiang2008/NX-Pctl-Manager/blob/v3.1.0/docs/pctl-reverse-engineering.md)).

Many thanks to [@puppywang](https://github.com/puppywang), who contributed the fixes and features in this release ([#8](https://github.com/tailiang2008/NX-Pctl-Manager/pull/8)).

### Fixes

- **The limit now applies right after writing it (#3, #6, #7).** v3.0.0 unlocked parental controls temporarily (cmd 1201) and never re-locked them. Every write now ends with cmd 1007 RevertRestrictionTemporaryUnlocked. The "Turn off & write" prompt is gone.
- **The timer counts down on offline consoles (#2).** pctl only enables the timer when the NetworkSystemClock is valid, and a console that can't reach Nintendo never sets it. The app now detects this at launch and offers to set the network clock from the system clock. The main menu has the same option.
- **Error 0x1088E when writing (#5).** This is pctl's "no PIN registered" result. A PIN is now required before any play-timer write; without one, pctl silently discards the settings anyway.
- Removing the limit goes through the same guarded write. In v3.0.0, removing it while the "time's up" screen was up could crash Atmosphère.
- Per-day editor: a day can be set back to "no limit".
- Play-timer reads and writes are refused below fw 21.0.0, where the struct has a different size.
- Fixed a start-up crash on fw 22.x. borealis rejects the `multiline` Label attribute, and the uncaught exception left its task thread running after exit (2168-0001).

### New

- **Bedtime alarm (#4).** Set a start time and the next-morning end time, applied to every day. The app reads the values back through pctl's own getters to confirm the write.
- **When time is up:** suspend the software (default) or notify only.
- **Launch-time PIN check.** The tool can lift every restriction, so it now asks for the console's parental-control PIN first.
- **Diagnostic report.** A read-only dump of firmware, clocks, the raw and decoded settings, and the bedtime getters is saved to `sd:/switch/nx_pctl_dump.txt`.
- **Logs on the SD card.** Writes go to `sd:/switch/nx_pctl_manager.log` and borealis output to `sd:/switch/nx_pctl_borealis.log`.
- Simplified Chinese translation.
- The `PROBE` build option was removed. Its diagnostic dump is now always available.

Tested on fw 22.5.0 / Atmosphère 1.12.0 (emuMMC).

### Before you upgrade
- **Firmware 21.0.0 or newer** is required for the play-timer features.
- **A parental-control PIN is required** to write any play-time setting, and the app asks for it at launch. It can no longer be used to recover a forgotten PIN.
- **Offline consoles:** accept the prompt to set the network clock, or the timer won't count down.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/tailiang2008/NX-Pctl-Manager/blob/v3.1.0/CHANGELOG.md) for the full history.

### Install
Drop `nx_pctl_manager.nro` into `/switch/` on the SD card and launch it from hbmenu. Or download `nx_pctl_manager.zip` and unzip it onto the SD card root (it places the `.nro` into `/switch/` for you).

> **Beta**: tested on hardware and playable, but bugs may remain. Please report them in
> [Issues](https://github.com/denpingus/NXCloud/issues) with your `sdmc:/switch/nxcloud/log.txt` and `sdmc:/switch/nxcloud/stream.log`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Unofficial homebrew, not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft, Xbox or Nintendo. You need an account that can
> play on Xbox Cloud Gaming (Game Pass Ultimate, or games you own that support streaming).

First release of NXCloud: an Xbox Cloud Gaming client for the Nintendo Switch, with a launcher (**NXCloud**) and its own native player (**NXStream**).

## Install
1. Copy `nxcloud.nro` and `nxstream.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/nxcloud/`.
2. Open the Homebrew Menu in **title mode** (hold **R** while launching a game), not from the Album. You can also use Sphaira to create a shortcut forwarder.
3. Sign in with the code shown on screen at microsoft.com/link, pick a game and play.

## Launcher
- Your whole playable library: **Recent** like a console home (last played first, "Go back to" a game still running in the cloud), **Discover** (Game Pass lists), **All** with sort and genre filter, **Favorites** and search
- Game details with landscape art, the xCloud queue estimate and **achievements**
- **Friends** (presence, requests, add, mute, block, play together) and **messages**, with real-time updates and notifications
- Opens instantly and works offline: library, details and art are cached on the SD card
- English, Português (Brasil), Español; dark and light themes

## Player
- 720p or 1080p decoded by the Switch's hardware, **sound**, and low lag on real networks (lost packets asked for again, bitrate that follows the network; priority: low lag / balanced / picture)
- Controller as an Xbox pad, **HD Rumble**, **motion aiming** with the gyroscope
- **On-screen gamepad** for handheld play, with a layout editor (move, resize, toggle buttons, opacity)
- **Menu over the game** (+ and −): Xbox button, friends and messages, settings, and **back to NXCloud with the game still running**
- Bad-network icon and performance stats
- Playable without a controller: everything works by touch

[Source, screenshots and README](https://github.com/denpingus/NXCloud)

Miracles that look and sound like the original's, its loading screen, and a touch camera that works like the original's hand.

### What's new

- **Miracle effects from the original's own files.** Miracles are now drawn and sounded by a port of the original's particle-system engine, running the effect files from your Black & White install. Food and wood pour from the hand grain by grain, and each grain adds what it did in the original.
- **Miracle seeds:** tapping one pops its bubble with the original's sound and starts its in-hand effect.
- **The loading screen:** a tip of the day with its picture and words, over the original's sweeping bar.
- **Control pictures in subtitles:** where the original shows a mouse button or key, you see the Switch control on a key cap.
- **Touch camera:** hold at a side of the screen to turn, at the top or bottom to tilt, and pinch to zoom.

3. Launch with full memory: hold **R** while starting any game to open the Homebrew Menu, then choose openblack.

Only Land 1 for now; miracles are cast from seeds, not gestures; water and heal miracles don't have their full effects yet (no rain cone); villagers don't react to miracles yet; camera shake and the intro's clouds and boat aren't drawn yet; saving uses two save points on the D-pad.

packages.changelog:
First public release of **openPREY**, a homebrew port of Prey (2006) for the Nintendo Switch, built on [OpenPrey](https://github.com/themuffinator/OpenPrey).

> **You need your own copy of Prey (2006) for PC.** No game data is included.

## Installation

1. Extract `openPREY-switch-0.1.0.zip` to the **root of the SD card**. This creates `switch/openprey/`.
2. Copy **every `.pk4` file** from the `base` folder of your Prey installation into `switch/openprey/base/`.
3. Hold **R** while starting any installed game (title override) and pick **openPREY** in the Homebrew Menu. It does not run from the Album.

The first visit to each map takes a few minutes while its texture cache is built; later loads are much faster. Full instructions, controls and tips are in the [README](https://github.com/hazevauks/openPREYswitch#readme).

## Highlights

- Prey's single-player campaign from your own PC files, with saving and loading.
- A 30 fps frame lock and dynamic resolution, up to 1280×720.
- Controls in the style of modern console shooters, optional gyro aiming, touch in menus and the system keyboard.
- A settings menu on the **−** button: FPS counter, frame lock, shadows, dynamic resolution, GPU clock profile, gyro, look speed, subtitles and noclip.
- Prey's own collision and monster navigation (AAS) data, loaded as shipped.
- Logs, crash reports and death reports on the SD card, ready for bug reports.

## Tested

Played on hardware from the start of the campaign, through the Land of the Ancients, up to the Leech Gun in the feeding tower, mostly in handheld mode with the CPU at 1224 MHz. With shadows off, the opening maps hold 30 fps, dipping to about 25 in the busiest moments. Later chapters have not been tested yet.

## Known issues

- **No Deathwalk.** When Tommy dies he does not go to the Deathwalk; the game continues from the last save.
- **Long first loads** of each map while its texture cache is built.
- **Some busy areas drop below 30 fps.** Performance is the focus of the next updates.
- **`vid_restart` leaves the screen black.** Restart the game instead.
- **No multiplayer.** Docked mode has had less testing than handheld.

## Reporting bugs

Open an [issue](https://github.com/hazevauks/openPREYswitch/issues) with `switch/openprey/basepr/logs/openprey.log` (plus `openprey-previous.log` and `switch/openprey/openprey_crash.txt` when they exist), and say where in the game it happened.

## Oracles NX 1.0

First release of Oracles NX, a native Nintendo Switch port of **Oracle of Ages** and **Oracle of Seasons**, built on [oracles-decomp](https://github.com/kirby-letsgo/oracles-decomp) by kirby-letsgo.

The games run as native C code: no CPU emulator and no ROM code.

### Features
- Both games in one app, with a launcher showing each game's save files
- Save states (4 slots with thumbnails) and a Resume state on quit
- Screen filters (sharp, scanlines, LCD grid, CRT) and widescreen 16:9 mode
- Fully remappable controls and fast-forward (hold ZR)
- Full screen in handheld (720p) and docked (1080p)

### Installation
1. Copy `oracles.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/oracles/`
2. Copy your own **USA / Australia** ROMs (`.gbc`, `.zip` or `.gz`) to `sdmc:/switch/oracles/roms/`
3. Launch Oracles NX from the Homebrew Menu. The ROMs are installed on first launch.

Only the USA / Australia versions are supported (checked by SHA1). See the README for the hashes.

### Default controls
A / B: A / B · +: Start · −: Select · R: pause menu · ZR (hold): fast-forward

> **No game files are included.** You need your own ROMs. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo or Capcom.

### Credits
All the real work on the game reimplementation is by **kirby-letsgo** ([oracles-decomp](https://github.com/kirby-letsgo/oracles-decomp)), based on the [oracles-disasm](https://github.com/Drenn1/oracles-disasm) community disassembly. Switch port by **Toniisound**.

packages.changelog:
From now on releases are numbered. This one is a big update.

**New**
- **Zoom and look around** in the DS and GBA games (beta): a click of the right stick zooms out, the right stick looks around.
- **FullDex Nav** in the GBA games too: the watch with Fly, Party, Open PC, Repel, Encounters, Reset, Map, Pokédex and Bag. On phones it's smaller and sits at the right; a NAV button opens it. **NAV STYLE: OFF** (Display) gives the left stick back its old job (#181).
- **Fly from the menu** in the DS games, a **fuller Pokédex** read from your own game, and a **Companion for the GBA games** (Party, Bag, Location, Battle Info, Guide), with Gameplay options, Day and Night, and Following Pokémon.
- **Steam shortcuts**: ADD TO STEAM in a game's menu, STEAM LAUNCHER in Settings, Shortcuts (thanks OzWookiee, #197). A game started from a shortcut now closes back to Steam when you quit (#196).
- **Repel from the Nav** in Black 2 and White 2.
- **Widescreen for Generation 3 Evolved v1.0.22** (thanks Saiborg23, #184).
- **RecompLauncher**: install and update FullDex from RecompLauncher (thanks elripalda, #182).
- **Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire**: their saves in Manage Saves and cloud saves; a 3DS dump opened with FullDex opens the 3DS game; the 3DS programs updated.

**Fixed**
- **The Hub showed old boxes, party and Pokédex** after the 15 November update (the new folders), and cloud sync used the wrong save. Fixed, with safer cloud syncing (thanks OzWookiee, #186 to #190, #192).
- **Pokémon moved or swapped with the Hub now count in the Pokédex** (#185).
- **The 3DS games no longer open as DS games** (green bars); a 3DS file that isn't listed says why (#155).
- **Smoother first start of Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire**: preparing the game now builds the widescreen shaders too, so they are no longer built while you play.
- **60 fps on a Steam Deck docked at 120 Hz** (#173), and more.

The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/mamesj/pokemon-fulldex/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

packages.changelog: # SwitchU v1.4.1 ## Stability, Compatibility & Quality-of-Life Improvements A polish and maintenance release following v1.4.0, with improvements to HOME stability, docked display scaling, controller support, SteamGridDB artwork, music playback, clock synchronization, localization, and more. --- ## 🗞 What's New & Fixed ### HOME Stability & Performance - **HOME Reliability & Art Cache** - Fixed HOME becoming unresponsive after a missed foreground transition. Improved folder and app reordering, reduced artwork cache rebuilds and browsing hitches, and optimized HOME artwork handling while Frame Tap is active. - **Music Resume** - Added **Resume music on return home** setting under Theme Shop → Sounds (enabled by default). When disabled tracks restart from the beginning on return to home. Resume improved by seeking off the UI thread in the background to keep HOME responsive. - **Leave Splash** - Suspended games always show the original HOME screenshot captured at launch instead of recapturing the screen on every resume. This keeps the return splash consistent with the original launch view, even if you navigate to another page or close a folder before resuming. ### Display & Artwork - **Live Dock / Undock Resizing** - Fixed the HOME menu retaining incorrect dimensions when docking or undocking while open. The managed display layer now correctly adjusts to handheld and TV resolutions, including display setting changes. - **SteamGridDB Hero Quality & Blur** - Added configurable hero backdrop quality (Off, Low, Medium, High) and adjustable blur (0–100%). Quality options control artwork resolution: - High: Native 1280px artwork - Medium: 640px artwork, upscaled 2× (default) - Low: 320px artwork, upscaled 4× - Off: Disables new hero downloads and backdrop rendering. Existing artwork remains on disk. - **High-Resolution Grid Posters** - Improved poster quality in 2×3 and legacy 1×2 grid layouts by using the dedicated high-resolution artwork pipeline, matching the sharper results already available in other layouts. ### Battery & Controller Status - **Battery Synchronization & Controller Indicators** - Fixed console battery status becoming stale after boot with a lightweight 30-second daemon PSM heartbeat, keeping HOME, Quick Settings, and the Batteries widget in sync. - Restored individual battery rings for Joy-Con L/R and Pro Controllers using an 8-second HID poll, including programmed controller body colors when reported by HID. - Improved docked controller detection, retaining last-known shell colors when handheld mode is unavailable and prioritizing Joy-Con rings over Pro Controllers when space is limited. - Refreshed widget graphics with more accurate Joy-Con proportions, tablet and rail assemblies, and a Pro Controller silhouette. Also removed the redundant charging bolt from the console battery ring. ### Controllers & Input - **Atmosphère Title Override Shortcut** - Fixed holding R + A being intercepted by HOME's button-chord handling. You can now launch the Atmosphère title override (full-RAM hbmenu) while holding R. Ultrahand's L + R + A shortcut still cancels as expected so it doesn't unintentionally trigger HOME sorting or Quick Settings. - **Sideways Single Joy-Con Support** - Fixed menu navigation when using a single Joy-Con held sideways. Button mappings and stick directions now correctly match the controller's orientation. - **GameCube & SystemExt Controller Support** - Added HOME navigation support for GameCube controllers and SystemE

# PPSSPP Switch Version 0.6.5

Nintendo Switch community release based on PPSSPP v1.20.4.

## Highlights

- Added hardware-tested ARM64 JIT cache-pointer preservation fixes.
- Corrected the tested ARM64 IR/JIT cache-pointer crash path.
- Added parallel software depth rasterization using safe, non-overlapping worker tiles.
- Added Nintendo Switch process-core detection for worker scheduling.
- Corrected affected texture and CLUT memory reads.
- Fixed video swizzle-buffer initialization and ownership.
- Corrected negative render-target offsets in the OpenGL ES path.
- Fixed SDL trigger mapping and right-stick diagonal threshold behavior.
- Improved native Switch keyboard and multilingual input support.
- Added fallback fonts for CJK, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Lao.
- Retains the validated FFmpeg 57 video and 48 kHz audio fixes from Version 0.6.0.

## Installation

1. Download `PPSSPP-Switch-0.6.5.zip`.
2. Extract the ZIP to the root of the Nintendo Switch SD card.
3. Confirm that the application is installed at:

   `SD:/switch/ppsspp/PPSSPP.nro`

4. Fully close and reopen the Homebrew Menu after replacing an older version so its icon and metadata refresh.

## Recommended Configuration

- CPU core: JIT
- Graphics backend: OpenGL ES

Version 0.6.5 includes the tested ARM64 IR/JIT correction, but regular JIT remains recommended for the widest compatibility. Vulkan is not supported.

## Package Identity

- Application: PPSSPP
- Author metadata: PPSSPP Team
- Version: 0.6.5
- Runtime directory: `/switch/ppsspp/`
- ZIP SHA-256: `78ae639f28e371260f52dccb05dfd820bc81c8086457a251674e0185922c6297`

## Русский

- Исправлено слишком яркое белое небо и пересвеченные асфальт и здания в солнечные дни (например, в миссии «Идите к координатам последнего места, где видели доктора Гутьерреса»). Автоэкспозиция игры теперь получает правильную яркость кадра.
- Выше производительность: средняя частота кадров в игре примерно 26–27 вместо 24–25, длинные подвисания реже, тяжёлые моменты в бою ровнее. Свой микшер звука, декодер XMA без пересоздания на каждый звук, нативное копирование памяти, облегчён поток перевода команд GPU, из релиза убраны остатки диагностики, профили PGO сняты заново (теперь и для библиотек SDK).

Скачайте `Prototype2-NX.zip` и распакуйте в корень SD, свою копию игры положите в `switch/Prototype2/game_root/`. Для запуска с HOME установите `Prototype2-forwarder.nsp`. Обновление с 0.4.0: замените в `SD:/switch/Prototype2/` файлы `prototype2.nro`, `prototype2.toml` и `VERSION`, установите новый NSP поверх старого. `game_root` и сохранения не трогайте, свои настройки перенесите в новый TOML вручную.

## English

- Fixed the overly bright white sky and over-exposed asphalt and buildings on sunny days (for example in the mission to go to Dr. Gutierrez's last known location). The game's auto exposure now gets the correct frame brightness.
- Better performance: the average frame rate in play is about 26–27 instead of 24–25, long hitches are rarer and heavy combat moments are smoother. A native sound mixer, an XMA decoder that is not recreated for every sound, a native memory copy, a lighter GPU command thread, leftover diagnostics removed from the release, and retrained PGO profiles (now covering the SDK libraries too).

Download `Prototype2-NX.zip` and extract it to the SD root; add your own game copy to `switch/Prototype2/game_root/`. Install `Prototype2-forwarder.nsp` for HOME launch. Updating from 0.4.0: replace `prototype2.nro`, `prototype2.toml` and `VERSION` in `SD:/switch/Prototype2/`, then install the new NSP over the old one. Keep `game_root` and your saves; move your own settings into the new TOML by hand.

RaceWave46 RC7 retains the **X112 rendering baseline used by RC6** and adds Nintendo Switch Online N64 controller improvements.

## Changelog

- **N64 controller rumble:** added the controller's native on/off motor support, with rumble following the game's pulses and no lingering vibration from an extra decay envelope.
- **N64 menu shortcut:** **L + R + Start** opens or closes settings, providing an alternative to the Minus button.
- **Controller priority:** an external player-one controller takes priority over attached Joy-Cons for input and rumble. Disconnecting it restores the attached Joy-Cons.

## Downloads and installation

- **RaceWave46-Switch-RC7-release.zip:** complete release package with the NRO, installation instructions and the same Nano Banana 2 v2 HD texture pack by elliotttate included with RC6. Extract to the root of your SD card.

packages.changelog:
## re:Blue for Switch 1.3.6

GPU and animation performance update.

### Performance
- **Faster vertex shaders** (built at compile time, same results):
  - each pipeline's vertex layout flags are written into its shader instead of being read for every vertex;
  - runs of predicated code on the same condition are merged into one branch (fewer branches and joins per vertex and pixel; −8 % shader code overall);
  - skinning's bone-matrix reads no longer do a per-read range check.
- **Animation:** the native animation key search now actually runs on the Switch build (it was bypassed), and `bdSinCos`'s entry is cheaper.
- **Fresh PGO profile** for the current code.

Measured on the base route at stock clocks (handheld, 960×540):

| | 1.3.5 | 1.3.6 |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| Castle town main street, busiest windows | 16–18 FPS | 19–23 FPS |
| Frames slower than 50 ms, whole route | 821 | 359 |
| Other areas | — | the same or slightly better |

### Fixes
- `switch_system_core_mixer` is now ignored (with a note in `stderr.log`). Moving a game sound thread to the system core could freeze the whole console at a save point or a warp. Delete the line from your `reblue.toml` if you added it.

### Note
- **First start after updating:** the vertex shaders are recompiled on the console once, so the first area load can freeze for a few seconds. They are kept in the shader cache; later starts are normal.

### Known issues
- The castle town's main street is still below 30 FPS: the GPU and the CPU (character animation) now limit it about equally.
- `bd_switch_dynamic_resolution` stays experimental and off by default.

### Building
Tag `v1.3.6`: `run-switch-build.bat -Pgo use -Lto -InPlace` (see `docs/SWITCH.md` and `docs/INSTALL-SWITCH.md`).

Ridge Racer 6 on the Nintendo Switch (homebrew). You need your own copy of the game.
Thanks to Ridge Racer 6 Recomp by Sirhalo23 for its codegen work and notes on this game, and to masterspike52's reNut, whose renderer this port draws with.

## Install or update

Use the **[web installer](https://chanseyisthebest.github.io/rr6-nx-installer/)**. It makes the whole package from your own disc (and any DLC packages) in your browser, and nothing is uploaded. It gives you this NRO too.

**Updating from 1.0.0: make a new package with the installer.** 1.0.1 packs more of the game files, and this NRO reads them. Delete your old `switch/rr6-nx/game_root` folder first (1.0.0's unpacked videos and music left there would be read instead of the packed ones), then extract the new `rr6-nx.zip` to the root of the SD card. Your saves are not in `game_root` and stay; the zip's `config.toml` replaces yours, so note any settings you changed first.

New install: extract `rr6-nx.zip` to the root of the SD card, then in **Sphaira** find Ridge Racer 6, press **X**, choose **Install Forwarder**, set **Address Space** to **39-bit**, choose **Create Forwarder**, and start the game from the Home Screen.

## What's new in 1.0.1

- **Smaller on the SD card:** every game file is packed now, not only the three RRM archives. The archives use LZ4, and the videos, music and sounds use ZXC, which packs them smaller. About 5.4 GB in all, 800 MB less than the disc's files and about 190 MB less than 1.0.0.
- **Quicker loading:** the archives are decoded with LZ4's own decoder, 2.5 times as fast as 1.0.0's on the console.
- Two renderer fixes from the shared base: a texture slot keeps its last texture only while it still describes the same data, and a guard against a GPU hang seen in another port with dynamic resolution.
- Built with link-time optimisation and a profile (PGO) collected from a play session on a Switch.

Bug reports: add `log_level = "info"` at the top of `switch/rr6-nx/config.toml`, play until the problem happens, and include the `switch/rr6-nx/logs/` folder.

packages.changelog:
Silent Hill 2 (Director's Cut / Restless Dreams) on the Switch: the PC game's executable recompiled to native ARM64, no emulator, with support for the Silent Hill 2: Enhanced Edition packs.

**What's changed in v1.03**

Fixes by [Ligux01](https://github.com/Ligux01):

- **Eddie's room**: no more crash when entering the room with Eddie (#19).
- **Opening bathroom cutscene**: no more black area when the handheld render size is lowered (#18).
- **No controller connected**: James no longer walks forward and menus no longer scroll by themselves (#20, mainly Linux).

**Features**

- **Native code**: every function of `sh2pc.exe` runs as ARM64 code; no emulator, no Wine.
- **Launcher**: Play and Options before the game; Options changes the main `sh2e.ini` settings on the console.
- **Widescreen**: 16:9, drawn at 720p handheld and 1080p docked, or the original 4:3 (ThirteenAG's WidescreenFix, ported).
- **Enhanced Edition packs**: HD textures and maps, the EE title and save screens, the restored music, voices and sound effects, EE menus and fonts, and the FMV pack's 1080p60 movies with their subtitles (`movie=1`).
- **Enhanced Edition fixes**: search camera on the right stick, movement on the d-pad, pause menu fix, vibration fixes.
- **Controller**: SH2EE's button layout with Nintendo's A/B, HD rumble following the in-game Vibration option.
- **Saving and loading**, movies with synced audio, every menu.
- **Shader cache**: shaders are compiled once and kept on the SD card, so areas only stutter the first time.
- Also builds for Linux (x86-64), which is where most of the debugging happens.

**Install**

1. On your PC, install Silent Hill 2 and run the Enhanced Edition setup with at least the Enhanced Executable, Essential Files, Image Enhancement Pack and Audio Enhancement Pack (plus the FMV Enhancement Pack for the HD movies). The port is built for that `sh2pc.exe` (5,685,248 bytes, SHA-1 `3201a5e1029f3ae3b77770255dcbe10360b3cd09`).
2. Put `sh2-nx.nro` in `/switch/sh2-nx/` on the SD card, together with `sh2pc.exe`, `data/` and `sh2e/` from your PC install, and an `sh2e.ini` ([example](https://github.com/cutarev/sh2-nx/blob/main/docs/sh2e.ini.example)). Updating from an older version: replace the NRO.
3. Launch it from the homebrew menu in title takeover mode (hold R while starting an installed game), not from the album.

Full instructions, controls and settings: see the [README](https://github.com/cutarev/sh2-nx#how-to-install). No game files are included.

### Changelog

* Added Start+R as an alternative way to open the overlay on controllers without a Back/Minus button (e.g. N64 controllers); pressing R alone closes it again (by @RandomTask-1)
* Fixed a pause menu crash caused by an uninitialized `nameSegment` (by @sedrecur)


> [!NOTE]
> A breaking change was introduced in version 9.3.0!
>
> The game now uses the proper Switch controller layout instead of the default Xbox layout in SDL, swapping A<>B and X<>Y. If you have previously used custom keybindings to workaround this issue, you need to remove them. 


**Known issues:** 
* The CPU performance mode is not correctly re-applied after waking the console from sleep while the game was running. You might notice performance issues and stuttering after doing so.
As a workaround, enter and exit the home menu to re-apply the overclocking parameters properly. Or use [sys-clk](https://github.com/retronx-team/sys-clk), it also supports RAM and GPU overclocking.
_______

### Usage

* See [README](https://github.com/timschneeb/Shipwright-Switch#nintendo-switch) for installation instructions. You need to generate the `oot.o2r` or `oot-mq.o2r` asset package on a computer with SoH version 9.0.0 or later.
* Press - to open the overlay, or hold Start and press R on controllers without a Minus button.
* Physical keyboard and mouse are supported (though the mouse cursor is invisible)
	* Press Esc to open the overlay with a keyboard.
	
### FAQ

<details>
  <summary>
    How to setup gyro controls for aiming (click to expand)
  </summary>
  
Gyro controls are disabled by default. To enable them: 

* Open 'Controls' and expand the 'Gyro' section
* Tap the plus button and then press any button on your joycon to register it

</details>

packages.changelog:
# Silent Hill: Downpour 0.3.0

## Главное

- **Чёткие субтитры и UI.** После первого glyph-вызова кадра текстовая цель Scaleform `1040`-pitch и `1280`-pitch композиция переключаются на guest-native образы с сохранением содержимого через blit. При 3D `720x405` область текста переходит примерно с `576x405` на `1024x720`; весь 3D-рендер в 720p не переводится.
- **Новый рекомендуемый режим: `720x405` + FSR 1.** Добавлены промежуточные значения с шагом 80 пикселей: `800x450`, `880x495`, `960x540`, `1040x585`, `1120x630`. Режимы `640x360` и `1280x720` сохранены.
- **Экран настроек:** разрешение и пункт «Качество субтитров». Рекомендуется `720x405` и `чёткие / high`; обычный режим субтитров можно выбрать для меньшей нагрузки.
- **Чистый релизный TOML:** диагностика, capture и trace выключены, журнал пишет только предупреждения.

## Установка / обновление

1. Скопируйте папку `switch/` из архива в корень SD-карты.
2. Установите NSP из `nsp/` через DBI.
3. Запустите игру с HOME. В первые 5 секунд **+** открывает настройки; рекомендуемые значения отмечены на экране.

Игровых файлов в архиве нет: нужна своя копия Xbox 360-версии с проверенным `default.xex` (SHA-256 `c686cbff8facad6fb6b78ed98e5a5a2f4f19337ef83517f56195a56b0db2c8d7`). Библиотека шейдеров для рендера `p2` не нужна. Скомпилированный driver cache и prewarm не распространяются; они создаются локально.

## Проверка

Пользователь подтвердил на Switch Lite (Mariko, Horizon OC CPU 1963 / GPU 1152 / RAM 2333 МГц) чистую пару NRO+TOML, установку NSP, экран настроек, чёткость субтитров и игровую работу. Полное прохождение игры по-прежнему не заявляется.

Контрольные суммы всех файлов находятся в `SHA256SUMS.txt` внутри архива.

packages.changelog:
Build 143: Faster map sharing, custom Xbox maps and moving game files!

### Map sharing

- New: between two SlipstreamCE machines, maps go over a fast encrypted connection of their own instead of the game's tunnel, for both MCC packages and Custom Edition maps. A joiner opens up to 16 connections to the host (4 on the Switch), all through one port, which the host forwards with UPnP; a host serves 32 in all. Over the internet a joiner connects straight to the host's address when it can. A Custom Edition map still comes from the other players too, with the host as one more source. OpenCE hosts and joiners work as before. (thelinkin3000)
- Uploads use the whole line outside a game. During a game they leave room for the game's own traffic and slow down only when the players' pings show the line filling up. (thelinkin3000)
- The upload limits in Network Setup and Server Setup go up to 250 MB/s. (thelinkin3000)
- A download's speed is shown correctly past 2 MB/s. (thelinkin3000)
- Fixed: a download stuck at 0 KB/s when the host offered the map as the player joined. (thelinkin3000)
- Fixed: the Switch froze for 20 to 30 seconds while downloading a map and was dropped from the game. Downloaded pieces are now written to the SD card on a thread of their own. (thelinkin3000)

### Custom Xbox multiplayer maps

- New: Xbox multiplayer maps (from mods such as Halo CE+ X) can go in custom_maps. They're listed, described as "Custom Xbox multiplayer map", shared, and played like the game's own maps, even when they have the same names as the stock ones. (thelinkin3000)
- A dedicated server's rotation takes them. An Xbox campaign map is still refused, with a message saying why. (thelinkin3000)
- A game on one of these maps needs a client that supports them. A player whose client doesn't is told "You need a client with support for custom OG Xbox multiplayer maps." and removed. (thelinkin3000)

### Game files (Android)

- New: Settings > Gameplay > GAME FILES moves your maps, custom maps, mods and MCC maps to another place: APP DATA (the app's storage) or OTHER FOLDER (any folder you choose, such as one on a memory card). The game restarts to move them and shows its progress, then says where they are. A move that stops loses nothing: try again, or move them back. (thelinkin3000)

### Hosted servers

- Watching a player through their eyes from the host's screen now turns smoothly, as a replay does, instead of jumping each time their input arrives. (thelinkin3000)

### Custom campaigns (experimental)

- New: play an Xbox or Custom Edition campaign from its own folder in custom_campaigns, alone or in split screen. Its maps are found by the names inside them, so nothing needs renaming, and a campaign never mixes with the stock maps or with another campaign. A campaign with its own ui.map uses it as the main menu, with a BACK TO HALO button added. Each campaign has its own saved game. For now a campaign is chosen in config.toml (`[debug] custom_campaign = "<folder>"`); a menu for it comes later. (thelinkin3000)
- The unpacked map cache is now kept in memory on Android and the PS5, as it already was on the Switch, and it's emptied whenever the maps change under the same names. The old cache files on disk (about 730 MB) are deleted once. (thelinkin3000)

### Steam Workshop and MCC

- A joiner's Workshop download shows its progress and speed, says it's from the Workshop, and moves to another content server sooner when one refuses. (thelinkin3000)
- Fixed: a joiner was asked to download from the host a package Steam had already installed. (thelinkin3000)
- The Workshop screen's NEXT and PREVIOUS PAGE select the new page's first item, an installed item asks DOWNLOAD AGAIN? before downloading it again, and the rows' names are wider with shorter messages. (thelinkin3000)
- A hosted server identifies an MCC package's Workshop item from its ModInfo.json when it has no download record. (thelinkin3000)
- Security fixes from a review of the Steam client: a malform
