**Songate 2.0** is here: the music player that began as Gatefold NX, now on the Nintendo Switch, Windows and Android. Automix, your own music server, your devices playing together, lyrics found and searched, and everything else since 1.1.0.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3b6d4ad-07db-4a47-a4db-08c79869ab03


**On the Switch, tests were only made on HOS 22.5.0 and 23.0.0, with the latest HATS pack from sthetix.** **On Windows, tests were only made on Windows 11.** **On Android, tests were only made on a Xiaomi 11 Lite 5G with Android 15; Android 10 or newer is needed.****Only MP3, M4A and FLAC are supported;** other formats are untested.

## 🎮 Install or update on the Switch

**From 2.0.0 BETA 1 or BETA 2:** Settings › Updates installs it, your settings backed up first. Then **restart the console**, so the new background player starts.

**By hand, or from Gatefold NX 1.x:**

1. Download **SongateNX-2.0.0.zip** below and unzip it onto the root of the SD card, replacing the old files.
2. **Restart the console.** Songate, the background player and the overlay must all be this version: all three files go on the card together.
3. Launch Songate by **holding R while starting a game** (applet mode, from the Album, has too little memory).

| In the zip | What |
|---|---|
| `switch/Songate/Songate.nro` | 🎵 the app |
| `atmosphere/contents/4200000047464E58/` | 🎧 the background player (sysmodule, starts at boot) |
| `switch/.overlays/Songate.ovl` | 🧩 the Ultrahand overlay |

🙈 **Can't find the overlay?** `switch/.overlays` is a hidden folder (its name starts with a dot): macOS and many phone file and zip apps hide it, and some leave it out when copying. Copy the whole `switch` and `atmosphere` folders from the zip, and on a Mac press ⌘ ⇧ . in Finder to see hidden folders. The overlay needs **Ultrahand**.

**Coming from Gatefold NX 1.x?** At its first start Songate moves your settings, playlists, Liked and edits from `sdmc:/config/gatefold-nx/` to `sdmc:/config/songate-nx/`. Nothing is lost.

## 💻 Install or update on Windows

**From a beta:** Settings › Updates installs it.

**Or by hand:** download **SongateWIN-2.0.0.exe** below and run it. It needs no administrator rights. Your settings stay in `%APPDATA%\Songate`.

🛡️ **"Windows protected your PC"?** The installer isn't signed, so Windows doesn't know it yet. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. To check the file first, compare its SHA-256 with the one at the bottom of this page.

## 📱 Install on Android

> [!NOTE]
> **The Android version is still very early**, above all its upright (portrait) layout. Future updates will bring it many quality-of-life improvements.

Download **SongateAND-2.0.0.apk** below and open it. Android asks once to allow your browser or file app to install apps. Songate needs Android 10 or newer, and asks for access to your music at its first start. Later versions install from Settings › Updates.

## ✨ Songate 2.0

- ✨ Gatefold NX is now Songate, on the Switch, on Windows and on Android, with everything below since 1.1.0
- 🎚️ Automix: playlists that play like a DJ set, in the app and in the background player
- 🌐 Your own music server: Navidrome, Airsonic or any Subsonic server, beside your local library
- 🔗 Your devices, together: sync, Listen together and Handoff between a Switch, a PC and an Android phone
- 🎤 Lyrics found online for a song with none, and search by the words of your songs
- 🎭 Mood playlists: your library sorted by how it sounds, in nine moods

## 🎚️ Automix and moods

- 🎚️ Automix playlists: Songate listens to each song once, puts them in the order where they join best, and blends each into the next on the drop, on the beat, through a bridge or by a fade
- ✨ The join on screen: the cover glides to the middle and frosts over with Automix's hint. Settings › Appearance › Automix chooses how it shows, on Now playing and on the Canvas

# Sonic Advance 2 NX v0.3

This update adds an optional retry shortcut to normal stages and Special Stages.

## What's new

- Added a retry option after completing a normal stage.
- Added retry support on the Game Over and Time Over screens.
- Added retry support after both successful and failed Special Stages.
- Added an on-screen retry prompt using X by default.
- Added a configurable `retry` binding with support for any button accepted by `config.ini`.
- Added `retry = NONE` support for players who prefer the original automatic flow.
- Preserved cleared-stage progress before replaying a completed normal stage.
- Preserved Special Stage score and Chaos Emerald rewards before replaying a successful attempt.

## Controls and configuration

The default retry button is X. Existing v0.2 configuration files do not need to be replaced; retry still defaults to X when the entry is absent.

To choose another button, close the game and add or edit this entry in:

```text
sdmc:/switch/sonic_advance_2/config.ini
```

Example:

```ini
[controls]
retry = ZR
```

To disable the retry prompt and retain the original result timing:

```ini
[controls]
retry = NONE
```

On normal Stage Clear screens, the prompt appears after score counting finishes. On Special Stage results, A continues and the configured retry button immediately starts the same Special Stage again.

## Updating from v0.2

Replace the old NRO with `sonic_advance2_nx_v0.3.nro`. Existing save data and `config.ini` files are preserved.

The port still requires a clean USA Sonic Advance 2 ROM at:

```text
sdmc:/switch/sonic_advance_2/sa2.gba
```

Expected ROM SHA-1:

```text
7bcd6a07af7c894746fa28073fe0c0e34408022d
```

## Known issues

- Some title-screen graphics and text can be offset or clipped.
- Parts of the character-selection screen can be misaligned.
- The world map / stage-selection screen can contain shifted elements.
- Some in-engine or illustrated story cutscenes can show offsets, clipping or incorrectly placed layers.
- Multiplayer and Tiny Chao Garden are not supported.

## Download verification

SHA-256 (`sonic_advance2_nx_v0.3.nro`):

```text
943af1044dbc04eaa5956d0fec0c6fb55d433dcc3c63f0c6f40feb1295046cff
```

This is an unofficial fan-made port. No ROM is included; users must provide their own legally obtained copy.

# Sonic R NX v0.1.0

Initial Nintendo Switch release of **Sonic R NX**, an unofficial Switch port of the open-source [[Sonic R reimplementation](https://github.com/jnmartin84/sonic-r)](https://github.com/jnmartin84/sonic-r) by jnmartin84.

This first release focuses on stability, native Switch support, and cross-platform multiplayer.

## Features

* Native Nintendo Switch homebrew build
* Stable **30 FPS** gameplay
* Full-screen 16:9 presentation
* Switch-specific GLES rendering compatibility layer
* Nintendo Switch controller support
* Switch-friendly network lobby controls
* Nintendo Switch software keyboard support
* Automatic save and ghost directory creation
* LAN multiplayer
* **PC ↔ Nintendo Switch cross-play**
* Automatic LAN host discovery
* Direct IP connection support
* Experimental internet play by connecting the Switch directly to a reachable PC host
* Custom Homebrew Menu icon

## Network Controls

* **L** — Host / Start Race
* **R** — Join / Search
* **Y** — LAN Mode
* **D-Pad Left / Right** — Change Character
* **D-Pad Up / Down** — Change Track
* **ZR** — Change Game Mode
* **Minus (-)** — Open Network Keyboard
* **Plus (+)** — Direct IP Join
* **A** — Confirm / Send
* **B** — Back

## Online Play

Full native matchmaking is not yet available on the Nintendo Switch version.

However, the Switch can connect directly to a PC host using its IP address, including over the internet if the PC host is reachable on UDP port **7847**.

Because of this, **PC ↔ Switch internet cross-play is partially supported**, although the Switch currently cannot independently sign into the upstream matchmaking service.

## Installation

Copy:

```text
sonicr.nro
```

to:

```text
sdmc:/switch/sonic-r/
```

You must provide your own legally owned Sonic R game data.

See the repository README for the required folder structure and setup instructions.

## Notes

* This release intentionally uses the original **30 Hz gameplay simulation** for stability.
* Experimental 60 FPS support was tested during development but is not included in this release.
* PC and Switch players should use compatible builds and matching game data for multiplayer.
* No original Sonic R assets are included.

## Credits

Huge thanks to **jnmartin84** for the Sonic R reimplementation that made this port possible.

Nintendo Switch port by **Bora Eskicioğlu**.

---

This is an early release, so bug reports and testing feedback are welcome.

# Sonic the Fighters NX v0.8.3

Sonic the Fighters comes to Nintendo Switch through **m2-hle2**, with Switch-specific rendering and audio, widescreen support, native controls, and the original arcade game flow.

## Highlights

- **External ROM loading:** supply your own `sfight.zip` on the SD card. No game ROM is included or embedded in the NRO.
- **Original arcade menus:** the original title screen and character selection are preserved.
- **In-game pause:** press Minus (−) to pause a match and press it again to resume, with the game timer and audio paused together.
- **ZR Hyper shortcut:** activate the original Hyper command with one button; normal activation conditions and barrier cost still apply.
- **Earlier Super Sonic access:** play as Sonic, collect seven Chaos Emeralds, and activate Hyper from stage 8 onward. The no-loss, no-continue, and Metal Sonic second-round restrictions are removed.
- **Rebalanced defense:** Super Sonic takes one quarter of incoming damage, rounded up to at least 1 for positive hits. He can still be knocked out.
- **Widescreen and rendering work:** includes the prior Switch-focused renderer, texture-upload, loading, and audio improvements.
- **ROM-free builds and releases:** the build and release scripts reject embedded RomFS and do not require a game ROM to compile.

## Installation

Extract the release ZIP to the root of your SD card, then add your own compatible ROM:

| File | Required SD-card path |
|---|---|
| Application | `SD:/switch/sonic_fighters_nx/sonic_fighters_nx.nro` |
| Your ROM | `SD:/switch/sonic_fighters_nx/sfight.zip` |

Keep `sfight.zip` zipped and named exactly as shown. Launch the application from the Homebrew Menu in application mode (title takeover).

**Upgrading from an embedded-ROM build?** Replace the older NRO and provide `sfight.zip` separately. Missing, empty, or invalid archives display an explanatory error; B or Plus (+) exits the error screen.

## Controls

| Action | Input |
|---|---|
| Move | Left stick / D-pad |
| Punch | B |
| Kick | A |
| Guard | Y |
| Hyper Mode | ZR |
| Start | Plus (+) |
| Pause / Resume | Minus (−), during gameplay |
| Exit | ZL + ZR + Plus (+) |

## Notes

- The external-ROM version has been reported working on real Switch hardware by the port maintainer.
- This release makes no new fixed-FPS or overclock claim.
- Game ROMs must be supplied by the user and are not distributed with the project.

Thanks to **[biggestsonicfan and the m2-hle2 contributors](https://github.com/biggestsonicfan/m2-hle2)**, devkitPro/libnx, Mesa/Nouveau, sokol, and miniz. Nintendo Switch port by **[Bora Eskicioğlu / BESK](https://github.com/boraeskicioglu)**.

Sonic the Fighters and related characters/assets belong to their respective rights holders. This unofficial project is not endorsed by SEGA or Nintendo. The upstream first-party license remains unselected at the pinned revision; the source includes the corresponding license-status and dependency notices.

# Super Paper Mario NX v0.5.0

An unofficial fan project. Not affiliated with Nintendo. No game data is included in this release: the port reads the game's files from your own extracted copy of the game, as before.

## What's new

- **Smoother frame pacing in 3D scenes.** The way each finished frame is handed off to the display has been reworked so the game thread spends less time waiting at the frame boundary. 3D areas pace noticeably steadier; how 2D plays is unchanged.
- **Less wasted work per frame.** The coplanar depth reference the renderer maintains for frozen draws is now computed only when something actually reads it, instead of being recomputed on every draw whether it is used or not.
- **The display-list apply memo is on by default.** When a display list and the vertex state it needs are unchanged since the last hand-off, the port skips re-applying that state. It has been verified extensively against the unmemoised path and produces identical output.

## Updating

Replace the .nro file with the new one. Nothing else needs to change unless the release notes say so, and for this release nothing else does. Your saves, settings and caches in `UserData/` carry over untouched.

If you have edited `dk_diag.txt` by hand, the new mechanisms each have an off ramp there: `sealdefer=0` restores the old frame hand-off, `zfreezelazy=0` restores the eager depth reference, and `applymemo=0` turns the apply memo off.

## Known issues

- Performance in heavy 3D areas is still much slower than the original game. This release improves frame pacing there; it does not close the gap. Keep expectations low in those areas.
- The Touch Tippi calibration is still the approximate one shipped in v0.4.0, with a known residual offset. Unchanged in this release.

The first release: **FIFA Street** (Xbox, 2005) running natively on the Nintendo Switch, statically recompiled from the original Xbox executable. No emulator.

> [!NOTE]
> No game files are included. You need your own copy of *FIFA Street* for the original Xbox, **USA** release (title ID `45410072`).

## What's in it

- The whole game: intro movies, menus, Game On, Rule the Street, saving and loading
- **60 fps in matches**, handheld (1280x720) and docked (1920x1080), at the console's stock clocks
- Sound and music
- English or Spanish, following your Switch's system language (`language` in the settings to choose another)
- Native **deko3d** renderer
- Anisotropic filtering x2 by default; optional SMAA anti-aliasing
- FPS and resolution in Status Monitor / Horizon OC Monitor (SaltyNX)

## Installation

The easy way: **[xsaja.github.io/street-nx](https://xsaja.github.io/street-nx/)**. Pick your disc image or game folder, download `street-nx.zip` and extract it into `SD:/switch/`. It all happens in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

By hand:

1. Download `street.nro`, `street-settings.toml` and `LICENSES.txt` into `SD:/switch/street-nx/`.
2. Copy the files of your disc into `SD:/switch/street-nx/game/`: `default.xbe` and the `data` folder.
3. Start it in **title mode**: hold R while launching any installed game and pick it in hbmenu, or use sphaira or a forwarder.

The first start compiles the shaders for deko3d: a few seconds of black screen, once.

## Good to know

- Your progress is loaded from **Options > Load saved game**.
- Saves are named in the game's language: a game saved in English and one saved in Spanish are two different saves.
- Kick-offs, goals and half-time load data, with a short hitch.
- Logs are in `SD:/switch/street-nx/logs/`; please attach them to any issue.

TGP482 (XboxXBE-Recomp), maddog847 (MVP05 XBE Recomp), gerisson1996 (BLACK-NX-PORT), ChanseyIsTheBest, fincs, danfromtico and NaGaa95, R-drg, the SMAA authors, and the SteamGridDB artists. Every license is in `LICENSES.txt`.

packages.changelog:
### **Release v1.0.0**

First release of the Sonic Triple Trouble 16-Bit wrapper for the Nintendo Switch. The game is fully playable from start to finish at a locked 60 FPS.

**What Works**

1. **Fully Playable:** The game can be completed from start to finish without crashes.
2. **Locked 60 FPS**: Native ARM64 execution with no emulation layer. The GMS2 runner runs directly on Switch hardware at full clock speed.
3. **Full Controller Support:** All physical buttons are mapped — A, B, X, Y, D-Pad (all 4 directions), both analog sticks, +, −, L, R, ZL, ZR. D-Pad support was implemented via reverse-engineered GameMaker's internal Hat event system (onGPNativeHat) rather than raw key codes.
4. **Analog Stick:** Both sticks work correctly with a deadzone filter and drift prevention. Startup centering is handled to eliminate the self-locking diagonal drift issue common in GMS2 ports.
5. **Full Audio:** Stereo audio using a custom OpenSL ES → SDL2 software mixer shim with full sound effects and background music.
6. **Save Data:** Game progress and settings persist correctly. Saves are flushed safely on exit and when the application is backgrounded.
7. **Performance:** Optimized with -O3 -ffast-math, extended CPU boost window for asset loading, and a larger SDL2 audio buffer to minimize callback overhead and frame time spikes.

**Known Issues**

None known at this time. Please open an issue if you encounter anything unexpected.

packages.changelog:
The first release of Super Mario War NX, a native Nintendo Switch port of [Super Mario War](https://github.com/mmatyas/supermariowar), the fan-made multiplayer Mario deathmatch game.

![Four players as Dice Guy on Ice Shelf, running on a Switch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brendongl/supermariowar-nx/main/docs/switch/screenshot-ice-shelf.jpg)

## What's in it

- Up to 4 players on one console: Joy-Con pairs, single sideways Joy-Cons, Pro Controllers or handheld mode, in any mix
- All 22 game modes, tournaments, tours and world maps, plus all the bundled maps, skins, music and sound packs
- Locked 60 fps on hardware, at 720p handheld and 1080p docked, with sharp pixel scaling
- Full 16:9 screen: scores, lives and stored items move to a side panel, so the whole arena is free
- New character: **Dice Guy**, the mascot of [Sip n Play](https://sipnplay.cafe), a board game cafe in Saigon
- Settings and screenshots are saved to `sdmc:/switch/supermariowar/`

## Install

You need a Switch running Atmosphère.

1. Extract `SuperMarioWar-NX-v1.0.0.zip` to the root of your SD card. This puts `smw.nro` in `sdmc:/switch/supermariowar/`.
2. Optional, for a HOME menu icon: install `SuperMarioWar-NX-v1.0.0-forwarder.nsp` with DBI, Tinfoil or Awoo. It starts the NRO above, so keep both. Installing NSPs needs signature patches for your firmware.

Or skip the NSP and start it from the Homebrew Menu. Launch the menu by holding R over a game (title override), not from the Album, so the game gets full memory.

`smw.nro` is also attached on its own if you'd rather copy just that file.

## Testing

- About 8 hours of 4-player CPU matches on a real Switch (Atmosphère, firmware 22.5.0), over 240 matches with no crashes
- 500+ matches under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer on Linux
- Played by people with real controllers

Fixes for bugs found on the way (several crashes after a player is knocked out, a crash on quitting mid-match, an out-of-bounds read in warps, and more) are general fixes that will also be offered upstream.

## Known issues

- No online play (local multiplayer only). Browser multiplayer is on the [roadmap](https://github.com/brendongl/supermariowar-nx/blob/main/ROADMAP.md).
- The level and world editors aren't included (they need keyboard and mouse).
- Only the forwarder NSP is provided. A standalone NSP build currently crashes on launch.

If something goes wrong, please [open an issue](https://github.com/brendongl/supermariowar-nx/issues/new/choose) and attach `sdmc:/switch/supermariowar/smw.log`.

---

<sub>Vibe-coded by the owner of [Sip n Play](https://sipnplay.cafe), a board game and video game cafe in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon), Vietnam. If you're ever in town, come visit and say hi to Dice Guy!</sub>

packages.changelog:
v0.7.23: firmware 23.5.0, and a newer firmware no longer stops the console

**Fixes**
- **Firmware 23.5.0: no more crash at boot** (#83, #87, #90, #99): the sysmodule is now built against Atmosphère 1.12.2, which knows 23.5.0. v0.7.22 and older were built against 1.12.0, whose library stops any program on a firmware newer than it knows - a fatal error (std::abort, 0100000000000C20) on every boot. Update Atmosphère to 1.12.2 first. Tested by users on firmware 21.1.0 and 23.0.1 (and an Atmosphère 1.12.2 build on 23.5.0).
- **A newer firmware no longer stops the console**: from this version on, when the console runs a firmware newer than the build knows, Switch Frame Tap boots without streaming and the app and viewer say to update (Setup > Allow untested firmware tries anyway).
- **Games with many buffers the size of their screen** (#70, Maestro): the stream finds which buffers hold the picture by watching them change; Maestro has 95 of them and the stream looked at the first 48 only, so it showed a wrong one (violet noise). It now looks at up to 96, reading the same amount per frame as before. When it still can't tell, the log says why.

**Viewers**
- **Playback volume** (thanks @myaumura, #85, #84): Settings > Sound > Playback volume, 0-100 %, saved. Recordings and the Switch's own volume are not changed.
- **Smoother under load** (thanks @Laliukz, #92): the packet queue hands buffers over instead of copying them, and the viewer's threads run at a higher priority. On Windows and Linux (OpenGL), **Y** sets an FSR/NIS render scale (150/200/300 %) and **F9** the sharpness. On Windows, the previous session's log is kept as viewer.prev.log.
- **USB on Macs** (#49): when USB reads fail, the viewer clears a stalled connection and, after 8 errors in a row, opens the Switch again as after a pulled cable.

Note: "Sound in no-record games" has no patch for 23.5.0 yet (exelix11/dvr-patches) - on 23.5.0 those games stay silent for now.

**Updating:** open the Switch app's **Updates** page (or unzip `switch-frame-tap-0.7.23-switch.zip` over the SD card root) and restart the console. Settings are kept. On firmware 23.5.0 with v0.7.22 installed the console stops at boot: unzip this version onto the SD card from a PC. The PC viewers and the Android app offer the update when they open.

---
<sub>Switch Frame Tap is free and open source. If you would like to support it: [buymeacoffee.com/papux200](https://buymeacoffee.com/papux200)</sub>

A small release on top of 0.3: a Spanish translation and classic Guitar Hero
fret handling for gamepads. It passes the desktop tests and the Switch
cross-build. The items marked *(hardware)* still need a run on a console.

### Spanish
- Spanish joins English and Brazilian Portuguese in the language picker
  (first launch and Options), shown as **Español**. Every string the game
  translates has a Spanish line, hit ratings included. Contributed by
  CHSDev360.
- The "you can change it later in options" line on the language screen moved
  down so it clears a third menu row.

### Classic gamepad frets *(hardware)*
- Single notes accept lower frets held under the target, like anchoring on a
  guitar controller. Pressing the note's own fret hits it as before.
- With the target fret held, pressing any lower fret re-strikes the same
  single note, so fast repeated notes can be played by alternating lower
  frets.
- HOPO and tap notes can be completed by any fret change that leaves the
  target as the highest held fret, so releasing a higher fret works as a
  pull-off. HOPOs still need an active combo; taps do not.
- Higher frets never count, and chords keep the exact-shape rule. A lower-fret
  re-strike consumes that press, so one press still hits one note.
  Contributed by aloumamae.

### Other
- The title screen and the download user agent show the full version
  (`v0.3.1`, `switch-hero/0.3.1`) rather than major.minor only.

Games now cache themselves when you play online. A new app caches all your games in one run.

## Changes

- **Games cache themselves online.** Start a game while the Switch has Wi-Fi. The module then saves its achievement data, so the game also has achievements offline. Before, the only way was `fetch-cache.py` on a computer.
- **New: ra-offline cacher app.** Start it from the Homebrew Menu and press **A**. It finds every game in `/roms`, `/tico/roms` and `/retroarch/roms`, and caches them in one run. You do not need to start each game or restart anything. Press **Y** to also check again the games that had no achievement set last time.
- **Clear offline message.** An uncached game now shows *"Not cached offline. Play this game once online to cache it."*

## Before you go offline

Offline, only cached games have achievements. We recommend that you start each game once while the Switch is online. That caches the game and shows that RetroArch loads its achievements. For a large library, run the cacher app before you go offline.

## Install or update

Copy the zip's `atmosphere` and `switch` folders to the root of your SD card. Then reboot the console once. The zip now also holds the cacher app (`switch/ra-offline-cacher/ra-offline-cacher.nro`).

The cacher app needs `sd:/switch/raoffline/account.json`. Run `tools/fetch-cache.py --user NAME --password PASS` once on a computer to make it.

## What's new

- **Dead connections are closed.** When a phone or Mac leaves without saying goodbye (for example when its Wi-Fi drops), its connection is now closed after 60 seconds of silence instead of staying open. Before, such connections were only noticed if they sent data again, and the receiver then read from a connection it had just closed.
- **Fixes from upstream UxPlay**, the AirPlay library SwitchAirCast is built on (through UxPlay `b1be2bd`, 2026-11-02): the AirPlay clock-sync replies now carry the full 64-bit timestamp the client sent, an uninitialized lock in the HTTP server is now set up properly, and a few spots with undefined behaviour in the byte-order and timestamp helpers are cleaned up.

Nothing changes in the menus or settings.

## Upgrading

Replace `/switch/SwitchAirCast.nro` with the new file. Your settings are kept.

## Install

1. Download `SwitchAirCast.nro` below and copy it to `/switch/` on your SD card. (Or download the zip and extract it to the root of the SD card.)
2. Open the Homebrew Menu **through a game** (hold **R** while starting any game) and start SwitchAirCast.
3. On your iPhone, iPad or Mac (same Wi-Fi network): Control Center → **Screen Mirroring** → choose your Switch.

See the [README](https://github.com/depende3000/SwitchAirCast#readme) for all buttons, settings and troubleshooting.

## Reporting a problem

Open an issue and attach `log.txt` and `log-previous.txt` from `/config/SwitchAirCast/` on the SD card, plus the newest file in `/atmosphere/crash_reports/` if the app crashed. With `debug_log = true` the log is much more detailed, and the last 10 runs are kept in `/config/SwitchAirCast/logs/`.

# SwitchNOW 1.3.0 — Streaming & Experience Update

Changes from the **1.2.1 R1–R73** branch, consolidated into **1.3.0**. SwitchNOW author and maintainer: **Blade-Punisher**.

## Highlights

- **Three streaming modes:** Performance, Balanced, and Quality, with refined frame delivery and recovery after packet loss.
- **More responsive controls:** up to four independent controllers, touch mouse input, and an expanded in-stream menu and keyboard shortcuts.
- **Improved session handling:** refined server selection, connection recovery, queue reporting, and in-place application updates.
- **A fuller, more stable library:** complete owned-game loading, shared store/library paging, and faster screenshot browsing.
- **Better HOME shortcuts and auto-login:** background artwork checks, redesigned shortcut creation, game-specific profiles, and shared Epic Games login excluding Fortnite.
- **Eight interface languages:** expanded offline UI translations and automatic translation of missing game descriptions.

## Installation / Updating

**New installation**
1. Download `SwitchNOW-1.3.0.zip` from the assets below.
2. Extract it and copy the `switch` folder to the root of your SD card.
3. Launch SwitchNOW through Homebrew Menu in **application/title-override mode**.

**Updating an existing installation**
1. Close SwitchNOW before replacing its file.
2. Download `SwitchNOW-1.3.0.nro` and replace the existing NRO **at the same path, keeping its current filename**. This also applies to installations directly in `SD:/switch/`.
3. Keep your existing account and settings files. Alternatively, use the built-in updater.

`SwitchNOW-1.3.0-source.zip` contains source code for developers. File hashes are available in `SwitchNOW-1.3.0-SHA256SUMS.txt`.

> [!WARNING]
> **Game and Epic auto-login profiles store your email/login and password as plain text on the SD card.** Anyone who can read the card can read these credentials. Auto-login is optional: protect your SD card and do not share these credential files. This warning concerns game/Epic profiles; GFN account password storage uses a separate encrypted local vault. CAPTCHA and 2FA prompts still require manual input.

---

## Streaming and image quality

- Added three streaming modes: **Performance**, **Balanced**, and **Quality**. Balanced is the default; resolution, frame rate, and maximum bitrate remain independently configurable. Legacy mode settings migrate to the current profiles.
- Refined local adaptation to packet loss, delivery jitter, and decoder pressure, with bounded frame waiting, protective intervals, and gradual recovery after conditions stabilize.
- Improved video recovery through RTP reordering, NACK/RTX, keyframe requests, and reference-frame damage handling. Added output-frame checks using PTS and a verified IDR after a fault.
- Fixed handling of resolution, pixel-format, and stride changes. Retained plane validation, GPU synchronization, and safe resource recreation.
- Reduced repeated NV12 storage and frame-header allocations. Added reuse of upload descriptors and command memory.
- Refined presentation queuing to limit stale-frame buildup, cautiously reduce excess latency during stable delivery, and back off after adverse events.
- Automatic video mode retains hardware NVDEC decoding with completed frames copied into owned Deko3D textures. The experimental zero-copy path is not enabled by default.

## Input responsiveness

- Support for up to **four independent controllers**, with separate state and connection/disconnection notifications.
- Dedicated controller sampling and priority for fresh input over periodic network maintenance, reducing unnecessary waits and contention with the UI.
- Fixed lost short button presses, trigger handling, and SCTP sequence errors when opening the input channel. Added bounded retransmission and correct handling of a fu

Pick the download for your disc:

| Your disc | Download | Disc image |
|---|---|---|
| USA (`GZLE01`, revision 0) | `SwitchWaker-v1.0.2-switch.zip` | `sdmc:/switch/switchwaker/GZLE01.iso` |
| Europe (`GZLP01`, revision 0) | `SwitchWaker-v1.0.2-switch-eur.zip` | `sdmc:/switch/switchwaker/GZLP01.iso` |

- **Updating from 1.0.0 or 1.0.1:** the game offers the update at the title screen (or options menu (Minus) > **Sistema**).
- **Updating from 0.5.0 or older:** copy the zip's `switch` folder over the old one. Your disc, saves, settings and the HOME-screen icon stay as they are.
- **New install:** copy the zip's `switch` folder to the root of the SD card and put your disc image (uncompressed `.iso`) at the path above. Details: **[INSTALL.md](https://github.com/centollOS/SwitchWaker/blob/v1.0.2/INSTALL.md)**.
- One region per SD card: both downloads install `sdmc:/switch/switchwaker/switchwaker.nro`.

## Known issues

- "Instant text" does not speed up the text of some cutscenes (for example the arrival on Outset Island).
- The disc's videos (the title screen's attract video and the ending video) do not play yet.
- Docked at 60 fps the frame rate can still drop to 30 in heavy scenes.

Credits, licenses and how AI was used: see the README.

# v1.2.0 — in-app updater, the panel in landscape, upstream v2.0.9, six languages

Built against **bighead's ladxhd_updated v2.0.9** (released 9 October 2026). If you are on
v1.1.0, just replace the NRO: the first start notices the assets are from v2.0.8, re-patches
your `original/` copy on the console (about a minute) and carries on. Your saves are untouched.

**This is the last time you have to copy an NRO by hand.** From here on the port updates itself
from the console.

## What's new

### In-app updater

Companion panel → **⚙ SETTINGS → UPDATE**. Tap the row and it checks this repository for a new
version; tap twice to confirm and it downloads, verifies and installs it, right there on the
console.

What it does *not* do matters as much as what it does:

- It never trusts the download. The manifest pins the exact **size and SHA-256** before a single
  byte is fetched, and the file is checked against both afterwards.
- It never touches the NRO you are running until a **verified backup** of it exists
  (`ProjectZ.Switch.bak`, right next to it). If the install goes wrong, that backup goes back.
- It never goes anywhere else: HTTPS only, `github.com` / `*.githubusercontent.com` only, using
  the console's own TLS and certificate store (no bundled certificates).
- Offline, it says "no connection" and stops. A console without wifi is not shown an error.

The design is the one from the *Minish Cap* edition of this project, which has shipped it since
its v1.3 — the parts that differ are the ones that had to.

### The companion panel works in landscape now

Press **Minus** and the panel opens over the game, centred, with everything dimmed behind it.
D-pad moves the selection, **A** uses it, **L**/**R** cycle the tabs, **Minus** closes. On the
ITEMS tab, **A** equips to the A slot and **B** to the B slot. Touch keeps working as well.

Until now the panel only existed in Flip Grip and only by touch, which meant that if you play
docked — and plenty of people do — none of it was reachable: no map, no story guide, no settings
without the combos.

**The game pauses while the panel is up.** That is deliberate, and it buys two things: the D-pad
belongs to the panel without Link wandering off, and the game never sees the `Minus` that opens
and closes the panel — in this game `Minus` is the game's own map, so without that it would open
underneath every time.

If you would rather keep `Minus` for the map, turn the panel off under
**Pause → Settings → Video → Panel with Minus**.

### Up to date with upstream v2.0.9

Everything bighead fixed in v2.0.9 comes with it, including:

- The boomerang is redirected when you smack it with the sword, following the direction Link faces.
- Picking up the Angler Fish heart container works in any state, not only while swimming.
- The enemy Urchin no longer crashes the game when burned.
- High definition texture replacement (for LAHDMods that ship one; it changes nothing otherwise).
- Improved Italian and German translations, and Chinese achievements.

### The port's own interface in six languages

- The **Switch rows in the game's own Video menu** (Switch resolution, FPS limit, Flip Grip,
  hide HUD, large UI) were English or Spanish only. They now follow the game language across
  **English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German and Italian**, tooltips included — the same
  six the companion panel already spoke.
- The **story guide** (the "next step" line on the QUEST tab, and the trading-sequence hint)
  was English and Spanish. It is now in all six as well: 27 main-quest steps and the 14 trades
  per language.

  The place, dungeon, key and character names are **not** invented or machine-translated: they
  are read out of the game's own language files, so French really says *Plage Coco*, *Cave
  Flagello* and *Toutou*, and German says *Torongastrand*, *Wurmpalast* and *Struppi* — the
  names those players actually see on their signposts.

Any other game language still falls back to English, as before.

# Alek’s Ultimate NX Edition 1.1.3

Two fixes: Kakariko’s Malo Mart no longer crashes, and Iron Boots on Twilit Essentials’ Z button come off again.

**Updating?** Use **Check for updates** on the main menu (or in **Settings → Aleks**). Your saves, settings and mods are kept.

## Fixed

- **Entering Kakariko’s Malo Mart no longer crashes the game.** Once you had talked to the Malo Mart clerk in Castle Town, the Goron in the Kakariko shop crashed the room as it loaded. The bug comes from the decompiled code our compiler handles differently (upstream issue [TwilitRealm/dusklight#2695](https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight/issues/2695)); it had nothing to do with your disc, region or mods. Thanks to **Malachite01** for the report (#14).
- **Iron Boots come off when you take them off.** With the boots on Twilit Essentials’ Z button (or kept equipped by its Quick Access), taking them off put them straight back on. - **Catalog check:** on 9 November 2026, 75 of the catalog’s 81 mods pass this build’s checks, the same as 1.1.2.

packages.changelog:
tico 0.8.2 fixes RetroAchievements sign-in, which failed for everyone on 0.8.1 with "Sign-in failed".

> [!NOTE]
> tico 0.8.2 works with the same 3.0.0 emulators as 0.8.0 and 0.8.1. Nothing to reinstall.

## RetroAchievements

- **Sign-in works again.** RetroAchievements now refuses sign-ins from apps that present themselves as a web browser, which tico did. tico now identifies itself as tico.
- **tico signs in by itself.** If your password is saved but games aren't signed in, tico signs in in the background after you pick your account, with no need to open Settings or start a game. You'll see "Signed in as …" once it works.
- If RetroAchievements turns down your password, tico doesn't try it again until you change it. If there's no connection, it tries again a minute later.
- When RetroAchievements refuses a sign-in without saying why, Settings › Accounts shows the server's answer (for example "HTTP 403") instead of only "Sign-in failed".

Achievements inside games were not affected: emulators already reached RetroAchievements correctly once tico had signed in.

## Updating

Open the Store in tico and install the tico update, or copy `tico.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/tico/` (over the old one).

If your account showed **Sign-in failed** in 0.8.1, you don't need to do anything: start tico 0.8.2 and it signs in by itself.

> [!WARNING]
> **Requires tico 0.8.0 or later.** This module doesn't work with older tico versions. If you're on an earlier version, wait for the tico 0.8.0 release before updating.

A big update: Dolphin is now a tico module. It gets the new in-game menu with every core option, button mapping, cheats, Riivolution mods, online play, auto save and per-game settings, and its saves move to tico's saves folder.

## Highlights

- **New quick menu**: the same menu as tico's other cores, with Save State, Load State, Change Disc, Cheats, Mods, Portal and Reset, plus a sidebar for Settings, Restart and Exit Game. It follows tico's theme and works by touch.
- **Full settings, in tico and in game**: every option the core supports, plus per-game settings (Settings › This Game).
- **Button mapping** (#7, #28, #44): Settings › Mapping remaps the GameCube Controller, Wii Remote (upright and sideways), Nunchuk and Classic Controller. **Shake**, **Tilt** and **Swing** can go on any button, for the Wii Remote and the Nunchuk.
- **Players screen**: Settings › Players shows the controller on each port and opens the Switch's controller screen.
- **Auto save and continue where you left off**, save states with pictures, Undo Load/Save State, and **Change Disc** for multi-disc games (states remember their disc).
- **Cheats** (#31): Gecko, Action Replay and patch codes in the Cheats menu, with **Download Gecko codes** for the running game.
- **Riivolution mods** (#22, #25): copy a mod's SD card files to `sdmc:/tico/mods/wii/`, then turn its options on in the quick menu's **Mods** screen and Restart.
- **Online play** (#14): the Wii now uses the Switch's internet connection, so games patched for **Wiimmfi** or **WiiLink WFC** can go online. Also **WiiConnect24 via WiiLink**, the GameCube **Broadband Adapter** with a choice of DNS, and **Correct time drift**.
- **Skylanders portal** (#39): Settings › System › Wii › Emulate Skylanders portal, then place figures from the quick menu's **Portal** screen. Figure dumps come from `sdmc:/tico/skylanders/` and from Emulanders' `sdmc:/emulanders/figures/`.
- **WiiWare and Virtual Console** (#4, #8): `.wad` files in the Wii list.
- **Triforce arcade games** (#42): a new Triforce system, `sdmc:/tico/roms/triforce/`. Coin is on −, Service on L3 and Test on R3.
- **Wii Menu and GameCube Menu** (#40): the first item in the Wii list once the Wii Menu is installed, and in the GameCube list once a GameCube BIOS is provided.
- **More formats** (#16): `.ciso` and `.gcz` games are listed.
- **Allow mismatched region settings** (#33): translated games can use the language you pick.
- **Boost mode**: Settings › Behavior › Boost mode (on by default) runs the CPU at 1785 MHz and the GPU at 768 MHz while you play.
- **deko3d renderer**: Dolphin now draws with deko3d, the Switch GPU's own API, from [nezumiiruka](https://github.com/PalindromicBreadLoaf/nezumiiruka) by @PalindromicBreadLoaf. Settings › Video › Renderer can switch to Vulkan if a game misbehaves on deko3d.
- **Game library**: opening Dolphin from the homebrew menu shows your GameCube and Wii games.

## Saves

- **Saves move to `sdmc:/tico/saves`** (#9), like the other cores: GameCube memory cards in `saves/gc/<region>`, each Wii game's save in `saves/wii/<GAMEID>`. Your existing saves are moved there on the first start, never over a save that's already there.
- **Wii save import** (#9): copy a Wii SD card's `private` folder (`data.bin` files) into `sdmc:/tico/saves/wii/import/`, and the save is imported when its game starts. The save it replaces is kept as a backup.
- **Wii save states** (#34): they now include the state of the Wii's system devices, which they used to miss. States made with older versions of Wii games won't load.

## Fixes

- **Boost clocks are kept** (#2): docking, undocking or waking from sleep no longer drops them back to stock. With **sys-clk**, **sys-clk-OC** (kefir) or **Horizon-OC**, Dolphin asks the clock manager for them instead of fighting

A fix for the console's clock speeds.

## Fixes

- **Clocks left to the Switch and your overclock tool**: the emulator no longer sets a fixed clock profile when a game starts. On the TV, that profile lowered the GPU and memory below the Switch's normal speeds, and with an overclock tool's override turned off, every game was held at 460 MHz GPU and 1600 MHz memory. Games now run at the Switch's normal clocks, or at what your overclock tool sets.

## Installing

Update from the tico Store, or extract `tico-fbneo-module.zip` into `sdmc:/tico/modules/`. Saves, states and settings carry over.

# tico Flycast 3.0.0

> [!WARNING]
> **Requires tico 0.8.0 or later.** This module doesn't work with older tico versions. If you're on an earlier version, wait for the tico 0.8.0 release before updating.

A big update: Flycast is now a tico module, based on Flycast v2.7. It gets the new in-game menu with every core option, plus RetroArch shaders with AMD FSR, frame generation, a game list, cheats, auto save, per-game settings, a BIOS check and upright vertical arcade games.

## Highlights

- **New quick menu**: the same menu as tico's other cores. The list holds Save State, Load State, Change Disc, Cheats and Reset, with a sidebar for Settings, Restart and Exit Game. Reset, Restart and Exit ask for confirmation, and tooltips explain the difference between Reset and Restart. The menu follows tico's light or dark theme, has the animated border in your Screen Colors tint, works by touch, and has an optional FPS / resolution display.
- **Full settings, in tico and in game**: options apply live. The ones that only take effect at boot (region, language, BIOS, cable, RAM size, widescreen cheats and so on) say *Use Restart to apply*.
- **Per-game settings**: Settings › This Game › *Save current settings for this game* stores the game's own settings. From then on, changes apply to that game only. *Delete this game's settings* (asked first) brings back the shared ones. You can also manage them from tico: press **+** on a game in the launcher, or use Emulator Settings › Game Settings.
- **Auto save and continue where you left off**: Flycast saves your spot automatically when you exit, restart, return to the game list or press HOME. Next time, it offers to continue from there, showing a picture and when it was saved. Choose *Ask*, *Always* or *Never* in tico › General › Continue Last Game.
- **Save states with pictures**: 5 slots plus the Auto slot. Each slot shows a picture of the game and when it was saved.
- **RetroArch slang shaders**: Settings › Shaders runs presets over Flycast's image. **CRT Easy Mode** and **AMD FSR 1.0** are built in, and you can add your own to `sdmc:/tico/shaders/`. Parameters are saved per preset. FSR upscales the game's picture to the screen and sharpens it: try it with a low internal resolution, for much less GPU than rendering higher.
- **Frame generation (LSFG)**: Settings › Display › Frame Generation puts a generated frame between each two of the game's, so 30 fps games show 60. Games already at 60 fps are left alone. It needs your own copy of Lossless Scaling's `Lossless.dll` in `sdmc:/tico/system/lsfg/` (a copy in Dolphin's `sdmc:/switch/dolphin/lsfg/` works too); it's never shipped. Motion Estimation Scale (25/50%) and Performance Shaders tune quality against GPU load.
- **Game list**: opening Flycast from the homebrew menu lists your Dreamcast, NAOMI and Atomiswave games. Exit Game returns to the list. Extra folders can be added in Settings › Library.
- **Players screen**: Settings › Players shows the controller each port has. It also opens the Switch's controller screen to change who is which player.
- **Vertical arcade games**: vertical shooters and other TATE arcade games are now turned upright. *Screen Orientation: Vertical* keeps them in TATE, smoothly scaled, for playing with the Switch on its side.
- **BIOS check**: before booting, Flycast checks that the game's BIOS is there: `dc_boot.bin` (unless HLE BIOS is on), `naomi.zip` or `awbios.zip`. A missing or broken file now shows a message naming the file and folder instead of a black screen. For Dreamcast games, it offers to switch to HLE BIOS and restart. It also tells you when your `dc_boot.bin` is an unknown dump.
- **Cheats**: Dreamcast GameShark / CodeBreaker codes from `.cht` or `.cheats` files in `sdmc:/tico/cheats/<dc|naomi|atomiswave>/`. Every cheat is off at launch.
- **Controller mapping**: the Input tab has a Dreamcast mapping and an Arcade (NAOMI / Atomiswave) mapping. Each puts any pad input on any Switch button.
- **Vibration**: g

# tico PPSSPP 3.0.0

> [!WARNING]
> **Requires tico 0.8.0 or later.** This module doesn't work with older tico versions. If you're on an earlier version, wait for the tico 0.8.0 release before updating.

A big update: PPSSPP is now a tico module, based on PPSSPP's latest development version, with Switch fixes from the ppsspp-nx port. It adds network multiplayer, frame generation, full button mapping and a settings menu that matches what the emulator actually does.

## Highlights

- **Based on PPSSPP's latest development version**: everything PPSSPP has gained since 1.20.4, about 2,450 changes.
- **Right stick as the D-Pad** (#1, #3): Settings › Input › *Right Stick As* sets the right stick to Face Buttons (as in 2.0.2, still the default), D-Pad (camera control in Peace Walker, Monster Hunter Freedom Unite, The Third Birthday), Analog or Disabled.
- **Button mapping**: Settings › Input › *Button Mapping* puts any PSP button, or none, on every Switch button.
- **Network multiplayer** (#5): a new Network tab turns on the PSP's network for ad hoc play over a relay server (`socom.cc` by default) or a server hosted on one console for a LAN. It also covers online games that have revival servers. Other players see your Switch user's name, or a nickname you choose. The console keeps the same PSP MAC address across launches, so servers and friend lists recognise it.
- **Frame generation (LSFG)**: Settings › Display › *Frame Generation* puts a generated frame between each two of a game's, so 30 fps games show 60. Games already at 60 fps are left alone. It needs your own copy of Lossless Scaling's `Lossless.dll` in `sdmc:/tico/system/lsfg/` (a copy in Dolphin's `sdmc:/switch/dolphin/lsfg/` works too); it's never shipped. Turning it on takes effect at the next launch.
- **More settings**: CPU core (JIT, IR JIT, Interpreter) and fast memory under System.

## Fixes

- **Analog circularity works** (#8): the Switch's round stick is now stretched to the PSP's square when *Analog Circularity* is on, so diagonals reach the corners at full speed. Deadzone and sensitivity now apply to the stick's whole movement, as in PPSSPP itself.
- **Buffer filtering** now changes how the picture is scaled; before, the option did nothing.
- **Settings that did nothing are gone**: hardware tessellation, software skinning, range culling and lazy texture caching (removed from PPSSPP), and frame skip type.
- **New options reach existing installs**: options added in an update are now written into your existing `ppsspp.jsonc`, so you no longer need to delete it (#7).
- **The PSP's clock follows the console's time zone.**
- **Hot Pixel's title screen** shows correctly (a compatibility fix from PPSSPP).
- **RetroAchievements over HTTPS**: logins and requests are now encrypted; before, they went over plain HTTP.
- More stable on the Switch: emulator threads are spread over the three game cores, and memory and JIT setup clean up properly when they fail.

## Credits

- Switch fixes, HTTPS and frame generation from @NaGaa95's ppsspp-nx.
- Button mapping, ad hoc multiplayer and config defaults by **@jhuz0** (#4, #6, #7).

## Under the hood

- PPSSPP is now a self-contained tico module: settings, game list and translations ship with it.
- Translated into English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian and Chinese.

## Installing

Extract `tico-ppsspp-module.zip` into `sdmc:/tico/modules/` (you'll get `sdmc:/tico/modules/ppsspp/`).

**Upgrading from 2.x:**
- Your saves, states and settings stay where they were. New options are added to your existing settings automatically.
- PPSSPP's data files in `sdmc:/tico/system/psp/` are updated automatically on the first launch.
- The 2.x `tico-ppsspp.nro` in `sdmc:/tico/cores/` isn't used anymore and can be deleted.

# tico YabaSanshiro 3.1.0

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Fixes YabaSanshiro closing as soon as a game starts from tico 0.8.0 or later.** If 3.0.0 crashed for you, this is the update to install.

> [!CAUTION]
> **Vulkan is heavier than OpenGL.** It needs an overclocked Switch to run at full speed. OpenGL is the default and the lighter renderer.

YabaSanshiro is updated to 1.20.55, with CRT filters, a high-quality sound option and more accurate VDP1 and rotation-screen graphics, and it no longer crashes when tico starts a game.

## Highlights

- **No more crash at launch.** YabaSanshiro opens the session tico hands it (your account, folders and RetroAchievements) with libsodium, whose random source reads `/dev/urandom`, which the Switch doesn't have. It aborted right away. It now uses the console's own random generator, as tico and the other emulators do.
- **CRT filters**: Settings › Video › Video Filter now has *CRT Hyllian*, *CRT Lottes* and *CRT NewPixie*, RetroArch's CRT shaders, with OpenGL or Vulkan. The game is drawn at the Saturn's own resolution and the shader scales it to the screen with scan lines. While one is on, the internal resolution and AMD FSR upscaling are set aside; they come back when you pick another filter.
- **High-quality sound**: Settings › Emulation › *High-quality sound* (off by default) renders the Saturn's sound again without the hardware's shortcuts: band-limited interpolation instead of the chip's linear one, which aliases on pitched-up samples, and the mix and effects in floating point. The emulated sound chip is unchanged, so games behave exactly the same. It costs extra CPU.

## From YabaSanshiro 1.20.46 to 1.20.55

- **VDP1 texture rows** follow the hardware's own stepping in GPU tessellation, the Vulkan renderer and the Compute Rasterizer, so textured sprites and polygons sample the right rows.
- **Rotation screens (RBG0/RBG1)** only read the VRAM banks the game gives them, as the Saturn does.
- Security fixes for upstream's online features (cloud saves, rankings), which the Switch build doesn't use.

## Under the hood

- Merged YabaSanshiro 1.20.55, keeping the Switch port's GPU clean-up on exit, its shader memory fixes and its word-aligned sound RAM writes.
- `sdmc:/tico/run/session.log` records whether YabaSanshiro could open tico's session. Please attach it to bug reports.
- The CRT shaders are built in: Hyllian (MIT), Lottes (public domain) and NewPixie (MIT), credited in the source.

## Credits

- YabaSanshiro by @devmiyax, including the CRT filters and the high-quality sound renderer.
- Core fixes from Thorhax's Switch port.
- Vulkan through NVK, from mesa-switch and @NaGaa95's work on it.

## Installing

Update from the tico Store, or extract `tico-yabasanshiro-module.zip` into `sdmc:/tico/modules/` (you'll get `sdmc:/tico/modules/yabasanshiro/`). Your settings, saves and states stay as they are.

Requires tico 0.8.0 or later.

# The Minish Cap — Nintendo Switch (native homebrew) · USA + PT‑BR

Native **Nintendo Switch** homebrew builds of the Minish Cap PC‑decompilation port — a **native recompilation** (it runs on the Switch's own CPU with a software PPU/APU; **it is not an emulator**). Two builds:

- 🇺🇸 **USA** — original English.
- 🇧🇷 **BR (PT‑BR)** — Brazilian Portuguese translation (*romsportugues* "T1.0‑Final") + Portuguese overlay UI by default.

> ⚠️ **No game data is included.** The `.nro` ships only the engine + a pre‑baked asset cache. You must provide your **own legally‑dumped GBA ROM** — it supplies the actual game data.

## ✨ What's included in these builds
- 🏆 **RetroAchievements** — full `rcheevos` / `rc_client` integration over HTTPS, with a styled in‑game unlock overlay (issue #12).
- ⚡ **GPU renderer (OpenGL ES 2)** — runs **60 fps without overclocking**.
- 🎮 **Controls** — A/B mapped to Nintendo's physical face‑button layout, analog‑stick support.
- 🔤 **On‑screen menu** — scaled overlay/settings (Minus button), FPS‑counter options, multilingual (EN / PT / ES).
- 📂 **Loads any `*.gba` by content**, not by filename — so a translation hack works as‑is.
- 🛠️ Opt‑in frame profiler; clean RELEASE build (no per‑frame SD logging).

---

## ✅ Requirements
- A Nintendo Switch with custom firmware (**Atmosphère**) and the **Homebrew Menu** (hbmenu).
- The **matching GBA ROM** for the build you want (table below).

## 💾 Required ROM per build (check the SHA‑1!)

| Build | ROM you need | SHA‑1 of the ROM |
|---|---|---|
| **USA** | The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap (USA) | `b4bd50e4131b027c334547b4524e2dbbd4227130` |
| **BR / PT‑BR** | Minish Cap PT‑BR translation — *romsportugues T1.0‑Final* | `6838e0405c1be5d867d84e019d1f131a366b07ad` |

Verify yours before copying: `sha1sum your_rom.gba`. It must match **exactly** or the game won't load correctly.

## 📥 Installation — where & how
1. On your SD card, create the folder **`/switch/tmc/`**.
2. Copy **your ROM** into it, renamed to exactly **`baserom.gba`** → so you end up with **`/switch/tmc/baserom.gba`**.
   - USA build → put the **USA** ROM here. · BR build → put the **PT‑BR hack** ROM here.
3. Copy the downloaded **`.nro`** to **`/switch/`** (any subfolder works; hbmenu scans recursively).
4. On the Switch, open the **Homebrew Menu** and launch the `.nro`.
5. First launch builds the asset cache (a few seconds) and the game starts.

> ⚠️ **One ROM at a time.** Both builds read `/switch/tmc/baserom.gba`. To switch between USA and BR, replace `baserom.gba` with the matching ROM **and delete the folder `/switch/tmc/assets/`** so the cache rebuilds for the new ROM.

## ℹ️ Notes
- The BR build is the proven USA engine running the translation's assets — there is no separate "EU" build here (the genuine European BZMP cart isn't supported yet).
- `.nro` download hashes (SHA‑256), to verify your download:
  - `TMC-Switch-USA-v0.2.5.nro` → `1f6701758fed77036899403a7dbe8648f79f56356bb2178988982d94b6288769`
  - `TMC-Switch-BR-PTBR-v0.2.5.nro` → `2443cf56b11e83b8b48fcac270203b33c91226a2aabfcacb11759ccb4456f7ec`

---

packages.changelog:
TMNT 1.1.0: SDL 3, the Raspberry Pi, and iPhone and iPad. As before, nothing of the game comes in these packages:
keep your own `tmnt.zip` (MAME's ROM set, World 4 Players) beside the game, and it takes its assets out of it the
first time it starts.

**New**

- **Raspberry Pi**: `tmnt-raspberrypi-arm64.tar.gz`, TMNT and TMNT Arcade for a Raspberry Pi 3 or later (3, Zero 2 W,
  4, 400, 5, 500) with the 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS, Debian 12 "Bookworm" or later; the 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS does not
  run it. Start `./TMNT` or `"./TMNT Arcade"` from the folder, in the desktop or with none (Raspberry Pi OS Lite,
  where the game takes the whole screen). The game plays the same frame by frame under emulation, the first run
  from `tmnt.zip` included. Not yet tried on a Raspberry Pi: the picture, the sound, the controllers and the speed on
  a Pi 3 are to be seen there.
- **iPhone and iPad**: `tmnt-ios.zip`, the two games as .ipa files for iOS and iPadOS 13 or later. They are not on
  the App Store, and never will be: you install them yourself (AltStore, SideStore or Sideloadly, which sign them
  with your own Apple ID; the package's README says how) and put `tmnt.zip` in the game's folder in the Files app.
  The touch screen's controls as on Android, or a game controller. Built and started in the iOS Simulator by the
  release's build; not yet tried on an iPhone or iPad, nor played there. If a game does not start, send `tmnt.log`
  from its folder in an issue. MULTIPLAYER is not expected to find the rooms there yet.

**Changed**

- **SDL 3** (the window, the sound and the controls: SDL 3.4.20 where SDL 2 was) on Windows, Linux, macOS and
  Android. The game is the same frame by frame; what a player may notice:
  - On Windows the window is at the screen's own pixels. On a desktop scaled to 125% or 150% it is smaller and sharp
    where it was stretched and soft; OPTIONS > VIDEO > WINDOW makes it larger.
  - On a computer a Nintendo controller's buttons go by their place, as an Xbox controller's: the button at the
    bottom attacks, the one at the right jumps.
  Not yet played through by hand on SDL 3: if the sound, the full screen, VSYNC, the pause or a controller is not as
  it was, tell in an issue, with `tmnt.log`.
- **The Nintendo Switch on SDL 3**: devkitPro has no SDL 3 of its own yet, so the games carry its branch of it (SDL
  3.4.0, not released). Not yet tried on a Switch: the picture docked and handheld, the sound and the controllers
  are the first things to tell. If it does not start on yours, 1.0.7 is the one that does.
- **Anbernic**: its games keep the firmware's SDL 2 under the same source. Not yet tried on a handheld.
- **Linux**: the package asks the system for nothing new; SDL finds PipeWire by itself now, beside PulseAudio and
  ALSA.

**Fixed**

- **Donatello lands with his bo** (issue 23): falling into areas 2, 3 and 7, his landing pose had a piece of
  Raphael's sai where the bo's lower end goes (one bit of the arcade board's own data; MAME shows it too). TMNT puts
  it right; TMNT Arcade keeps the board's data.

Each package's `README.txt` says what it needs. What a tool makes is yours alone: never share it.

The game is free, and stays free. To support the decompilations and the ports, and have a say in what comes
next: [patreon.com/ChevimanPorts](https://www.patreon.com/ChevimanPorts). Entirely optional.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is a trademark of its owner, and the arcade game is Konami's; this project is not
affiliated with or endorsed by either, nor by Nintendo, Google, Apple, Anbernic or Raspberry Pi.

## torchlight-nx 1.0.6

A smaller performance update, mostly felt in the dungeons, with the CPU and the memory still at their **stock clocks**.
**To update:** replace `sdmc:/switch/torchlight/torchlight.nro` with the one from the zip. Your game files, saves and
settings stay where they are.

### Faster

- **Single-precision fused multiply-adds are rounded once, like on the Xbox 360**, and without any extra check where
  the build can prove their inputs are already single precision.
- **Vector element stores read straight from the register** instead of going through memory.
- **The equipment texture blend runs as native code**, checked against the recompiled loop.
- **Missing game files are remembered**, so the game no longer asks the SD card again for files it already knows are
  not there.
- **Fewer allocations every frame** for particle billboards, and the floating-point mode is no longer rewritten when it
  does not change.
- **A new optimization profile** built from a play session on this code.

The game looks the same as before.

### Saves

Saving no longer copies the whole save file: the file is now renamed in place, as on the Xbox 360. Existing saves load
as before.

### Thanks

- [renut_nx_ultimate_base](https://github.com/ChanseyIsTheBest/renut_nx_ultimate_base) by ChanseyIsTheBest (with fixes
  from blur-nx, sasrt-nx and tw2de_nx): the fused multiply-add rounding, the vector element stores, the floating-point
  mode and the deferred system call fixes.
- [torchlight-recomp](https://github.com/YaPeL/torchlight-recomp) by YaPeL: the missing file cache and the equipment
  texture blend.

### Installation

Unchanged: see the README. You need your own copy of the Xbox Live Arcade game (its package from your Xbox 360).

**RUS**

1. **Автоматическая очистка старых версий обновлений (патчей)**:
   - При установке новой версии обновления игры теперь автоматически удаляются устаревшие версии патча и их NCA-файлы как с SD-карты, так и из системной памяти (NAND).
   - **Защита общих данных**: общие NCA-архивы, используемые новым обновлением совместно со старым, сохраняются и не удаляются.
   - **Очистка системных записей**: добавлен вызов `nsDeleteRedundantApplicationEntity()` для удаления избыточных/осиротевших записей приложений в системе и освобождения места.
2. **Улучшение выбора хранилища при загрузке**:
   - В окне выбора файлов перед загрузкой (`FileSelectView`) режим «Скачать без установки» исключён из стандартного цикла смены накопителей (`Авто` → `SD` → `NAND`), что предотвращает его случайную активацию при переключении места установки.

---

**ENG**

1. **Automatic Cleanup of Obsolete Game Updates (Patches)**:
   - When installing a new patch version, older patch versions and their obsolete NCA files are now automatically detected and deleted from both the SD card and internal storage (NAND).
   - **Shared NCA Protection**: content archives shared between update versions are safely preserved.
   - **Redundant Entity Cleanup**: added `nsDeleteRedundantApplicationEntity()` call to remove orphaned application entities from the system and reclaim free space.
2. **Storage Selector Improvement**:
   - In the file selection view (`FileSelectView`), the "Download without installing" mode is now excluded from the storage toggle cycle (`Auto` → `SD` → `NAND`), preventing accidental switching to no-install mode when cycling through target storages.

Fixes and better logs for bug reports. Update from KaiKart with **Check for updates**, or download `KaiKart-0.4.1.nro` below. Still Retro Rewind 6.13.5.

### Settings menu
- In the controller settings, hold A on a button row to clear that button ("None"). Tapping A still changes it.
- Resolution, Show FPS and the clocks stop at their lowest and highest settings instead of wrapping round, so a stray push can't jump from 3x to 1x. Pressing A on a clock row still steps through all its speeds.
- Every setting change is written to the log.

### Logs
- The previous run's logs are kept as `kaikart.prev.log` and `kaihen.prev.log`, so a problem isn't lost when you start again.
- The game log starts with the game's name and version.
- The game log notes the battery level, the battery state (including when it's too low for boosted clocks) and any CPU slowdown.

When reporting a bug, please attach the logs from `wiicompiled/UserData/Logs/` on the card. The bug report form says which ones.

Tested with kaiHEN 20261117.1.

### ☁️ SoundCloud (по желанию, через официальное API)
- Поиск треков и плейлистов, ссылки `soundcloud.com/…`, в том числе закрытые `/s-…`
- Вход в аккаунт: волна из похожих на ваши лайки, «Мне нравится», лента подписок, плейлисты
- Лайки ([ZR]) и скачивание ([ZL]): оригинал, если автор разрешил, иначе AAC 160 или mp3
- Музыка SoundCloud продолжается в фоне (mp3 128 kbps), волна дописывается сама
- Быстрый старт треков: поток начинает играть сразу, следующий трек готовится заранее
- Прокси `socks5h://` / `http://` в `switch/yamu-nx/proxy.txt` — если SoundCloud не открывается из вашей сети

Для SoundCloud нужны свои ключи — как их получить, написано в README.

### 🧭 Главный экран
- Боковое меню: «Яндекс», «SoundCloud» и общие «Настройки»; разделы переключаются кнопками [L] / [R]

### 🛠 Исправления
- Фоновый модуль ждёт сеть после включения консоли и сам повторяет вход — «Моя волна» из оверлея работает сразу после загрузки
- Убрано пустое место на экране поиска между «Лучшим результатом» и «Треками»
- Значки на низких плитках главной больше не наезжают на названия

### 📦 Установка
Скопируйте папки `switch` и `atmosphere` из архива в корень SD-карты с заменой и **перезагрузите консоль**, чтобы запустился новый фоновый модуль.

The first release of YTB Player: a YouTube client for Nintendo Switch homebrew, built on [Switch-NewPipe](https://github.com/mirusu400/switch-newpipe), with the screens redone after YouTube's tablet app.

### What's in it
- Home with category chips (L and R switch them), Shorts with their own player, channel pages with tabs, a watch page with comments and replies
- Subscriptions with filters, a two-pane library with your account's lists, notifications
- Player: a quality, speed and loop menu, chapters, subtitles, SponsorBlock, loudness levelling, resume where you left off, autoplay
- Sign in over Wi-Fi: the Switch shows an address, and the page there walks you through exporting your YouTube cookies
- English, Turkish and Korean; buttons and touch everywhere

### Install
Copy `ytb-player.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/ytb-player/ytb-player.nro` and start it from the Homebrew Menu. Open the Homebrew Menu through a game (hold R while starting one) so that the player gets the full memory.

Coming from Switch-NewPipe? Its settings, history and login are copied over on the first start.

`SHA256SUMS.txt` holds the file's checksum.

packages.changelog:
# Zelda Save Editor 0.1.5-alpha.5

Public prerelease by StockiestThree9. This update retains BOTW support and adds the TOTK development work completed since 0.1.4-beta.1.

## Changes since the store beta

- Experimental Tears of the Kingdom save discovery and editing, with player values, stamina wheels, battery cells, abilities and pouch capacity.
- Grouped item selection: choose an armor family, then its stars and supported style. Hylian Hood up/down is independent of rank. Weapons offer verified Decayed/Pristine and appearance choices. Search and category filters shorten the lists.
- Inventory add/replace/remove/equip, fusion choices, durability repair, armor upgrades, pristine conversion, meal effects and bulk stack tools.
- Registered horses, world/completion flags, compendium states, direct quest stages, map stamps and daily amiibo reset.
- Autobuild slot/favorite management and import/export using this editor's checksummed `.zsbp` format.
- BOTW inventory validation improvements, stale-selection protection after undo/redo, faster change tracking and clearer menu flows.

Game names, item relationships and other resource tables are read from the user's installed game and cached privately. No Nintendo resource cache, save, font or audio sample is distributed.

## Install or update

Extract `Zelda-Save-Editor-v0.1.5-alpha.5.zip` at the SD root, preserving existing files. The executable remains `/switch/Zelda_Save_Editor.nro`; documentation and notices are under `/switch/zelda-save-editor/`. Existing saves, backups, cache, settings and blueprints are not included or replaced by the package. A standalone NRO and a source archive including libpulsar are also provided.

Launch Sphaira in full application mode by holding R while opening the relevant game, then launch Zelda Save Editor. Close the actual game before editing its save. Settings → Game resources can retry loading the installed resources.

## Testing and current limits

Rechecked on 19 October 2026: native Switch build; 495 synthetic/core checks; 580 BOTW real-fixture checks; 7,090 TOTK checks with a real fixture and installed 1.4.3 resources; storage/backup/conflict checks; 230 BOTW normal-profile-swap checks; and both host UI walkthroughs.

This is still an **alpha for TOTK**. Host checks do not establish that every edited save is valid in-game. Gameplay acceptance of the expanded edits and resource loading on a fresh console installation remain unverified. Only one accepted TOTK save revision has a real test fixture. Keep an independent backup and begin with a small edit before testing broader changes.

World/quest edits change saved fields without reconciling all related story events or rewards. Graphical maps, sparse object completion such as individual bosses/Addison signs, full horse creation/customization and community Autobuild formats are not implemented. BOTW profile swapping excludes Master Mode; gameplay after swaps still needs wider device testing.

See [TOTK feature details and limits](https://github.com/amarkham23/Zelda-Save-Editor/blob/v0.1.5-alpha.5/docs/TOTK-ALPHA.md), [full changes](https://github.com/amarkham23/Zelda-Save-Editor/blob/v0.1.5-alpha.5/docs/CHANGES.md), and [BOTW profile-swap behavior](https://github.com/amarkham23/Zelda-Save-Editor/blob/v0.1.5-alpha.5/docs/PROFILE-SWAPS.md).

# ZERODROID v1.0.1 — Official Launch Release / Versión Oficial de Lanzamiento

## [ES] Español

### 🎮 ZERODROID v1.0.1: Cliente No Oficial de Boosteroid para Nintendo Switch

`ZERODROID_v1.0.1.nro` es la versión oficial de lanzamiento de ZERODROID, diseñada desde cero para ofrecer la experiencia completa de Boosteroid en Nintendo Switch con interfaz gráfica nativa a 60 FPS, aceleración de video H.264 por hardware NVDEC, decodificación de audio Opus y controles personalizados.

---

### ✨ Novedades Principales de la v1.0.1

1. **Carátulas y Posteres en Alta Definición:**
   * Reemplazo de marcos anchos con barras laterales por ranuras verticales tipo póster (`v101-poster` / `v101-banner`), con recorte centrado automático y marco azul marino sin deformación.
2. **Biblioteca Paginada y Navegación Intuitiva:**
   * Navegación completa por pestañas: **Mis juegos**, **Catálogo**, **Favoritos** y **Recientes**.
   * Búsqueda nativa, filtrado por estados de licencia (Gratuito, Requiere licencia, Instalar y Jugar) y favoritos persistentes.
   * Navegación fluida mediante botones de control (**ZL/ZR** para secciones, **L/R** para páginas) y pantalla táctil nativa.
3. **Centro de Control e Interfaz de Transmisión:**
   * Acceso rápido mediante el botón **X lila** táctil superior derecho.
   * Acciones rápidas: **Xbox Guide**, **Steam Menu** (`Shift + Tab`), **ALT+TAB**, **Keyboard Info**, **Mouse Virtual / Trackpad**, **Reconexión UDP**, **Ajustes Gráficos** y **Volver al Juego**.
   * Cursor virtual lila de GPU deko3d con auto-ocultado tras 3 segundos de inactividad.
4. **Perfiles de Imagen y Resoluciones:**
   * Soporte para modos **Auto** (720p portátil / 1080p dock), **720p**, **1080p** y **1440p experimental**.
   * Perfiles de color: *Natural*, *Nítido (Sharp)*, *Vivo*, *Cine*, *Suave* y *Personalizado*.

---

### 💻 Instalación en Nintendo Switch

1. Descarga los archivos `ZERODROID_v1.0.1.nro` y `ZERODROID_v1.0.1.sha256`.
2. Copia el binario a tu tarjeta SD en `sdmc:/switch/ZERODROID/ZERODROID.nro`.
3. Inicia Homebrew Menu en modo **Title Takeover**: mantén presionado **R** mientras inicias cualquier juego instalado en tu consola.
   *(Nota: No uses el modo Álbum/Applet Mode, ya que no otorga la memoria RAM necesaria para la decodificación de video y red WebRTC)*.

---

## [EN] English

### 🎮 ZERODROID v1.0.1: Unofficial Boosteroid Client for Nintendo Switch

`ZERODROID_v1.0.1.nro` is the first complete official launch release of ZERODROID, tailored specifically for Nintendo Switch homebrew with native 60 FPS rendering, NVDEC hardware H.264 video decoding, Opus audio playback, and customizable streaming profiles.

---

### ✨ Key Features & Improvements in v1.0.1

1. **High-Definition Poster Artwork:**
   * Replaced letterboxed card artwork with vertical poster slots (`v101-poster` / `v101-banner`), featuring centered source crop and slim navy borders. Cover art is never stretched or distorted.
2. **Complete Paginated Library & Touch Navigation:**
   * Full tabbed browsing: **My Games**, **Catalog**, **Favorites**, and **Recent**.
   * Native search bar, license badges (*Free*, *License Required*, *Install & Play*), and persistent favorites.
   * Dual controller (**ZL/ZR** for section switching, **L/R** for pagination) and release-on-tap Switch touch navigation.
3. **In-Stream Control Center (Top-Right Purple X):**
   * Accessible in-game via the top-right purple X touch overlay.
   * Actions: **Xbox Guide**, **Steam Menu** (`Shift + Tab`), **ALT+TAB**, **Keyboard Info**, **Virtual Mouse / Trackpad**, **UDP Reconnection**, **Graphic Presets**, and **Return to Game**.
   * Hardware-rendered purple virtual cursor via deko3d GPU quad with 3-second auto-hide.
4. **Resolution Modes & Image Profiles:**
   * Resolution selector: **Auto** (720p handheld / 1080p docked), **720p**, **1080p**, and **1440p experimental**.
   * Preset color profiles: *Natural*, *Sharp*, *Vivid*, *Cinema*, *Soft*, and *Custom*.
